title.en: Volume 29: Book of Wei 29 - Biographies of fangshis and artisans
title.raw: 卷二十九 魏書二十九 方技傳 Volume 29: Book of Wei 29 - Biographies of fangshis and artisans

sentences.zh: 華佗杜夔朱建平周宣管輅

translations.literal: Hua Tuo, Du Kui, Zhu Jianping, Zhou Xuan, Guan Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo, Du Kui, Zhu Jianping, Zhou Xuan, and Guan Lu.

sentences.zh: 華佗字元化，沛國譙人也，一名旉。

translations.literal: Hua Tuo, courtesy name Yuanhua, man of Qiao in the Pei state, also had one name Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo, whose courtesy name was Yuanhua, came from Qiao in the kingdom of Pei; he was also known as Fu.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：古「敷」字與「專」相似，寫書者多不能別。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi submits: In antiquity the character fu 敷 resembled zhuan 專, and those who copied texts mostly could not tell them apart.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: In older scripts the character for "spread" looked much like the one for "sole," and copyists often confused the two.

sentences.zh: 尋佗字元化，其名宜為旉也。〉

translations.literal: Considering Tuo's courtesy name Yuanhua, his name ought to have been Fu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Given his courtesy name Yuanhua, his true given name was almost certainly Fu.〉

sentences.zh: 遊學徐土，兼通數經。

translations.literal: Traveled for study in the lands of Xu, and concurrently mastered several classics.
translations.idiomatic: He studied abroad in the Xu region and gained a thorough command of more than one classic.

sentences.zh: 沛相陳珪舉孝廉，太尉黃琬辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Pei, Chen Gui, nominated him for Filial and Incorrupt; the Grand Commandant Huang Wan summoned him; in neither case did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui, the chancellor of Pei, recommended him as filial and incorrupt, and Grand Commandant Huang Wan offered him a post; he declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 曉養性之術，時人以為年且百歲而貌有壯容。

translations.literal: Understood the arts of nurturing nature; people of the time thought him nearly a hundred years in age yet his appearance had robust countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the arts of nurturing vitality; contemporaries believed he was close to a hundred years old, yet he still looked vigorous.

sentences.zh: 又精方藥，其療疾，合湯不過數種，心解分劑，不復稱量，煮熟便飲，語其節度，捨去輒愈。

translations.literal: Also skilled in formulas and drugs; in treating illness, combining decoctions used no more than several kinds; in mind understood portions and doses, did not again weigh measure; when cooked drank at once; told them the regimen; when they left according to it they were cured.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a master of prescriptions and materia medica. When he treated the sick, his decoctions used only a handful of ingredients; he knew the proportions by heart and never bothered to weigh them. Once the brew was ready the patient drank it at once, followed Hua Tuo's instructions on timing and regimen, and was cured as soon as he left.

sentences.zh: 若當灸，不過一兩處，每處不過七八壯，病亦應除。

translations.literal: If moxibustion was appropriate, it was never more than one or two places; each place never more than seven or eight cones; the illness also responded by being removed.
translations.idiomatic: When moxibustion was called for, he never used more than one or two points, and at each point no more than seven or eight cones; the ailment would clear all the same.

sentences.zh: 若當針，亦不過一兩處，下針言「當引某許，若至，語人」。

translations.literal: If needling was appropriate, likewise never more than one or two places; inserting the needle he said, "It ought to extend to such-and-such a point; if it reaches there, tell the person."
translations.idiomatic: When acupuncture was needed, again he limited himself to one or two insertions. As he set the needle he would say, "You should feel it reach about here; when it does, let me know."

sentences.zh: 病者言「巳到」，應便拔針，病亦行差。

translations.literal: The sick person said, "It has arrived"; he thereupon pulled out the needle; the illness also proceeded to improve.
translations.idiomatic: When the patient said, "It's there," he would withdraw the needle immediately, and the symptoms would begin to lift.

sentences.zh: 若病結積在內，針藥所不能及，當須刳割者，便飲其麻沸散，須臾便如醉死無所知，因破取。

translations.literal: If the illness knotted and accumulated inside, where needle and drugs could not reach, when it was necessary to cut open and excise, then made them drink his mafeisan powder; in a moment they were as if drunk dead, knowing nothing; thereupon broke open and took it out.
translations.idiomatic: When a morbid mass lay deep inside, beyond the reach of needles or drugs, and surgery was required, he had the patient drink his mafeisan anesthetic. In moments they sank into a deathlike stupor, insensible to pain, and he could open the body and remove the lesion.

sentences.zh: 病若在腸中，便斷腸湔洗，縫腹膏摩，四五日差，不痛，人亦不自寤，一月之間，即平復矣。

translations.literal: If the illness was in the intestines, then severed the intestines, rinsed and washed, sewed the belly, rubbed with ointment; in four or five days improved, no pain; the person also did not themselves awake; within one month, then was restored.
translations.idiomatic: If the disease lay in the bowels, he would resect the affected segment, cleanse it, sew the abdomen closed, and apply a salve. Within four or five days the wound healed without pain; the patient scarcely knew what had happened, and in about a month they were fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 故甘陵相夫人有娠六月，腹痛不安，佗視脈，曰：「胎巳死矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the wife of the former Chancellor of Ganling, pregnant six months, had belly pain and was uneasy; Tuo inspected the pulse, said: "The fetus is already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of a former chancellor of Ganling was six months pregnant and suffered restless abdominal pain. Hua Tuo examined her pulse and said, "The child in the womb is already dead.

sentences.zh: 」使人手摸知所在，在左則男，在右則女。

translations.literal: " Had a person hand-feel to know the location; if on the left then male, if on the right then female.
translations.idiomatic: " He had someone palpate her belly to learn where it lay: on the left meant a boy, on the right a girl.

sentences.zh: 人云「在左」，於是為湯下之，果下男形，即愈。

translations.literal: People said "on the left"; thereupon made a decoction to purge it down; indeed discharged male form; then was cured.
translations.idiomatic: They reported it was on the left, so he prepared a purgative decoction. She passed the form of a male fetus and was cured.

sentences.zh: 縣吏尹世苦四支煩，口中乾，不欲聞人聲，小便不利。

translations.literal: County clerk Yin Shi suffered vexation in the four limbs, mouth inside dry, did not wish to hear human voices, urination not smooth.
translations.idiomatic: The county clerk Yin Shi was tormented by aching limbs, a parched mouth, an aversion to any human voice, and difficulty passing urine.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「試作熱食，得汗則愈；

translations.literal: Tuo said: "Try making hot food; if obtain sweat then will be cured;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo said, "Try a hot meal; if you break a sweat you will recover.

sentences.zh: 不汗，後三日死。

translations.literal: If no sweat, after three days will die.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not sweat, you will die in three days."

sentences.zh: 」即作熱食而不汗出，佗曰：「藏氣已絕於內，當啼泣而絕。

translations.literal: " Immediately made hot food but sweat did not emerge; Tuo said: "The visceral qi has already been severed inside; ought to weep and cry and expire.
translations.idiomatic: " They prepared a hot meal, yet no sweat came. Hua Tuo said, "The visceral breath is already exhausted within; you will perish amid weeping and lamentation.

sentences.zh: 」果如佗言。

translations.literal: " Indeed as Tuo said.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 府吏兒尋、李延共止，俱頭痛身熱，所苦正同。

translations.literal: Prefecture clerks Ni Xun and Li Yan lodged together; both had headache and body fever; what they suffered was exactly the same.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural clerks Ni Xun and Li Yan were staying under the same roof, both complaining of headache and fever with identical symptoms.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「尋當下之，延當發汗。

translations.literal: Tuo said: "Xun ought to be purged downward; Yan ought to be made to sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo said, "Xun needs a purgative; Yan needs a diaphoretic.

sentences.zh: 」或難其異，佗曰：「尋外實，延內實，故治之宜殊。

translations.literal: " Someone questioned their difference; Tuo said: "Xun is externally replete; Yan is internally replete; therefore treating them ought to differ.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone challenged the discrepancy. Hua Tuo replied, "Xun presents an excess on the exterior, Yan an excess in the interior, so the treatment must differ.

sentences.zh: 」即各與藥，明旦並起。

translations.literal: " Immediately gave each medicine; next dawn both rose.
translations.idiomatic: " He prescribed to each accordingly, and by the next morning both were on their feet again.

sentences.zh: 鹽瀆嚴昕與數人共候佗，適至，佗謂昕曰：「君身中佳否？

translations.literal: Yan Xin of Yandu together with several people jointly waited for Tuo; just as arrived, Tuo said to Xin: "In your body is it well or not?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xin of Yandu and several others were waiting on Hua Tuo when he arrived. Hua Tuo asked him, "How are you feeling in yourself?

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「自如常。

translations.literal: " Xin said: "As usual.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin answered, "Quite my usual self.

sentences.zh: 」佗曰：「君有急病見於面，莫多飲酒。

translations.literal: " Tuo said: "You have acute illness showing on the face; do not drink much wine.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua Tuo said, "A grave illness is already written on your face; do not drink heavily.

sentences.zh: 」坐畢歸，行數里，昕卒頭眩墮車，人扶將還，載歸家，中宿死。

translations.literal: " When sitting finished returned, traveled several li, Xin suddenly dizzy fell from cart; people supported and brought back, carried returned home; in the middle of the night died.
translations.idiomatic: " When the visit ended Yan Xin set out for home. A few miles along the road he was suddenly overcome by vertigo and tumbled from his carriage. Passersby helped him into a cart and took him home, and he died before midnight.

sentences.zh: 故督郵頓子獻得病已差，詣佗視脈，曰：「尚虛，未得復，勿為勞事，御內即死。

translations.literal: Former Chief Clerk Dun Zixian's illness had already improved; went to Tuo to inspect pulse; said: "Still depleted, not yet able to recover; do not engage in laboring matters; if engage in bedroom matters then will die.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief clerk Dun Zixian had apparently recovered from an illness and came to Hua Tuo for a pulse reading. Hua Tuo said, "You are still depleted and not ready to resume normal life. Avoid exertion; if you take a woman to bed you will die.

sentences.zh: 臨死，當吐舌數寸。

translations.literal: At the time of death, ought to spit out tongue several cun.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of death your tongue will protrude several inches."

sentences.zh: 」其妻聞其病除，從百餘里來省之，止宿交接，中間三日發病，一如佗言。

translations.literal: " His wife heard his illness removed, came from more than a hundred li to visit him, stopped overnight and coupled; in the middle after three days fell ill; exactly as Tuo said.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife, hearing that he was cured, traveled more than a hundred li to see him. They spent the night together and lay together. Three days later he fell ill, and everything unfolded exactly as Hua Tuo had predicted.

sentences.zh: 督郵徐毅得病，佗往省之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Xu Yi fell ill; Tuo went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk Xu Yi fell ill, and Hua Tuo went to examine him.

sentences.zh: 毅謂佗曰：「昨使醫曹吏劉租針胃管訖，便苦欬嗽，欲臥不安。

translations.literal: Yi said to Tuo: "Yesterday had medical office clerk Liu Zu needle the stomach duct finished, then suffered bitter cough, wished to lie but was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi told him, "Yesterday I had Liu Zu, a clerk in the medical office, needle the region of my stomach conduit. Since then I have had a racking cough and cannot rest when I try to lie down.

sentences.zh: 」佗曰：「刺不得胃管，誤中肝也，食當日減，五日不救。

translations.literal: " Tuo said: "The needling did not hit the stomach duct; mistakenly struck the liver; eating ought daily to decrease; in five days cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua Tuo said, "The needle missed the stomach conduit and pierced the liver by mistake. Your appetite will fall away day by day, and in five days nothing can save you.

sentences.zh: 」遂如佗言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon was as Tuo said.
translations.idiomatic: " Events followed his words to the letter.

sentences.zh: 東陽陳叔山小男二歲得疾，下利常先啼，日以羸困。

translations.literal: Chen Shuxiao of Dongyang's small boy two years obtained illness, diarrhea always first cried, day by day became emaciated and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The two-year-old son of Chen Shuxiao of Dongyang fell ill with dysentery and always wept before each movement of the bowels; day by day the child grew wasted and weak.

sentences.zh: 問佗，佗曰：「其母懷軀，陽氣內養，乳中虛冷，兒得母寒，故令不時愈。

translations.literal: Asked Tuo; Tuo said: "His mother when pregnant, yang qi internally nurtured, in the milk was depleted cold; the child obtained the mother's cold; therefore caused not timely cure.
translations.idiomatic: They consulted Hua Tuo, who said, "While carrying this child the mother drew on her yang vitality to nourish the fetus, so her milk turned deficient and cold. The infant has inherited that chill from her, which is why the ailment will not clear.

sentences.zh: 」佗與四物女宛丸，十日即除。

translations.literal: " Tuo gave four-substances nüwan pills; in ten days then removed.
translations.idiomatic: " He prescribed a four-ingredient "lady's garden" pill, and in ten days the trouble was gone.

sentences.zh: 彭城夫人夜之廁，蠆螫其手，呻呼無賴。

translations.literal: The Lady of Pengcheng at night went to the privy; a scorpion stung her hand; moaned and cried without recourse.
translations.idiomatic: The lady of Pengcheng went to the privy by night, where a scorpion stung her hand. She cried out in pain with no relief.

sentences.zh: 佗令溫湯近熱，漬手其中，卒可得寐，但旁人數為易湯，湯令暖之，其旦即愈。

translations.literal: Tuo ordered warm water near hot, soak hand inside it, finally could obtain sleep; only those beside repeatedly for them changed water, water ordered warmed; by dawn then was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo had her immerse the hand in water as hot as she could bear. She could then fall asleep, provided attendants kept changing the water so it stayed warm. By morning she was well.

sentences.zh: 軍吏梅平得病，除名還家，家居廣陵，未至二百里，止親人舍。

translations.literal: Army clerk Mei Ping fell ill, name removed returned home, home resided in Guangling, not yet reached two hundred li, stopped at a relative's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: The army clerk Mei Ping fell ill, was struck from the rolls, and set out for his home in Guangling. He had not yet covered two hundred li when he stopped at a kinsman's house.

sentences.zh: 有頃，佗偶至主人許，主人令佗視平，佗謂平曰：「君早見我，可不至此。

translations.literal: After a while, Tuo by chance arrived at the host's place; host ordered Tuo to inspect Ping; Tuo said to Ping: "If you had early seen me, could not have reached here.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Hua Tuo happened to call on the host, who asked him to look at Mei Ping. Hua Tuo told Ping, "Had you come to me sooner, you would never have reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 今疾已結，促去可得與家相見，五日卒。

translations.literal: Now the illness has already knotted; hasten to depart can obtain to meet family; in five days will die.
translations.idiomatic: The disease has now set firm. Hurry home and you may still see your family; in five days you will be dead.

sentences.zh: 」應時歸，如佗所刻。

translations.literal: " Responded to the time returned, as Tuo had carved.
translations.idiomatic: " He left at once and died on the very day Hua Tuo had named.

sentences.zh: 佗行道，見一人病咽塞，嗜食而不得下，家人車載欲往就醫。

translations.literal: Tuo traveled on the road, saw one person ill with throat blockage, craved food but could not get it down; family members cart-carried wished to go seek a doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo was walking along the road when he saw a man whose throat was blocked: he hungered for food yet could not swallow. His family had loaded him into a cart to find a physician.

sentences.zh: 佗聞其呻吟，駐車往視，語之曰：「向來道邊有賣餅家蒜齏大酢，從取三升飲之，病自當去。

translations.literal: Tuo heard his moaning, stopped cart went to look, told him saying: "Just now on the road side there is a cake-seller's garlic mash in strong vinegar; go take three sheng and drink it; the illness by itself ought to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo heard his groans, stopped the cart, and went to him. "There is a pie-seller back along the road," he said, "who keeps a jar of garlic mash in strong vinegar. Send someone for three sheng of that liquor and drink it down; the obstruction will clear.

sentences.zh: 」即如佗言，立吐蛇一枚，縣車邊，欲造佗。

translations.literal: " Immediately as Tuo said; immediately vomited one snake; hung at cart side; wished to go to Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: " They did as he said. The man at once vomited up a snake-like worm and hung it on the side of the cart, then wanted to visit Hua Tuo.

sentences.zh: 佗尚未還，小兒戲門前，逆見，自相謂曰：「似逢我公，車邊病是也。

translations.literal: Tuo had not yet returned; small children played before the gate, met coming, said to each other: "Seems to have met our lord; the sickness at cart side is this.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo was not yet back. Some boys were playing at his gate and saw the visitor coming. "That looks like our master's cure," they said to one another; "the thing hanging on the cart is it.

sentences.zh: 」疾者前入坐，見佗北壁縣此蛇輩約以十數。

translations.literal: " The sick person went forward entered sat, saw on Tuo's north wall hung these snakes approximately numbering ten.
translations.idiomatic: " The patient went in and took a seat. On the north wall of Hua Tuo's clinic hung a dozen such "snakes" like the one he had brought.

sentences.zh: 又有一郡守病，佗以為其人盛怒則差，乃多受其貨而不加治，無何棄去，留書罵之。

translations.literal: Also there was one prefect ill; Tuo thought that if this person greatly raged then would improve; then much received his goods but did not add treatment; before long abandoned and left, left a letter cursing him.
translations.idiomatic: Another prefect fell ill. Hua Tuo judged that a violent fit of rage would cure him, so he accepted a large fee, gave no real treatment, soon walked away, and left a letter full of abuse.

sentences.zh: 郡守果大怒，令人追捉殺佗。

translations.literal: The prefect indeed greatly angry, ordered people pursue and seize and kill Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect flew into a rage and sent men to run Hua Tuo down and kill him.

sentences.zh: 郡守子知之，屬使勿逐。

translations.literal: The prefect's son knew it, instructed the agents do not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: His son understood the stratagem and told the pursuers not to give chase.

sentences.zh: 守瞋恚既甚，吐黑血數升而愈。

translations.literal: The prefect's fury and rage already extreme, vomited several sheng of black blood and was cured.
translations.idiomatic: The official's wrath mounted until he vomited several sheng of black blood and recovered.

sentences.zh: 又有一士大夫不快，佗云：「君病深，當破腹取。

translations.literal: Also there was one scholar-official unwell; Tuo said: "Your illness is deep; ought to break open the belly and take it.
translations.idiomatic: Another gentleman felt unwell. Hua Tuo said, "The malady lies deep; the abdomen must be opened and the growth removed.

sentences.zh: 然君壽亦不過十年，病不能殺君，忍病十歲，壽俱當盡，不足故自刳裂。

translations.literal: Yet your lifespan also will not exceed ten years; the illness cannot kill you; endure illness ten years, lifespan together ought to be exhausted; not sufficient reason therefore to cut open yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your allotted span will not pass ten years in any case. The sickness will not kill you; if you bear it for ten years, your years and the disease will end together. There is no need to cut yourself open for that.

sentences.zh: 」士大夫不耐痛癢，必欲除之。

translations.literal: " The scholar-official could not endure the pain and itch, necessarily wished to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: " The gentleman could not abide the discomfort and insisted on having it cut out.

sentences.zh: 佗遂下手，所患尋差，十年竟死。

translations.literal: Tuo thereupon applied hands; what he suffered soon improved; in ten years in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo operated; the complaint soon cleared, but ten years later the man died as foretold.

sentences.zh: 廣陵太守陳登得病，胸中煩懣，面赤不食。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator of Guangling, Chen Deng, fell ill, chest inside vexed and full, face red, did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng, the grand administrator of Guangling, fell ill with oppression in the chest, a flushed face, and loss of appetite.

sentences.zh: 佗脈之曰：「府君胃中有蟲數升，欲成內疽，食腥物所為也。

translations.literal: Tuo pulsed him saying: "My lord's stomach inside has worms several sheng, about to form internal abscess, caused by eating rank-smelling things.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo felt his pulse and said, "Your honor, you have several sheng of parasites in the stomach, verging on an internal abscess, brought on by eating raw fish and the like.

sentences.zh: 」即作湯二升，先服一升，斯須盡服之。

translations.literal: " Immediately made decoction two sheng, first drank one sheng, in a moment finished drinking it all.
translations.idiomatic: " He prepared two sheng of a medicinal broth, had Chen drink one sheng first, then the remainder a moment later.

sentences.zh: 食頃，吐出三升許蟲，赤頭皆動，半身是生魚膾也，所苦便愈。

translations.literal: In the time of a meal, vomited about three sheng of worms, red heads all moving, half the bodies were raw fish slices; what he suffered then was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Within the space of a meal he brought up nearly three sheng of worms with wriggling red heads, half their bodies still recognizable as raw fish sashimi. The distress lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「此病後三期當發，遇良醫乃可濟救。

translations.literal: Tuo said: "This illness afterward at three periods ought to flare; encountering a good physician then can be aided and saved.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo warned him, "The condition will return three times on a fixed cycle; only a skilled physician can save you then.

sentences.zh: 」依期果發動，時佗不在，如言而死。

translations.literal: " According to the period indeed flared; at the time Tuo was not present; as said died.
translations.idiomatic: " It broke out on schedule each time, but Hua Tuo was no longer at hand, and Chen died as predicted.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而召佗，佗常在左右。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard and summoned Tuo; Tuo constantly was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor heard of him and summoned Hua Tuo, who thereafter attended him constantly.

sentences.zh: 太祖苦頭風，每發，心亂目眩，佗針鬲，隨手而差。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor suffered head wind; each time it flared, heart chaotic eyes dizzy; Tuo needled the diaphragm point; following the hand then improved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestor was tormented by splitting headaches; whenever an attack came his mind reeled and his sight swam. Hua Tuo needled the point below the diaphragm, and with a turn of the hand the fit subsided.

sentences.zh: 〈佗別傳曰：有人病兩腳躄不能行，轝詣佗，佗望見云：「己飽針灸服藥矣，不復須看脈。

translations.literal: 〈Tuo's separate biography says: There was a person ill with both feet lame unable to walk, carried in a litter went to Tuo; Tuo looked from afar and said: "Already full had acupuncture and moxibustion and took medicine; not again need inspect pulse.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The separate biography of Hua Tuo records: A man whose legs were paralyzed so that he could not walk was carried in a litter to Hua Tuo. From a distance Hua Tuo said, "You have already had your fill of needles, moxa, and drugs; there is no need to take the pulse again.

sentences.zh: 」便使解衣，點背數十處，相去或一寸，或五寸，縱邪不相當。

translations.literal: " Then ordered remove clothes, dotted back several tens of places, apart from each other sometimes one cun, sometimes five cun, vertical and slanting not corresponding.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the man strip and marked several dozen spots on his back, some an inch apart, some five, in no regular alignment.

sentences.zh: 言灸此各十壯，灸創愈即行。

translations.literal: Said moxibustion on these each ten cones; when moxa wounds healed then would walk.
translations.idiomatic: He directed that ten cones be applied at each mark and that the patient should walk as soon as the burns healed.

sentences.zh: 後灸處夾脊一寸，上下行端直均調，如引繩也。〉

translations.literal: Afterward the moxa places flanked the spine one cun, upper and lower lines end-straight even and regulated, as if pulling a cord.〉
translations.idiomatic: When the sores healed, a neat line of moxa scars stood a cun to either side of the spine, straight as a chalked cord from neck to waist.〉

sentences.zh: 李將軍妻病甚，呼佗視脈，曰：「傷娠而胎不去。

translations.literal: General Li's wife was very ill, called Tuo to inspect pulse, said: "Injured pregnancy yet the fetus did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of General Li was gravely ill. Hua Tuo was summoned to read her pulse and said, "She has suffered a miscarriage, but the dead fetus remains in the womb.

sentences.zh: 」將軍言：「聞實傷娠，胎已去矣。

translations.literal: " The general said: "I heard indeed injured pregnancy, the fetus already departed.
translations.idiomatic: " The general replied, "She did indeed miscarry, and we believe the fetus has passed.

sentences.zh: 」佗曰：「案脈，胎未去也。

translations.literal: " Tuo said: "According to the pulse, the fetus has not departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua Tuo said, "The pulse says the fetus is still there.

sentences.zh: 」將軍以為不然。

translations.literal: " The general thought it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: " The general did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 佗捨去，婦稍小差。

translations.literal: Tuo abandoned and left; the woman slightly small improved.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo withdrew, and the woman seemed to improve a little.

sentences.zh: 百餘日復動，更呼佗，佗曰：「此脈故事有胎。

translations.literal: After more than a hundred days again stirred, again called Tuo; Tuo said: "This pulse according to precedent has a fetus.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-odd days later her symptoms returned, and they sent for Hua Tuo again. He said, "By the pulse this is plainly a retained pregnancy.

sentences.zh: 前當生兩兒，一兒先出，血出甚多，後兒不及生。

translations.literal: Previously ought to have borne two children; one child first came out, blood came out very much; the later child did not reach being born.
translations.idiomatic: She was carrying twins. The first child was born with heavy bleeding, and the second never followed.

sentences.zh: 母不自覺，旁人亦不寤，不復迎，遂不得生。

translations.literal: The mother herself did not realize; those beside also did not awake; did not again receive; therefore could not be born.
translations.idiomatic: The mother herself did not realize it, nor did anyone else; no midwife attended the second birth, so that child never emerged.

sentences.zh: 胎死，血脈不復歸，必燥著母脊，故使多脊痛。

translations.literal: The fetus died; blood vessels no longer returned; necessarily dried adhering to the mother's spine; therefore caused much spine pain.
translations.idiomatic: The fetus died in the womb; the blood channels failed to close, so the corpse must have dried against the mother's spine, which is why her back hurts so fiercely.

sentences.zh: 今當與湯，並針一處，此死胎必出。

translations.literal: Now ought to give decoction, and together needle one place; this dead fetus necessarily will come out.
translations.idiomatic: I shall give her a draught and a single needle puncture; the dead child will pass.

sentences.zh: 」湯針既加，婦痛急如欲生者。

translations.literal: " Decoction and needle already applied; the woman's pain urgent as if about to give birth.
translations.idiomatic: " After the medicine and the needle, she was seized with labor pains as if she were delivering.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「此死胎久枯，不能自出，宜使人探之。

translations.literal: " Tuo said: "This dead fetus long dried, cannot by itself come out; ought to have a person probe it.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua Tuo said, "The dead fetus has been desiccated too long to pass on its own; someone must reach in and extract it.

sentences.zh: 」果得一死男，手足完具，色黑，長可尺所。

translations.literal: " Indeed obtained one dead male, hands and feet complete, color black, length about one chi.
translations.idiomatic: " They brought out a dead male infant, fully formed but blackened, roughly a foot in length.

sentences.zh: 佗之絕技，凡此類也。

translations.literal: Tuo's supreme skills, all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such feats were typical of Hua Tuo's singular skill.

sentences.zh: 然本作士人，以醫見業，意常自悔，後太祖親理，得病篤重，使佗專視。

translations.literal: Yet originally was a scholar-gentleman, by medicine seen as profession, mind constantly self-regretted; afterward the Grand Progenitor personally managed affairs, fell ill severely heavy, ordered Tuo solely to treat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had begun life as a literatus and bitterly regretted that the world knew him only as a physician. Later, when the Ancestor took personal charge of government and fell gravely ill, he ordered Hua Tuo to attend him exclusively.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「此近難濟，恆事攻治，可延歲月。

translations.literal: Tuo said: "This is near difficult to cure; constantly attend attack treatment, can extend years and months.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo said, "This is a chronic condition that cannot be cured outright; regular treatment can only prolong your years.

sentences.zh: 」佗久遠家思歸，因曰：「當得家書，方欲暫還耳。

translations.literal: " Tuo long far from home thought to return, therefore said: "Ought to obtain a letter from home; just wish temporarily to return.
translations.idiomatic: " He had been away from home a long time and longed to go back, so he said, "I have had word from my family; I must visit them for a short while.

sentences.zh: 」到家，辭以妻病，數乞期不反。

translations.literal: " Arrived home, excused with wife's illness, repeatedly begged extension did not return.
translations.idiomatic: " Once home he pleaded his wife's illness and repeatedly asked for more leave, refusing to return.

sentences.zh: 太祖累書呼，又敕郡縣發遣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor repeatedly wrote summoning, also ordered commanderies and counties to dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestor wrote again and again summoning him and ordered the local authorities to send him on his way.

sentences.zh: 佗恃能厭食事，猶不上道。

translations.literal: Tuo relied on ability, detested serving in office matters, still did not take the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo trusted in his own gifts, despised menial service at court, and still would not set out.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，使人往檢。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly angry, sent people to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestor flew into a rage and sent agents to investigate.

sentences.zh: 若妻信病，賜小豆四十斛，寬假限日；

translations.literal: If the wife truly ill, bestow forty hu of small beans, extend grace limit days;
translations.idiomatic: If his wife were truly ill, grant forty hu of beans and extend his leave.

sentences.zh: 若其虛詐，便收送之。

translations.literal: If it was false deceit, then seize and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: If the story were a lie, arrest him and bring him in.

sentences.zh: 於是傳付許獄，考驗首服。

translations.literal: Thereupon transmitted delivered to Xu prison, examined and tested confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo was therefore sent to the jail at Xu and under interrogation confessed to the fraud.

sentences.zh: 荀彧請曰：「佗術實工，人命所縣，宜含宥之。

translations.literal: Xun Yu requested saying: "Tuo's art is truly skillful; human lives hang from it; ought to contain and forgive him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu pleaded, "Hua Tuo's art is truly masterful; men's lives depend on him; you should show mercy.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「不憂，天下當無此鼠輩耶？

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "Not worried; under Heaven ought there not be these rat fellows?
translations.idiomatic: " The Ancestor retorted, "Why worry? Are there no other vermin like him under heaven?

sentences.zh: 」遂考竟佗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon examined to the end Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua Tuo was therefore executed.

sentences.zh: 佗臨死，出一卷書與獄吏，曰：「此可以活人。

translations.literal: Tuo at the point of death, produced one scroll book gave to prison clerk, said: "This can keep people alive.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Hua Tuo handed a scroll to the jailer and said, "This can save lives.

sentences.zh: 」吏畏法不受，佗亦不強，索火燒之。

translations.literal: " The clerk feared the law and did not accept; Tuo also did not force, sought fire and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: " The man dared not take it for fear of the law. Hua Tuo did not insist, called for a fire, and burned the book.

sentences.zh: 佗死後，太祖頭風未除。

translations.literal: After Tuo died, the Grand Progenitor's head wind was not removed.
translations.idiomatic: After Hua Tuo's death the Ancestor's headaches were never cured.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「佗能愈此。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Tuo can cure this."
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestor said, "Hua Tuo could have cured this."

sentences.zh: 小人養吾病，欲以自重，然吾不殺此子，亦終當不為我斷此根原耳。

translations.literal: This petty man nursed my illness, wishing thereby to make himself weighty; yet had I not killed this fellow, in the end he still would never have rooted out this source for me."
translations.idiomatic: "That wretch kept my sickness lingering so he could make himself indispensable; yet even if I had spared him, he would never have cut out the root of the malady for me."

sentences.zh: 」及後愛子倉舒病困，太祖歎曰：「吾悔殺華佗，令此兒強死也。」

translations.literal: " And afterward the beloved son Cangshu fell ill in extremity, the Grand Progenitor sighed saying: "I regret killing Hua Tuo, causing this child to die before his time.""
translations.idiomatic: "Later, when his beloved son Cangshu lay at death's door, the Ancestor sighed, 'I regret putting Hua Tuo to death — it has forced this boy to die before his time.'"

sentences.zh: 初，軍吏李成苦欬嗽，晝夜不寤，時吐膿血，以問佗。

translations.literal: Originally, army clerk Li Cheng suffered bitter cough, day and night without rest, at times spat pus and blood, and consulted Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the army clerk Li Cheng had been racked by a cough that allowed him no rest day or night and sometimes brought up bloody pus; he consulted Hua Tuo.

sentences.zh: 佗言：「君病腸臃，欬之所吐，非從肺來也。

translations.literal: Tuo said: "Your illness is an intestinal abscess; what the cough brings up does not come from the lungs."
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo said, "You have an abscess in the intestines; what you cough up does not come from the lungs."

sentences.zh: 與君散兩錢，當吐二升餘膿血訖，快自養，一月可小起，好自將愛，一年便健。

translations.literal: I give you two qian of powder; you ought to vomit more than two sheng of pus and blood; then convalesce at ease; in one month you may rise a little; take good care of yourself; in one year you will be strong."
translations.idiomatic: "I will give you two measures of powder; it will bring up over two sheng of pus and blood. Rest well afterward — in a month you may be up and about, and in a year you will be hale again if you mind your regimen."

sentences.zh: 十八歲當一小發，服此散，亦行復差。

translations.literal: At eighteen sui there ought to be one small flare; take this powder, and you will again recover.
translations.idiomatic: When you are eighteen a mild relapse will occur; take this same powder and you will recover again.

sentences.zh: 若不得此藥，故當死。

translations.literal: If you cannot obtain this medicine, you will therefore die."
translations.idiomatic: "Without that medicine you will die."

sentences.zh: 」復與兩錢散，成得藥去。

translations.literal: " Again gave two qian of powder; Cheng obtained the medicine and departed."
translations.idiomatic: "He gave Li two measures of the powder, and Li took it home."

sentences.zh: 五六歲，親中人有病如成者，謂成曰：「卿今強健，我欲死，何忍無急去藥，

translations.literal: Five or six years later, someone among relatives had an illness like Cheng's, and said to Cheng: "You are now strong and healthy; I am dying; how can you bear, without urgent need, to withhold the medicine —
translations.idiomatic: Five or six years later a kinsman fell ill with the same complaint and said to Li, "You are sound and strong now, while I am dying; how can you begrudge me the powder you no longer urgently need —

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：古語以藏為去。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi submits: In ancient parlance the word cang "store" was used in the sense "withhold."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: In older idiom the word for "storing" could mean withholding from someone.〉

sentences.zh: 以待不祥？

translations.literal: — to await an ill fate?"
translations.idiomatic: — and make me wait for a fatal end?"

sentences.zh: 先持貸我，我差，為卿從華佗更索。

translations.literal: First lend it to me; when I improve, I will for you seek more from Hua Tuo."
translations.idiomatic: "Lend it to me now; when I am well I shall get a fresh supply from Hua Tuo for you."

sentences.zh: 」成與之。

translations.literal: " Cheng gave it to him."
translations.idiomatic: "Li gave it to him."

sentences.zh: 已故到譙，適值佗見收，怱怱不忍從求。

translations.literal: Therefore he had already reached Qiao, just as it happened that Tuo was being seized; in haste he could not bear to go and seek.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Qiao to refill the prescription, Hua Tuo had been arrested; in the press of events he could not bring himself to ask.

sentences.zh: 後十八歲，成病竟發，無藥可服，以至於死。

translations.literal: Later at eighteen sui, Cheng's illness in the end flared; there was no medicine to take, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years later Li's sickness returned as foretold; with no medicine left, he died.

sentences.zh: 〈佗別傳曰：人有在青龍中見山陽太守廣陵劉景宗，景宗說中平日數見華佗，其治病手脈之候，其驗若神。

translations.literal: 〈Tuo's separate biography says: Someone during the Qinglong era saw Liu Jingzong, Grand Administrator of Shanyang at Guangling; Jingzong said that in the Zhongping years he had often seen Hua Tuo treat the sick — his pulse diagnosis was as if divine.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The separate biography of Hua Tuo records: During the Qinglong era someone met Liu Jingzong, grand administrator of Shanyang then living at Guangling, who said that in the Zhongping years he had often watched Hua Tuo work — his pulse reading seemed almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 瑯琊劉勛為河內太守，有女年幾二十，左腳膝裡上有瘡，癢而不痛。

translations.literal: Liu Xun of Langya was Grand Administrator of Henei; he had a daughter nearly twenty years old; on the inside of her left knee she had a sore; it itched but did not hurt.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun of Langya was serving as grand administrator of Henei. His daughter, not yet twenty, had an itch beneath the left kneecap that did not truly hurt.

sentences.zh: 瘡愈數十日復發，如此七八年，迎佗使視，佗曰：「是易治之。

translations.literal: The sore would heal for several tens of days and then flare again; thus for seven or eight years; they welcomed Tuo to inspect; Tuo said: "This is easy to treat."
translations.idiomatic: The sore would clear for a few weeks and then return, and so it went for seven or eight years. They sent for Hua Tuo, who said, "This is easy to cure."

sentences.zh: 當得稻糠黃色犬一頭，好馬二疋。

translations.literal: You ought to obtain one yellow dog fed on rice husks, and two good horses.
translations.idiomatic: You will need one yellow dog raised on rice husks and two sound mounts."

sentences.zh: 」以繩繫犬頸，使走馬牽犬，馬極輒易，計馬走三十餘里，犬不能行，復令步人拖曳，計向五十里。

translations.literal: He tied a rope around the dog's neck, had a galloping horse drag the dog; when the horse was exhausted he exchanged it; counting, the horse ran more than thirty li and the dog could not walk; again he ordered foot-soldiers to drag it; counting toward fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: He tethered the dog and had a horse gallop to tow it along, changing mounts whenever one tired until they had covered thirty-odd li and the dog collapsed; foot soldiers then hauled the beast until the tally neared fifty li.

sentences.zh: 乃以藥飲女，女即安臥不知人。

translations.literal: Thereupon gave the girl medicine to drink; the girl then lay peacefully insensible.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the girl a draught, and she sank into a sleep as deep as unconsciousness.

sentences.zh: 因取大刀斷犬腹近後腳之前，以所斷之處向瘡口，令去二三寸。

translations.literal: Then took a large knife and cut open the dog's belly just in front of the hind legs, placed the cut against the mouth of the sore, and held it away two or three cun.
translations.idiomatic: With a great knife he opened the dog's belly just forward of the hind legs, pressed the wound to the girl's ulcer, and held the edges two or three cun apart.

sentences.zh: 停之須臾，有若蛇者從瘡中而出，便以鐵椎橫貫蛇頭。

translations.literal: After pausing a moment, something like a snake came out from within the sore; then he used an iron spike to transfix the snake's head crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: After a pause something serpent-shaped wriggled out of the ulcer; he drove an iron skewer sideways through its head.

sentences.zh: 蛇在皮中動搖良久，須臾不動，乃牽出，長三尺所，純是蛇，但有眼處而無童子，又逆鱗耳。

translations.literal: The snake moved and shook inside the skin for a long time; after a moment it did not move; then he pulled it out; length about three chi; it was purely a snake, but where there should have been eyes there were no pupils, and it had reversed scales.
translations.idiomatic: It thrashed under the skin for a long time, then went still; when drawn out it was about three feet long, serpent-like though eyeless and with scales set backward.

sentences.zh: 以膏散著瘡中，七日愈。

translations.literal: He applied ointment and powder to the sore; in seven days she was cured.
translations.idiomatic: He packed the wound with salve and powder, and in seven days she was healed.

sentences.zh: 又有人苦頭眩，頭不得舉，目不得視，積年。

translations.literal: Also there was someone who suffered head vertigo; his head could not be raised; his eyes could not see; for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: Another man had endured years of vertigo — he could not lift his head or open his eyes.

sentences.zh: 佗使悉解衣倒懸，令頭去地一二寸，濡布拭身體，令周匝，候視諸脈，盡出五色。

translations.literal: Tuo had him completely strip, hang him inverted, ordered his head to be one or two cun from the ground, used a soaked cloth to wipe the body, made it all around, waited and inspected all the vessels; they all showed five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo stripped him, hung him upside down with his head an inch or two above the floor, and swabbed his body with a wet cloth until every vessel showed through the skin in five colors.

sentences.zh: 佗令弟子數人以鈹刀決脈，五色血盡，視赤血，乃下，以膏摩被覆，汗自出周匝，飲以亭歷犬血散，立愈。

translations.literal: Tuo ordered several disciples to use lances to open the vessels; when the five-colored blood was exhausted and true red blood appeared, then he stopped; he rubbed ointment on him and covered him; sweat emerged all around; he gave him to drink tingli and dog-blood powder; immediately he was cured.
translations.idiomatic: He had disciples lance the vessels until the colored blood ran clear and scarlet blood appeared, then salved and wrapped him; when sweat broke out all over he administered a powder of tingli and dog blood, and the man recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 又有婦人長病經年，世謂寒熱注病者。

translations.literal: Also there was a woman long ill for accumulated years; the world called it alternating chills and fever pouring illness.
translations.idiomatic: Another woman had lain ill for years with what people called a chronic alternating fever.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月中，佗令坐石槽中，平旦用寒水汲灌，云當滿百。

translations.literal: In the middle of the eleventh month of winter, Tuo ordered her to sit in a stone trough; at dawn he used cold water drawn and poured, saying it ought to reach a hundred dippers.
translations.idiomatic: One winter in the eleventh month he seated her in a stone basin at daybreak and had boys pour in cold water until a hundred bucketfuls had been emptied.

sentences.zh: 始七八灌，會戰欲死，灌者懼，欲止。

translations.literal: At the start, after seven or eight pourings, she convulsed as if she would die; the pourers feared and wished to stop.
translations.idiomatic: After the seventh or eighth dousing she convulsed as if dying; the pourers panicked and wanted to quit.

sentences.zh: 佗令滿數。

translations.literal: Tuo ordered them to complete the number.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo made them finish the count.

sentences.zh: 將至八十灌，熱氣乃蒸出，囂囂高二三尺。

translations.literal: Approaching the eightieth pouring, hot vapor then steamed forth, hissing two or three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Near the eightieth dousing steam began to rise from her body in a column two or three feet high.

sentences.zh: 滿百灌，佗乃使然火溫床，厚覆，良久汗洽出，著粉，汗燥便愈。

translations.literal: When the hundred pourings were complete, Tuo then ordered a fire to warm the bed, thick coverings; after a long time copious sweat emerged; he applied powder; when the sweat dried she was cured.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundredth was poured, he had a bed warmed with coals and wrapped her thickly until sweat poured forth; he dusted her with powder, and when the sweat dried she was cured.

sentences.zh: 又有人病腹中半切痛，十餘日中，鬢眉墮落。

translations.literal: Also there was someone whose belly suffered half-cutting pain; within ten-odd days, his temple hair and eyebrows fell off.
translations.idiomatic: Another patient felt as if his vitals were being sliced in two; within a fortnight his brows and sideburns fell out.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「是脾半腐，可刳腹養治也。

translations.literal: Tuo said: "This is the spleen half rotten; one can open the belly and nurse it."
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo said, "Half the spleen has putrefied; open the abdomen and nurse it."

sentences.zh: 」使飲藥令臥，破腹就視，脾果半腐壞。

translations.literal: He made him drink medicine and lie down; he broke open the belly and looked; the spleen was indeed half rotten and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He drugged the man to sleep, opened the belly, and found the spleen half in ruins.

sentences.zh: 以刀斷之，刮去惡肉，以膏傅瘡，飲之以藥，百日平復。〉

translations.literal: With a knife he cut it away, scraped off the bad flesh, smeared ointment on the wound, gave him medicine to drink; in a hundred days he was restored.〉
translations.idiomatic: He excised the ruin, scraped away the dead tissue, salved the wound, and administered medicine; in a hundred days the patient was whole again.〉

sentences.zh: 廣陵吳普、彭城樊阿皆從佗學。

translations.literal: Wu Pu of Guangling and Fan A of Pengcheng both studied under Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Pu of Guangling and Fan A of Pengcheng both studied under Hua Tuo.

sentences.zh: 普依準佗治，多所全濟。

translations.literal: Pu modeled himself on Tuo's treatment and many were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Pu followed Hua Tuo's methods and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 佗語普曰：「人體欲得勞動，但不當使極爾。

translations.literal: Tuo told Pu: "The human body wishes to obtain exertion, but one ought not drive it to the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo told him, "The body wants exercise, but you must never exhaust it."

sentences.zh: 動搖則谷氣得消，血脈流通，病不得生，譬猶戶樞不朽是也。

translations.literal: If it is shaken and moved, then the grain qi can digest, blood vessels flow freely, and illness cannot arise — it is like a door hinge that never rots."
translations.idiomatic: "Stir the frame and the grain qi will digest, the channels will run clear, and sickness cannot take hold — it is like a gate hinge that never rusts."

sentences.zh: 是以古之仙者為導引之事，熊頸鴟顧，引輓腰體，動諸關節，以求難老。

translations.literal: Therefore the immortals of old practiced daoyin — bear-neck and owl-turn, pulling waist and torso, moving all the joints — to seek to postpone old age.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the immortals of old practiced daoyin — stretching like a bear, turning the neck like an owl, working waist and spine, flexing every joint — to keep age at bay."

sentences.zh: 吾有一術，名五禽之戲，一曰虎，二曰鹿，三曰熊，四曰猿，五曰鳥，亦以除疾，並利蹄足，以當導引。

translations.literal: I have one technique, named the Five-Animal Play: first the tiger, second the deer, third the bear, fourth the ape, fifth the bird. It also removes illness and benefits sinew and bone, and can substitute for daoyin."
translations.idiomatic: "I teach a sequence called the Five-Animal Frolic — tiger, deer, bear, ape, and bird. It drives out disease, strengthens sinew and bone, and serves the same purpose as daoyin."

sentences.zh: 體中不快，起作一禽之戲，沾濡汗出，因上著粉，身體輕便，腹中欲食。

translations.literal: If the body feels unwell, rise and perform one animal's play; a light sweat will emerge; then powder yourself; the body becomes light and nimble, and the belly wishes to eat."
translations.idiomatic: "Whenever you feel out of sorts, rise and perform one animal: you will sweat lightly, then dust yourself; the body grows supple and the appetite returns."

sentences.zh: 」普施行之，年九十餘，耳目聰明，齒牙完堅。

translations.literal: Pu practiced it; he lived more than ninety years; ears and eyes were sharp and bright; teeth remained complete and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Pu kept at it past ninety with keen hearing and sight and sound teeth.

sentences.zh: 阿善針術。

translations.literal: A was skilled at the art of needling.
translations.idiomatic: Fan A excelled at acupuncture.

sentences.zh: 凡醫咸言背及胸藏之間不可妄針，針之不過四分，而阿針背入一二寸，巨闕胸藏針下五六寸，而病輒皆瘳。

translations.literal: All physicians alike said that between the back and the chest over the viscera one must not rashly needle, and needling must not exceed four fen; yet A needled the back one or two cun deep, and at the Juque point over the chest viscera needled five or six cun down, and the illness was always cured.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians warned that the back and the regions over the vitals must not be needled rashly, and never deeper than four fen; Fan A drove needles an inch or two into the back and five or six cun into Juque over the heart — yet every sickness cleared.

sentences.zh: 阿從佗求可服食益於人者，佗授以漆葉青黏散。

translations.literal: A sought from Tuo something that could be swallowed and eaten to benefit people; Tuo gave him lacquer-leaf and qinglian powder.
translations.idiomatic: Fan A asked Hua Tuo for a formula that could be taken for long-term benefit, and Hua Tuo gave him the lacquer-leaf and qinglian powder.

sentences.zh: 漆葉屑一升，青黏屑十四兩，以是為率，言久服去三蟲，利五藏，輕體，使人頭不白。

translations.literal: Lacquer-leaf scrapings one sheng, qinglian scrapings fourteen liang — take this as the proportion; he said long-term use expels the three worms, benefits the five viscera, lightens the body, and keeps a person's hair from turning white.
translations.idiomatic: One sheng of lacquer-leaf shavings to fourteen liang of qinglian shavings — that is the ratio. Prolonged use, he said, expels the three worms, benefits the five viscera, lightens the body, and keeps the hair from graying.

sentences.zh: 阿從其言，壽百餘歲。

translations.literal: A followed his words and lived more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Fan A followed his advice and lived past a hundred.

sentences.zh: 漆葉處所而有，青黏生於豐、沛、彭城及朝歌云。

translations.literal: Lacquer leaves are found in every district; qinglian is said to grow in Feng, Pei, Pengcheng, and Chaoge.
translations.idiomatic: Lacquer leaves grow almost everywhere; qinglian is said to come from Feng, Pei, Pengcheng, and Chaoge.

sentences.zh: 〈佗別傳曰：青黏者，一名地節，一名黃芝，主理五藏，益精氣。

translations.literal: 〈The separate biography says: Qinglian has one name "earth node" and one name "yellow fungus"; it governs the five viscera and benefits essence and qi.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The separate biography identifies qinglian as "earth node" or "yellow fungus," said to regulate the five viscera and replenish essential breath."

sentences.zh: 本出於迷入山者，見仙人服之，以告佗。

translations.literal: Originally it came from a man lost in the mountains who saw an immortal ingest it and reported it to Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: It first came to light when a lost traveler saw an immortal take it and told Hua Tuo.

sentences.zh: 佗以為佳，輒語阿，阿又秘之。

translations.literal: Tuo deemed it excellent and always told A; A again kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tuo judged it excellent and passed it to Fan A, who guarded it as a secret.

sentences.zh: 近者人見阿之壽而氣力強盛，怪之，遂責阿所服，因醉亂誤道之。

translations.literal: Those who lately saw A's longevity and his great strength marveled, pressed A for what he took, and because of drunken confusion he mistakenly told them.
translations.idiomatic: In time people marveled at Fan A's vigor and pressed him for his formula; he let it slip one drunken night.

sentences.zh: 法一施，人多服者，皆有大驗。

translations.literal: Once the method was broadcast, many who took it all obtained great confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the recipe spread, everyone who tried it found dramatic benefit.

sentences.zh: 文帝《典論論郤儉等事》曰：「潁川郤儉能辟穀，餌伏苓。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's *Dianlun* essay "On Xi Jian and Others" says: "Xi Jian of Yingchuan could abstain from grain and fed on poria."
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen's *Dianlun* essay "On Xi Jian and Others," he writes: "Xi Jian of Yingchuan could fast from grain and lived on poria."

sentences.zh: 甘陵甘始亦善行氣，老有少容。

translations.literal: Gan Shi of Ganling was also good at moving qi; in old age he had a youthful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Shi of Ganling was likewise skilled in breath control and kept a youthful face in old age.

sentences.zh: 廬江左慈知補導之術。

translations.literal: Zuo Ci of Lujiang understood supplementation and guiding arts.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Ci of Lujiang knew restorative daoyin.

sentences.zh: 並為軍吏。

translations.literal: Together they served as army clerks.
translations.idiomatic: They all held minor military posts.

sentences.zh: 初，儉之至，巿伏苓價暴數倍。

translations.literal: At first, when Jian arrived, the market price of poria suddenly multiplied several times.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Jian first arrived the price of poria in the market shot up several fold.

sentences.zh: 議郎安平李覃學其辟穀，餐伏苓，飲寒水，中洩利，殆至隕命。

translations.literal: Gentleman-Consultant Li Tan of Anping studied his grain-avoidance, ate poria, drank cold water, suffered internal diarrhea, and nearly lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan of Anping, a gentleman-consultant, imitated the fast, ate poria, drank cold water, and fell into such violent diarrhea that he barely survived.

sentences.zh: 後始來，眾人無不鴟視狼顧，呼吸吐納。

translations.literal: Later when Shi came, the crowd all owl-stared and wolf-glanced, breathing in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan Shi appeared the crowd mimicked him with owl stares and wolfish glances, practicing inhales and exhales.

sentences.zh: 軍謀祭酒弘農董芬為之過差，氣閉不通，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Military Libationer Dong Fen of Hongnong overdid it; his qi blocked and would not pass; after a long time he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fen of Hongnong, the army libationer, pushed the exercise too far, stopped his breath, and lay unconscious for a long time before he revived.

sentences.zh: 左慈到，又競受其補導之術，至寺人嚴峻，往從問受。

translations.literal: When Zuo Ci arrived, they again vied to receive his supplementation arts, until even the eunuch Yan Jun went to follow and learn.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Ci joined them and everyone scrambled to learn his daoyin, until even the eunuch Yan Jun went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 閹豎真無事於斯術也，人之逐聲，乃至於是。

translations.literal: Eunuchs truly have no business with this art; yet people chase fashion to such lengths.
translations.idiomatic: That castrates should chase such arts shows how hollow men's pursuit of novelty can be.

sentences.zh: 光和中，北海王和平亦好道術，自以當仙。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era, Wang Heping of Beihai also loved the arts of the Way and imagined himself destined for immortality.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghe era Wang Heping of Beihai dabbled in esoteric arts and fancied himself a future immortal.

sentences.zh: 濟南孫邕少事之，從至京師。

translations.literal: Sun Yong of Jinan had served him in youth and followed him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong of Jinan had been his disciple since boyhood and accompanied him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會和平病死，邕因葬之東陶，有書百餘卷，藥數囊，悉以送之。

translations.literal: When Heping died of illness on the way, Yong buried him east of Tao; there were more than a hundred scrolls and several bags of drugs, all of which were sent into the grave with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Heping died on the road, Sun buried him east of Tao, interring more than a hundred scrolls and several sacks of drugs with the corpse.

sentences.zh: 後弟子夏榮言其屍解。

translations.literal: Later the disciple Xia Rong said he had "liberated his corpse."
translations.idiomatic: Later the disciple Xia Rong claimed he had "liberated the corpse" — a Daoist euphemism for ascension.

sentences.zh: 邕至今恨不取其寶書仙藥。

translations.literal: Yong to this day regrets not taking his treasure books and immortal drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong still rues not seizing those precious tomes and elixirs.

sentences.zh: 劉向惑於鴻寶之說，君遊眩於子政之言，古今愚謬，豈唯一人哉！

translations.literal: Liu Xiang was deluded by the Hongbao lore; you, my lord, were dazzled by Zizheng's words — folly runs through the ages — can it be blamed on a single man!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang was misled by the *Hongbao*; you, my lord, were dazzled by Liu Xiang's rhetoric — folly is not the monopoly of one age or one man!

sentences.zh: 」東阿王作

translations.literal: " The Prince of Dong'e composed
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dong'e composed the following treatise.

sentences.zh: 〈辯道論〉

translations.literal: 〈"On Discerning the Way"〉
translations.idiomatic: The essay was entitled *On Discerning the Way*.

sentences.zh: 曰：「世有方士，吾王悉所招致，甘陵有甘始，廬江有左慈，陽城有郤儉。

translations.literal: says: "In the world there are recipe masters; my prince has gathered them all: at Ganling there is Gan Shi, at Lujiang Zuo Ci, at Yangcheng Xi Jian."
translations.idiomatic: It says: "The world has its recipe masters, and my royal brother has collected them: Gan Shi at Ganling, Zuo Ci at Lujiang, Xi Jian at Yangcheng."

sentences.zh: 始行氣導引，慈曉房中之術，儉善辟穀，悉號三百歲。

translations.literal: Shi practiced moving qi and daoyin; Ci understood chamber arts; Jian was good at grain-avoidance; all were styled three hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Shi practiced breath circulation and daoyin; Zuo Ci knew bedroom arts; Xi Jian excelled at fasting; each claimed three centuries of life.

sentences.zh: 卒所以集之於魏國者，誠恐斯人之徒，接姦宄以欺眾，行妖慝以惑民，豈復欲觀神仙於瀛洲，求安期於海島，釋金輅而履雲輿，棄六驥而美飛龍哉？

translations.literal: The reason they were finally assembled in the state of Wei was truly the fear that such men might join treachery to deceive the multitude and work occult evil to bewitch the people — was it because he wished to watch immortals on Yingzhou, seek Anqi on an island, cast aside the metal-wheeled carriage to tread a cloud-chariot, abandon six matched steeds to prize flying dragons?"
translations.idiomatic: They were rounded up in Wei because the court dreaded their kind abetting villains to swindle the people and peddling sorcery to lead them astray — was it really so that anyone hoped to sight immortals off Yingzhou, summon Anqi from the sea, trade a bronze carriage for a cloud chariot, or trade six fine coursers for winged dragons?"

sentences.zh: 自家王與太子及餘兄弟咸以為調笑，不信之矣。

translations.literal: From our prince and the crown prince down to the rest of us brothers, we all took it for mockery and did not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: From our royal brother and the heir apparent to the rest of us princes, we treated it all as a joke and put no faith in them.

sentences.zh: 然始等知上遇之有恆，奉不過於員吏，賞不加於無功，海島難得而遊，六黻難得而佩，終不敢進虛誕之言，出非常之語。

translations.literal: Yet Shi and the others knew that the sovereign's favor toward them had its limits — their stipends never exceeded those of ordinary clerks, and rewards were not heaped on the undeserving — the fairy isles were hard to visit and the six emblem-horses hard to harness; in the end they dared not advance empty boasts or utter outlandish claims.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gan Shi and his like saw that imperial favor had its limits — their salaries never outranked a clerk's, and unearned gifts were withheld — the fairy isles were unreachable and the six coursers impossible to yoke; so they never ventured hollow boasts or wild tales.

sentences.zh: 余嘗試郤儉絕穀百日，躬與之寢處，行步起居自若也。

translations.literal: I once put Xi Jian on a grain fast for a hundred days, lodged with him myself, and his walking and rising were as usual.
translations.idiomatic: I once kept Xi Jian on a grainless diet for a hundred days, sharing his quarters; he walked and rose as usual.

sentences.zh: 夫人不食七日則死，而儉乃如是。

translations.literal: A person who does not eat for seven days will die, yet Jian was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary men starve in seven days, yet Jian endured thus.

sentences.zh: 然不必益壽，可以療疾而不憚饑饉焉。

translations.literal: Yet it need not lengthen life; it can treat illness and free one from fear of famine.
translations.idiomatic: It may not extend the years, but it can cure certain ills and blunt the edge of hunger.

sentences.zh: 左慈善修房內之術，差可終命，然自非有志至精，莫能行也。

translations.literal: Zuo Ci was good at cultivating chamber arts — enough perhaps to finish one's allotted span — yet unless the will is utterly concentrated, none can practice them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Ci was skilled in bedroom cultivation — enough perhaps to live out one's natural term — yet none but the most resolute can keep the discipline.

sentences.zh: 甘始者，老而有少容，自諸術士咸共歸之。

translations.literal: As for Gan Shi, he was old yet had a youthful face, and all the recipe masters deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Shi was old but looked young, and every adept bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 然始辭繁寡實，頗有怪言。

translations.literal: Yet Shi's words were prolix and thin on fact, and he uttered quite a few marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his speech ran on with little substance and plenty of tall tales.

sentences.zh: 余常辟左右，獨與之談，問其所行，溫顏以誘之，美辭以導之，始語余：『吾本師姓韓字世雄，嘗與師於南海作金，前後數四，投萬斤金於海。

translations.literal: I often dismissed attendants and spoke with him alone, asking what he practiced; with gentle face I enticed him, with fair words I guided him; Shi told me: "My original teacher surnamed Han, styled Shixiong, once with my teacher at the South Sea made gold, four times in all, casting ten thousand jin of gold into the sea."
translations.idiomatic: I often sent servants away and questioned him alone, coaxing with kind looks and smooth phrases until he told me: "My first master was surnamed Han, styled Shixiong; he and I once transmuted gold on the South Sea four separate times, casting ten thousand jin of gold into the waves."

sentences.zh: 』又言：『諸梁時，西域胡來獻香罽、腰帶、割玉刀，時悔不取也。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the Liang era western-region Hu came to present fragrant rugs, belts, and jade-cutting knives — I regret I did not take them."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "When the Liang ruled, Hu from the Western Regions brought perfumed felts, belts, and jade knives — I still regret I did not accept them."

sentences.zh: 』又言：『車師之西國。

translations.literal: He also said: "West of the kingdom of Cheshi lies another realm."
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed that west of Cheshi lay another country.

sentences.zh: 兒生，擘背出脾，欲其食少而弩行也。

translations.literal: when a child is born they split its back to expose the spleen, wishing it to eat little and to walk like a crossbow."
translations.idiomatic: — they split a newborn's back to expose the spleen so the child eats little and strides like a drawn bow."

sentences.zh: 』又言：『取鯉魚五寸一雙，合其一煮藥，俱投沸膏中，有藥者奮尾鼓鰓，遊行沉浮，有若處淵，其一者已熟而可啖。

translations.literal: He also said: "Take a pair of carp five cun long; boil one with medicine and put both into boiling fat — the medicated one thrashes tail and gills and swims up and down as if in a pool, while the other is already cooked and ready to eat."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Take two five-cun carp: stew one with drugs and drop both into boiling lard — the treated fish lashes tail and gills and swims about as if in a pond, while the other is simply cooked and ready to eat."

sentences.zh: 』余時問：『言率可試不？

translations.literal: I then asked: "Can these claims generally be tested?"
translations.idiomatic: I asked, "Can any of this actually be demonstrated?"

sentences.zh: 』言：『是藥去此逾萬里，當出塞；

translations.literal: He answered: "That drug lies more than ten thousand li away; one must leave the frontier;"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The drug grows beyond ten thousand li; you must cross the border;"

sentences.zh: 始不自行不能得也。

translations.literal: Shi himself cannot go and cannot obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: and Gan Shi himself cannot fetch it."

sentences.zh: 』言不盡於此，頗難悉載，故粗舉其巨怪者。

translations.literal: His words did not end here, but they are hard to record in full; therefore I roughly cite the chief marvels.
translations.idiomatic: There was more, but it is tedious to set it all down — so I give only the wildest samples.

sentences.zh: 始若遭秦始皇、漢武帝，則復為徐巿、欒大之徒也。」〉

translations.literal: Had Shi met Qin Shihuang or Han Wudi, he would again have been another Xu Fu or Luan Da."〉
translations.idiomatic: Had Gan Shi served the First Emperor or Emperor Wu, he would have been another Xu Fu or Luan Da."〉

sentences.zh: 杜夔字公良，河南人也。

translations.literal: Du Kui, courtesy name Gongliang, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui, courtesy name Gongliang, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 以知音為雅樂郎，中平五年，疾去官。

translations.literal: Because he understood pitch he became a Gentleman of Elegant Music; in the fifth year of Zhongping he fell ill and left office.
translations.idiomatic: His ear for pitch won him a post as gentleman of refined music; in the fifth year of Zhongping he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 州郡司徒禮辟，以世亂奔荊州。

translations.literal: Provinces, commanderies, the Minister of Education, all ceremonially summoned him; because the age was in chaos he fled to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery authorities and the minister of education all offered him posts, but he fled to Jingzhou amid the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表令與孟曜為漢主合雅樂，樂備，表欲庭觀之，夔諫曰：「今將軍號

translations.literal: The Governor of Jingzhou, Liu Biao, ordered him together with Meng Yao to compose elegant music for the Han sovereign; when the music was ready, Biao wished to watch it in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Biao paired him with Meng Yao to compose the Han court's ritual music. When the score was complete, Liu wanted a courtyard performance.

translations.literal: (The character 'not' appears in some versions.)
translations.idiomatic: (Some manuscripts insert the word "not" here.)

sentences.zh: 為天子合樂，而庭作之，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: To compose music for the Son of Heaven and yet perform it in your own courtyard — surely that cannot be proper!"
translations.idiomatic: To assemble the Son of Heaven's ritual music and then play it in your private hall — that cannot be right!"

sentences.zh: 」表納其言而止。

translations.literal: " Biao accepted his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Biao took his advice and dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 後表子琮降太祖，太祖以夔為軍謀祭酒，參太樂事，因令創製雅樂。

translations.literal: Later Biao's son Cong surrendered to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor appointed Kui Army Libationer in charge of the Grand Music, ordered him to devise new ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao's son Liu Cong submitted to the Ancestor, Du Kui was named army libationer with charge of the grand music and was told to create fresh ritual scores.

sentences.zh: 夔善鐘律，聰思過人，絲竹八音，靡所不能，惟歌舞非所長。

translations.literal: Kui was skilled in bells and pitch-pipes; his intelligence exceeded others'; of the eight kinds of strings and winds there was none he could not play — only song and dance were not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui mastered bells and temperament; he was brighter than most and could handle every instrument of the orchestra, though he was no dancer or singer.

sentences.zh: 時散郎鄧靜、尹齊善詠雅樂，歌師尹胡能歌宗廟郊祀之曲，舞師馮肅、服養曉知先代諸舞，夔總統研精，遠考諸經，近採故事，教習講肄，備作樂器，紹复先代古樂，皆自夔始也。

translations.literal: At the time Gentlemen of Scattered Rank Deng Jing and Yin Qi were good at chanting elegant music; the singing master Yin Hu could sing the hymns for the ancestral temple and suburban sacrifices; the dance masters Feng Su and Fu Yang understood the dances of former ages; Kui presided over them all, studied deeply, consulted the classics from afar and collected precedents from recent times, taught and rehearsed, prepared the instruments, and restored the ancient music of earlier dynasties — all began with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The scattered gentlemen Deng Jing and Yin Qi excelled at singing the ritual airs; Yin Hu led the temple and suburban hymns; Feng Su and Fu Yang knew the old choreography. Du Kui directed them all, pored over the canon, drew on recent precedent, drilled the musicians, built the instruments, and revived the antique repertoire — work that began with him.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，為太樂令、協律都尉。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era he became Director of the Grand Music and Commandant of Harmonized Pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Huangchu reign he rose to director of the grand music and commandant of harmonized pitch.

sentences.zh: 漢鑄鐘工柴玉巧有意思，形器之中，多所造作，亦為時貴人見知。

translations.literal: The Han bell-founder Chai Yu was clever and inventive; among vessels and tools he made many things, and he was also noticed by the notables of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Han bell-caster Chai Yu was ingenious and prolific; he fashioned many implements and had won favor among the great men of the day.

sentences.zh: 夔令玉鑄銅鐘，其聲均清濁多不如法，數毀改作。

translations.literal: Kui ordered Yu to cast bronze bells; their tones were evenly clear and muddy but mostly did not accord with the rule; repeatedly destroyed and recast.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui told him to cast bronze bells, but their balance of clear and muffled notes kept missing the standard, so the work was smashed and begun again.

sentences.zh: 玉甚厭之，謂夔清濁任意，頗拒捍夔。

translations.literal: Yu greatly hated this, saying Kui made clear and muddy tones arbitrarily, and rather resisted Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Yu grew resentful, accusing Du Kui of arbitrary tuning and openly defying him.

sentences.zh: 夔、玉更相白於太祖，太祖取所鑄鐘，雜錯更試，然知夔為精而玉之妄也，於是罪玉及諸子，皆為養馬士。

translations.literal: Kui and Yu each reported the other to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor took the bells cast, mixed and tested them, then knew Kui was precise and Yu was reckless; thereupon punished Yu and his sons, all becoming horse-keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Each man appealed to the Ancestor, who had the bells tried at random and saw that Du Kui was right and Chai Yu wrong; Chai Yu and his sons were reduced to stable hands.

sentences.zh: 文帝愛待玉，又嘗令夔與

translations.literal: Emperor Wen favored Yu and once ordered Kui together with
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen doted on Chai Yu and once told Du Kui to join

sentences.zh: （左原）

translations.literal: (Zuo Yuan)
translations.idiomatic: (Zuo Yuan)

sentences.zh: 〔左𩥄〕等於賓客之中吹笙鼓琴，夔有難色，由是帝意不悅。

translations.literal: 〔Zuo Dan〕 and others among the guests to blow sheng and strum qin; Kui had a troubled look, whereupon the emperor's mind was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Dan and other guests in blowing the sheng and plucking the qin; Du Kui looked pained, and the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 後因他事系夔，使

translations.literal: Later on another matter he imprisoned Kui and had
translations.idiomatic: Later, on another pretext, he jailed Du Kui and sent

translations.literal: (Yuan)
translations.idiomatic: (Yuan)

sentences.zh: 等就學，夔自謂所習者雅，仕宦有本，意猶不滿，遂黜免以卒。

translations.literal: and others go study; Kui said what he practiced was elegant music, that office had its roots, yet his mind was still dissatisfied, and so he was dismissed and died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: others to study under him. Du Kui insisted that what he taught was orthodox ritual music with a proper pedigree, yet he remained bitter and was stripped of his post and died.

sentences.zh: 弟子河南邵登、張泰、桑馥，各至太樂丞，下邳陳頏司律中郎將。

translations.literal: His disciples Shao Deng of Henan, Zhang Tai, and Sang Fu each rose to Assistant Director of the Grand Music; Chen Hui of Xiapi became General of the Household in Charge of Pitch.
translations.idiomatic: His pupils Shao Deng, Zhang Tai, and Sang Fu of Henan each became assistant directors of the grand music; Chen Hui of Xiapi rose to general of the household for pitch.

sentences.zh: 自左延年等雖妙於音，咸善鄭聲，其好古存正莫及夔。

translations.literal: Although Zuo Yanian and others were subtle in music, they all favored Zheng tunes; none matched Kui in loving antiquity and preserving orthodoxy.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zuo Yanian were clever musicians, yet they favored the licentious Zheng airs; none rivaled Du Kui in reverence for the old orthodox style.

sentences.zh: 〈時有扶風馬鈞，巧思絕世。

translations.literal: 〈At that time there was Ma Jun of Fufeng, whose ingenuity was unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: 〈At the same time lived Ma Jun of Fufeng, whose inventiveness was unrivaled under heaven.

sentences.zh: 傅玄

translations.literal: Fu Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan

translations.literal: 〈Preface〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Preface〉

sentences.zh: 之曰：「馬先生，天下之名巧也，少而遊豫，不自知其為巧也。

translations.literal: says of him: "Master Ma is the most famous craftsman under heaven; in youth he roamed at ease and did not himself know he was clever.
translations.idiomatic: writes: "Master Ma is the foremost artisan of the realm; in his youth he wandered idly and scarcely knew his own gift.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，言不及巧，焉可以言知乎？

translations.literal: At such a time, speech did not touch on cleverness — how could one speak of knowing?"
translations.idiomatic: In those days no one spoke of ingenuity — how could he have known his worth?"

sentences.zh: 為博士居貧，乃思綾機之變，不言而世人知其巧矣。

translations.literal: Serving as erudite while poor, he then thought of changes to the damask loom; without speaking the world knew his cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Poor while holding an erudite's post, he redesigned the figured-silk loom; though he said nothing, the world saw his genius.

sentences.zh: 舊綾機五十綜者五十躡，六十綜者六十躡，先生患其喪功費日，乃皆易以十二躡。

translations.literal: Old damask looms with fifty heddles had fifty treadles, those with sixty heddles had sixty treadles; the master worried they wasted labor and time, and therefore replaced them all with twelve treadles.
translations.idiomatic: Older looms needed fifty treadles for fifty heddles, sixty for sixty; Ma Jun found the waste unbearable and replaced the whole rig with twelve treadles.

sentences.zh: 其奇文異變，因感而作者，猶自然之成形，陰陽之無窮，此輪扁之對不可以言言者，又焉可以言校也。

translations.literal: Their marvelous patterns and strange transformations, arising from stimulus and creation, were still like nature forming things or yin and yang without end — this is what Wheelwright Bian meant when he said it cannot be told in words — how then can it be matched in argument.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade's shifting patterns seemed to shape themselves like nature or the endless dance of yin and yang — the sort of thing Wheelwright Bian said words cannot capture — and mere debate cannot compass it.

sentences.zh: 先生為給事中，與常侍高堂隆、驍騎將軍秦朗爭論於朝，言及指南車，二子謂古無指南車，記言之虛也。

translations.literal: When the master was Palace Attendant, he disputed at court with Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Tang Long and General Who Rallies the Valiant Qin Lang; the talk turned to the south-pointing carriage; the two sons said antiquity had no south-pointing carriage, that the records were empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: As palace attendant he argued in court with Gao Tang Long and General Qin Lang about the south-pointing cart; the pair insisted the ancients never built one and that the histories lied.

sentences.zh: 先生曰：『古有之，未之思耳，夫何遠之有！

translations.literal: The master said: 'Antiquity had it; you have not thought it through — how far away can it be!'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun replied, 'The ancients had such a cart; you simply have not thought it through — the truth is not far to seek!'

sentences.zh: 』二子哂之曰：『先生名鈞字德衡，鈞者器之模，而衡者所以定物之輕重；

translations.literal: ' The two sons sneered: 'The master's name is Jun, style Deheng; jun means the model of a vessel, and heng is what fixes the weight of things —
translations.idiomatic: ' The pair mocked him: 'Your name is Jun and your style Deheng — a template for vessels and a balance for weight —

sentences.zh: 輕重無準而莫不模哉！

translations.literal: if weight has no standard, is there anything that is not a template!'
translations.idiomatic: yet without a true standard for weight, everything becomes a mere mold!'

sentences.zh: 』先生曰：『虛爭空言，不如試之易效也。

translations.literal: ' The master said: 'Empty quarrel in words is not as good as trying it — easy to show effect.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Ma Jun answered, 'Idle words prove nothing; build it and we shall see.'

sentences.zh: 』於是二子遂以白明帝，詔先生作之，而指南車成。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the two sons reported to Emperor Ming; an edict ordered the master to make it, and the south-pointing carriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: ' They carried the matter to Emperor Ming, who ordered Ma Jun to build the device, and the south-pointing cart was finished.

sentences.zh: 此一異也，又不可以言者也，從是天下服其巧矣。

translations.literal: This is one marvel, and again it cannot be captured in words; from this the realm acknowledged his cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: That was one wonder words cannot exhaust, and thereafter the empire conceded his genius.

sentences.zh: 居京都，城內有地，可以為園，患無水以灌之，乃作翻車，令童兒轉之，而灌水自覆，更入更出，其巧百倍於常。

translations.literal: Residing in the capital, he had land inside the walls that could serve as a garden, but worried there was no water to irrigate it; then he made a chain-pump, ordered boys to turn it, and irrigation water poured itself back and forth in and out — its cleverness a hundredfold beyond the usual.
translations.idiomatic: He owned a city plot he wished to turn into a garden but lacked water, so he devised a chain-pump turned by boys that lifted irrigation in an endless loop — a device scores of times cleverer than ordinary pumps.

sentences.zh: 此二異也。

translations.literal: This is the second marvel.
translations.idiomatic: That was the second marvel.

sentences.zh: 其後人有上百戲者，能設而不能動也。

translations.literal: Afterward someone presented a set of mechanical entertainments that could be set up but could not move.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone offered a set of mechanical stage tricks that could be assembled but not animated.

sentences.zh: 帝以問先生：『可動否？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the master: 'Can they move?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'Can you make them move?'

sentences.zh: 』對曰：『可動。

translations.literal: ' He answered: 'They can move.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Ma Jun said they could.

sentences.zh: 』帝曰：『其巧可益否？

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'Can their cleverness be increased?'
translations.idiomatic: ' The ruler asked whether the display could be made still more ingenious?'

sentences.zh: 』對曰：『可益。

translations.literal: ' He answered: 'It can be increased.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Ma Jun said it could.'

sentences.zh: 』受詔作之。

translations.literal: ' He received the edict and made them.
translations.idiomatic: ' He took the commission and built the mechanisms.'

sentences.zh: 以大木彫構，使其形若輪，平地施之，潛以水發焉。

translations.literal: He carved great timbers into a framework like a wheel, set it on level ground, and secretly powered it with water.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a great wheel, set it on flat ground, and drove it with hidden water power.

sentences.zh: 設為女樂舞象，至令木人擊鼓吹簫；

translations.literal: He arranged female musicians and dancing elephants, so that wooden figures beat drums and blew panpipes;
