translations.idiomatic: He set up female musicians and elephant dancers, with wooden automata beating drums and playing pipes;

sentences.zh: 作山岳，使木人跳丸擲劍，緣絙倒立，出入自在；

translations.literal: he made mountains and ranges, had wooden men juggle balls and throw swords, walk tightropes upside down, entering and exiting at will;
translations.idiomatic: he added miniature peaks where wooden figures juggled, tossed swords, walked ropes head-down, and moved at will;

sentences.zh: 百官行署，舂磨鬥雞，變巧百端。

translations.literal: officials walking offices, pestles grinding grain, cocks fighting — changes and tricks by the hundred.
translations.idiomatic: he showed miniature yamens, grinding mills, and cockfights — a hundred shifting tricks.

sentences.zh: 此三異也。

translations.literal: This is the third marvel.
translations.idiomatic: That was the third marvel.

sentences.zh: 先生見諸葛亮連弩，曰：『巧則巧矣，未盡善也。

translations.literal: The master saw Zhuge Liang's repeating crossbow and said: 'Clever indeed, yet not yet perfect.'
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhuge Liang's repeating crossbow, he said, 'Clever, but not yet perfect.'

sentences.zh: 』言作之可令加五倍。

translations.literal: ' He said if he made it, it could be increased fivefold.
translations.idiomatic: ' He claimed he could quintuple its rate of fire.'

sentences.zh: 又患發石車，敵人之於樓邊縣濕牛皮，中之則墮，石不能連屬而至。

translations.literal: He also worried about the stone-throwing cart — the enemy hung wet oxhides on the towers; when hit they fell off, and stones could not arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also faulted the stone-throwing engine: defenders hung wet hides on the towers so missiles slipped off and could not strike in volleys.

sentences.zh: 欲作一輪，縣大石數十，以機鼓輪為常，則以斷縣石飛擊敵城，使首尾電至。

translations.literal: He wished to make one wheel, hang several dozen large stones on it, use a mechanism to drum the wheel at a steady rate, then cut the ropes so the suspended stones flew to strike the enemy city, making head and tail arrive like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a wheel hung with dozens of boulders, kept spinning by machinery until the ropes were cut and the rocks flew against the walls in a lightning volley.

sentences.zh: 嘗試以車輪縣瓴甓數十，飛之數百步矣。

translations.literal: He once tested by hanging several dozen roof-tiles on a cart wheel and flung them several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: He once hung dozens of tiles on a wheel and hurled them hundreds of paces.

sentences.zh: 有裴子者，上國之士也，精通見理，聞而哂之。

translations.literal: There was Master Pei, a gentleman of the upper state, clear in principle, who heard this and sneered.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar named Pei, a man of the capital and a clear thinker, heard the boast and laughed.

sentences.zh: 乃難先生，先生口屈不對。

translations.literal: Then he challenged the master; the master's mouth was defeated and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He cross-examined Ma Jun until the inventor could not reply.

sentences.zh: 裴子自以為難得其要，言之不已。

translations.literal: Master Pei thought he had grasped the essentials and spoke without end.
translations.idiomatic: Pei thought he had won the argument and kept pressing.

sentences.zh: 傅子謂裴子曰：『子所長者言也，所短者巧也。

translations.literal: Master Fu said to Master Pei: 'What you excel at is words; what you lack is ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan told Pei, 'Your strength is debate; your weakness is mechanical wit.

sentences.zh: 馬氏所長者巧也，所短者言也。

translations.literal: What Master Ma excels at is ingenuity; what he lacks is words.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun's strength is ingenuity; his weakness is rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 以子所長，擊彼所短，則不得不屈。

translations.literal: With what you excel at, striking what he lacks, he cannot but be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Strike his weak point with your strong suit and he must fall silent.

sentences.zh: 以子所短，難彼所長，則必有所不解者矣。

translations.literal: With what you lack, challenging what he excels at, there must be things you do not understand.'
translations.idiomatic: Challenge his strength with your weakness and you will find much you cannot fathom.'

sentences.zh: 夫巧，天下之微事也，有所不解而難之不已，其相擊刺，必已遠矣。

translations.literal: Ingenuity is the subtlest affair under heaven; to keep challenging what you do not understand — the mutual thrusts must already be far apart.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmanship is the subtlest of skills; to harangue what you cannot grasp only widens the gulf between you.

sentences.zh: 心乖於內，口屈於外，此馬氏所以不對也。

translations.literal: The heart at odds inside, the mouth defeated outside — this is why Master Ma did not answer.'
translations.idiomatic: Heart and tongue pull apart — that is why Ma Jun fell silent.'

sentences.zh: 』傅子見安鄉侯，言及裴子之論，安鄉侯又與裴子同。

translations.literal: ' Master Fu saw the Marquis of Anxiang; speaking touched on Master Pei's discourse; the Marquis of Anxiang again agreed with Master Pei.
translations.idiomatic: ' When Fu Xuan spoke with the Marquis of Anxiang about Pei's attack, the marquis sided with Pei.

sentences.zh: 傅子曰：『聖人具體備物，取人不以一揆也：有以神取之者，有以言取之者，有以事取之者。

translations.literal: Master Fu said: 'The sage embodies all things complete; in taking men he does not use one measure: some are taken by spirit, some by words, some by deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan said, 'The sage judges men by many measures — spirit, speech, and deeds alike.

sentences.zh: 有以神取之者，不言而誠心先達，德行顏淵之倫是也。

translations.literal: Those taken by spirit — without speaking yet sincere mind first reaches — such are the class of Yan Hui in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Those chosen for spirit need no words — think of Yan Hui's moral grace.

sentences.zh: 以言取之者，以變辯是非，言語宰我、子貢是也。

translations.literal: Those taken by words — using changing debate to settle right and wrong — such are Zai Wo and Zigong in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Those chosen for eloquence are debaters like Zai Wo and Zigong.

sentences.zh: 以事取之者，若政事冉有、季路，文學子遊、子夏。

translations.literal: Those taken by deeds — such as Ran You and Ji Lu in government, Ziyou and Zixia in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Those chosen for deeds are administrators like Ran You and Ji Lu or scholars like Ziyou and Zixia.

sentences.zh: 雖聖人之明盡物，如有所用，必有所試，然則試冉、季以政，試遊、夏以學矣。

translations.literal: Although the sage's clarity exhausts things, if he would use someone he must test him — thus test Ran and Ji with government, test You and Xia with learning.'
translations.idiomatic: Even the sage tests men: try Ran and Ji in office, You and Xia in scholarship.'

sentences.zh: 遊、夏猶然，況自此而降者乎！

translations.literal: You and Xia are still thus — how much more those who rank below them!
translations.idiomatic: If even Ziyou and Zixia needed testing, what of lesser men!

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 懸言物理，不可以言盡也，施之於事，言之難盡而試之易知也。

translations.literal: Hanging speech on physical principles cannot exhaust them in words; applied to deeds, speech is hard to exhaust but trial is easy to know.
translations.idiomatic: Words cannot exhaust physical principles, but a trial settles the matter at once.

sentences.zh: 今若馬氏所欲作者，國之精器，軍之要用也。

translations.literal: Now what Master Ma wishes to make is the refined instrument of the state, the essential use of the army.
translations.idiomatic: What Ma Jun proposes are the state's precision tools and the army's vital engines.

sentences.zh: 費十尋之木，勞二人之力，不經時而是非定。

translations.literal: It costs ten xun of timber and the labor of two men; without passing much time right and wrong are settled.
translations.idiomatic: They cost a few beams and two workmen; in short order success or failure is plain.

sentences.zh: 難試易驗之事而輕以言抑人異能，此猶以己智任天下之事，不易其道以御難盡之物，此所以多廢也。

translations.literal: To slight easy-to-test matters and lightly use words to suppress another's unusual ability — this is still to use one's own wisdom to undertake all affairs under heaven, not to change one's way to control things that speech cannot exhaust — this is why much is wasted.
translations.idiomatic: To dismiss an easy experiment and silence rare talent with talk is to trust one's own wits for everything and refuse the trial that endless things demand — that is how great work is ruined.

sentences.zh: 馬氏所作，因變而得是，則初所言者不皆是矣。

translations.literal: What Master Ma makes, if through change one obtains the right, then what was first said was not all right.
translations.idiomatic: If Ma Jun's prototypes improve on the plan, the carping was wrong from the start.

sentences.zh: 其不皆是，因不用之，是不世之巧無由出也。

translations.literal: If it is not all right, and therefore not used, then unmatched cleverness of the age has no way to emerge.
translations.idiomatic: If naysayers block him because the first sketch was imperfect, a once-in-a-generation gift never reaches the world.

sentences.zh: 夫同情者相妒，同事者相害，中人所不能免也。

translations.literal: Those who share feelings envy one another; those who share office harm one another — this is what middling men cannot avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Kindred spirits envy one another; rivals in office wound one another — ordinary men cannot escape it.

sentences.zh: 故君子不以人害人，必以考試為衡石；

translations.literal: Therefore the noble man does not use men to harm men; he must use examination as the balance-stone;
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman never harms another's reputation without proof; he weighs claims with experiment;

sentences.zh: 廢衡石而不用，此美玉所以見誣為石，荊和所以抱璞而哭之也。

translations.literal: to discard the balance-stone and not use it — this is why fine jade is slandered as stone, and why Bian He hugged his jade and wept.'
translations.idiomatic: to throw away that balance is why flawless jade is called common stone and why Bian He wept clutching his uncut block.'

sentences.zh: 』於是安鄉侯悟，遂言之武安侯，武安侯忽之，不果試也。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the Marquis of Anxiang understood, then spoke to the Marquis of Wu'an; the Marquis of Wu'an dismissed it, and in the end it was not tried.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Marquis of Anxiang saw the point and spoke to the Marquis of Wu'an, who brushed the matter aside, so nothing was ever built.

sentences.zh: 此既易試之事，又馬氏巧名已定，猶忽而不察，況幽深之才，無名之璞乎？

translations.literal: This being an easy thing to test, and Master Ma's clever name already settled, yet he was neglected and not examined — how much more for talents hidden deep, unnamed jade?
translations.idiomatic: If a proven genius can be ignored for an easy test, what hope is there for hidden talent without fame?

sentences.zh: 後之君子其鑑之哉！

translations.literal: Later gentlemen, take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Let later ages take warning!

sentences.zh: 馬先生之巧，雖古公輸般、墨翟、王爾，近漢世張平子，不能過也。

translations.literal: Master Ma's cleverness — though ancient Gongshu Ban, Mozi, and Wang Er, or in recent Han times Zhang Heng, could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun's skill exceeded Gongshu Ban, Mozi, Wang Er of antiquity, or even Zhang Heng of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 公輸般、墨翟皆見用於時，乃有益於世。

translations.literal: Gongshu Ban and Mozi were both employed in their time, and then benefited the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshu Ban and Mozi served their courts to the world's profit.

sentences.zh: 平子雖為侍中，馬先生雖給事省中，俱不典工官，巧無益於世。

translations.literal: Although Zhang Heng was Palace Attendant and Master Ma was Palace Attendant in the ministry, neither presided over the office of works — their cleverness did not benefit the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng was a palace attendant and Ma Jun a ministry attendant, yet neither ran the directorate of works — so their genius never served the state.

sentences.zh: 用人不當其才，聞賢不試以事，良可恨也。

translations.literal: To employ men not according to their talent, to hear of the worthy and not test them with deeds — truly it is hateful.
translations.idiomatic: Misusing talent and refusing to test the worthy is a bitter shame.

sentences.zh: 」裴子者，裴秀。

translations.literal: " The Master Pei is Pei Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: "The 'Master Pei' was Pei Xiu.

sentences.zh: 安鄉侯者，曹羲。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Anxiang is Cao Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Anxiang was Cao Xi.

sentences.zh: 武安侯者，曹爽也。〉

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wu'an is Cao Shuang.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wu'an was Cao Shuang.〉

sentences.zh: 朱建平

translations.literal: Zhu Jianping
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jianping

sentences.zh: 朱建平，沛國人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Jianping was a man of the Pei state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jianping came from the kingdom of Pei.

sentences.zh: 善相術，於閭巷之間，效驗非一。

translations.literal: He was good at physiognomy; in lanes and alleys his verifications were not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced face-reading in the streets, and his predictions repeatedly came true.

sentences.zh: 太祖為魏公，聞之，召為郎。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became Duke of Wei, hearing of him, summoned him as Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ancestor became duke of Wei he heard of Zhu and appointed him a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 文帝為五官將，坐上會客三十餘人，文帝問己年壽，又令遍相眾賓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was General of the Five Offices, at a banquet with more than thirty guests, Wen asked his own lifespan in years and also ordered him to read every guest in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wen was general of the five offices he hosted thirty-odd guests, asked Zhu for his own span, and had him read each man in turn.

sentences.zh: 建平曰：「將軍當壽八十，至四十時當有小厄，願謹護之。

translations.literal: Jianping said: "The general ought to live eighty years; at forty there will be a small calamity; I pray you guard yourself carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said, "Your lordship should reach eighty, but at forty a minor crisis will strike; guard yourself well.

sentences.zh: 」謂夏侯威曰：「君四十九位為州牧，而當有厄，厄若得過，可年至七十，致位公輔。

translations.literal: " He said to Xiahou Wei: "At forty-nine you will attain the rank of regional governor, yet there will be a calamity; if the calamity passes, you can reach seventy years and rise to the rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: " To Xiahou Wei he said, 'At forty-nine you will become a regional inspector, but a crisis awaits; survive it and you may reach seventy as a chief minister.'

sentences.zh: 」謂應璩曰：「君六十二位為常伯，而當有厄，先此一年，當獨見一白狗，而旁人不見也。

translations.literal: " He said to Ying Qu: "At sixty-two you will attain the rank of Palace Attendant, yet there will be a calamity; one year before this you ought alone to see a white dog, while those beside you will not see it.
translations.idiomatic: " To Ying Qu he said, 'At sixty-two you will be a palace attendant, yet danger looms; the year before, you alone will glimpse a white dog others cannot see.'

sentences.zh: 」謂曹彪曰：「君據藩國，至五十七當厄於兵，宜善防之。」

translations.literal: " He said to Cao Biao: "You will hold a fief; at fifty-seven you will meet calamity from weapons; you ought well to guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: " To Cao Biao he said, 'You will rule a princedom; at fifty-seven war will threaten you — prepare for it.'"

sentences.zh: 初，潁川荀攸、鍾繇相與親善。

translations.literal: Originally Xun You of Yingchuan and Zhong Yao were mutually intimate and good.
translations.idiomatic: In former days Xun You of Yingchuan and Zhong Yao were close friends.

sentences.zh: 攸先亡，子幼。

translations.literal: You died first; the son was young.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You died first, leaving a young son.

sentences.zh: 繇經紀其門戶，欲嫁其妾。

translations.literal: Yao managed his household gates and wished to marry off his concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao handled Xun You's household and planned to give Xun's concubine a proper remarriage.

sentences.zh: 與人書曰：「吾與公達曾共使朱建平相，建平曰：『荀君雖少，然當以後事付鍾君。

translations.literal: In a letter to someone he said: "I and Gongda once together had Zhu Jianping physiognomize us; Jianping said: 'Though Lord Xun is young, yet you ought to entrust later affairs to Lord Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to an acquaintance: "Lord Xun and I once consulted Zhu Jianping together. Zhu said, 'Xun You is young, yet you should leave your final affairs in Zhong Yao's hands.'

sentences.zh: 』吾時啁之曰：『惟當嫁卿阿騖耳。

translations.literal: ' At the time I teased him saying: 'It would only be marrying off your Ah Wu.
translations.idiomatic: ' I joked, 'Then I need only marry off your girl Ah Wu.'

sentences.zh: 』何意此子竟早隕沒，戲言遂驗乎！

translations.literal: ' Who would have thought this child would early perish; the jesting words then came true!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Who imagined the boy would die so soon — and a jest would prove prophetic!'

sentences.zh: 今欲嫁阿騖，使得善處。

translations.literal: Now I wish to marry off Ah Wu, so that she obtains a good situation.
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to settle Ah Wu in a worthy household."

sentences.zh: 追思建平之妙，雖唐舉、許負何以復加也！」

translations.literal: Recalling Jianping's subtlety — even Tang Ju or Xu Fu, how could they add more!"
translations.idiomatic: Thinking back on Zhu Jianping's insight, not even Tang Ju or Xu Fu could have surpassed it!

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初七年，年四十，病困，謂左右曰：「建平所言八十，謂晝夜也，吾其決矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, Huangchu seventh year, age forty, ill in extremity, said to those around: "What Jianping spoke of as eighty means day and night; I suppose it is decided.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Huangchu, Wen-di lay ill at forty and told his attendants, "When Zhu Jianping said I would reach eighty, he meant each day paired with its night as a year — my span is sealed."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，果崩。

translations.literal: " In a moment, indeed he collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died."

sentences.zh: 夏侯威為兗州刺史，年四十九，十二月上旬得疾，念建平之言，自分必死，豫作遺令及送喪之備，咸使素辦。

translations.literal: Xiahou Wei as Inspector of Yanzhou, age forty-ninth, in the upper ten days of the twelfth month fell ill, remembered Jianping's words, reckoned himself sure to die, beforehand made final instructions and prepared for the funeral, all ordered in plain white.
translations.idiomatic: At forty-nine, while serving as Yanzhou inspector, he fell ill in early twelfth month, recalled Zhu's warning, assumed he would die, and had his testament and funeral goods readied in mourning white.

sentences.zh: 至下旬轉差，垂以平復。

translations.literal: By the lower ten days he turned better, nearly restored.
translations.idiomatic: Toward month's end he rallied and seemed out of danger.

sentences.zh: 三十日日昃，請紀綱大吏設酒，曰：「吾所苦漸平，明日雞鳴，年便五十，建平之戒，眞必過矣。

translations.literal: On the thirtieth day at sundown, he invited chief clerks and set wine, saying: "What I suffered gradually eases; tomorrow at cockcrow the year will reach fifty; Jianping's warning, truly must be passed.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirtieth he feasted his senior clerks at dusk, saying, "My pains are easing; at cockcrow tomorrow I turn fifty — I shall have passed Zhu's predicted crisis."

sentences.zh: 」威罷客之後，合瞑疾動，夜半遂卒。

translations.literal: " After Wei dismissed the guests, closing eyes illness stirred, at midnight then died.
translations.idiomatic: After the guests left he lay down; his sickness returned with violence, and he died before dawn."

sentences.zh: 璩六十一為侍中，直省內，欻見白狗，問之眾人，悉無見者。

translations.literal: Qu at sixty-one became Palace Attendant, attending within the palace, suddenly saw a white dog, asked the crowd, all had not seen it.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-one Ying Qu was palace attendant on duty in the inner compound when he alone saw a white dog; no one else did.

sentences.zh: 於是數聚會，並急遊觀田裡，飲宴自娛，過期一年，六十三卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon repeatedly gathered parties, together urgently roamed viewing fields, feasted and drank for amusement, passed the deadline one year, at sixty-three died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw feast after feast, raced about the countryside, drowned his cares in wine — a full year past the warned date — then died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 曹彪封楚王，年五十七，坐與王淩通謀，賜死。

translations.literal: Cao Biao enfeoffed King of Chu, age fifty-seven, sitting crime conspired with Wang Ling, was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cao Biao of Chu, aged fifty-seven, was condemned for plotting with Wang Ling and compelled to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 凡說此輩，無不如言，不能具詳，故粗記數事。

translations.literal: All who told this sort, none was not as spoken; unable to record in full detail, therefore roughly noted several matters.
translations.idiomatic: Every case of the kind I heard matched the prophecy; a full record is impossible, so I sketch only a few.

sentences.zh: 惟相司空王昶、征北將軍程喜、中領軍王肅有蹉跌云。

translations.literal: Only Minister of Works Wang Chang, General Who Conquers the North Cheng Xi, and Central Army Commander Wang Su are said to have stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: They say Wang Chang, Cheng Xi, and Wang Su alone missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 肅年六十二，疾篤，眾醫並以為不愈。

translations.literal: Su at age sixty-two, illness grave, all physicians together thought he would not recover.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-two Wang Su was near death, and every physician despaired.

sentences.zh: 肅夫人問以遺言，肅云：「建平相我踰七十，位至三公，今皆未也，將何慮乎！

translations.literal: Su's wife asked for final words; Su said: "Jianping physiognomized me as passing seventy, rank reaching the Three Dukes; now none yet are so; what is there to worry!
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked for a last testament. He said, "Zhu Jianping said I would pass seventy and rise to the three dukes — none of that has happened, so what cause have I to fret!"

sentences.zh: 」而肅竟卒。

translations.literal: " Yet Su in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: He died all the same."

sentences.zh: 建平又善相馬。

translations.literal: Jianping was also good at judging horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jianping was also a master judge of horse flesh.

sentences.zh: 文帝將出，取馬外入，建平道遇之，語曰：「此馬之相，今日死矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was about to go out, drew a horse from outside; Jianping met him on the way, said to him: "This horse's appearance, today will die.
translations.idiomatic: As Wen-di was leaving, grooms led in a mount Zhu met in the corridor and said, "This beast's marks foretell its death today."

sentences.zh: 」帝將乘馬，馬惡衣香，驚囓文帝膝，帝大怒，即便殺之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was about to mount; the horse hated the scent of clothes, startled and bit Emperor Wen's knee; the emperor greatly angry, immediately had it killed.
translations.idiomatic: The horse shied at perfume on the imperial robes, reared, and snapped at the emperor's knee; in a fury Wen-di had it slaughtered on the spot."

sentences.zh: 建平黃初中卒。

translations.literal: Jianping died in Huangchu.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Huangchu era.

sentences.zh: 周宣字孔和，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuan, courtesy name Konghe, man of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan, styled Konghe, came from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 為郡吏。

translations.literal: Became a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 太守楊沛夢人曰：「八月一日曹公當至，必與君杖，飲以藥酒。

translations.literal: Prefect Yang Pei dreamed someone said: "On the first day of the eighth month Lord Cao will arrive, and will surely give you a staff and make you drink medicinal wine.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yang Pei dreamed a voice declare, "On the first of the eighth month Lord Cao will come, beat you with a rod, and force you to drink drugged wine."

sentences.zh: 」使宣占之。

translations.literal: " Ordered Xuan to interpret it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhou Xuan to divine the dream."

sentences.zh: 是時黃巾賊起，宣對曰：「夫杖起弱者，藥治人病，八月一日，賊必除滅。

translations.literal: At that time Yellow Turban bandits rose; Xuan replied: "The staff aids the weak, medicine cures people's illness; on the first of the eighth month, the bandits will surely be destroyed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: With the Yellow Turbans rising, Zhou replied, "A staff helps the feeble, medicine cures the sick — on the first of the eighth the rebels will be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 」至期，賊果破。

translations.literal: " When the date came, the bandits were indeed broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, the bandits were crushed."

sentences.zh: 後東平劉楨夢蛇生四足，穴居門中，使宣占之，宣曰：「此為國夢，非君家之事也。

translations.literal: Later Pingdong Liu Zhen dreamed a snake grew four feet, dwelt in a hole in the gate, ordered Xuan to interpret; Xuan said: "This is a dream for the state, not your household's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen of Dongping dreamed a four-legged snake living in the gate-hole. Zhou said, "That portends the realm, not your private house."

sentences.zh: 當殺女子而作賊者。

translations.literal: It concerns women who will be killed while acting as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: It means woman-led brigands will be put to the sword."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，女賊鄭、姜遂俱夷討，以蛇女子之祥，足非蛇之所宜故也。

translations.literal: " In a while the woman bandits Zheng and Jiang were both exterminated, because snake is an omen of women, yet feet are not what snakes should have.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the female outlaws Zheng and Jiang were extirpated — the snake signified women, the extra feet marked the anomaly."

sentences.zh: 文帝問宣曰：「吾夢殿屋兩瓦墮地，化為雙鴛鴦，此何謂也？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen asked Xuan: "I dreamed two roof-tiles fell to the ground and turned into a pair of mandarin ducks — what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di asked, "Two tiles fell from my hall roof and became mandarin ducks — what is the portent?"

sentences.zh: 」宣對曰：「後宮當有暴死者。

translations.literal: " Xuan replied: "In the rear palace there ought to be someone who dies a violent death.
translations.idiomatic: "There will be a violent death among the palace women."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾詐卿耳！

translations.literal: " Emperor said: "I deceived you!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "I invented that dream!"

sentences.zh: 」宣對曰：「夫夢者意耳，苟以形言，便佔吉凶。

translations.literal: " Xuan replied: "Dreams are what the mind intends; if one speaks them in images, then one can divine good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou answered, "Dreams follow the mind's intent; once shaped in images, they yield auspice or bale regardless of invention."

sentences.zh: 」言未畢，而黃門令奏宮人相殺。

translations.literal: " Before the words finished, the Yellow Gate director reported palace women killed one another.
translations.idiomatic: He had hardly finished when the eunuch director reported infighting among the concubines."

sentences.zh: 無幾，帝復問曰：「我昨夜夢青氣自地屬天。

translations.literal: Not long after, the emperor again asked: "Last night I dreamed blue-green qi rose from earth to sky.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Wen-di asked again, "I dreamed a green vapor climbing from earth to heaven."

sentences.zh: 」宣對曰：「天下當有貴女子冤死。

translations.literal: " Xuan replied: "Under Heaven there will be a noble woman who dies unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: "A lady of high rank will die a wrongful death in the realm."

sentences.zh: 」是時，帝已遣使賜甄後璽書，聞宣言而悔之，遣人追使者不及。

translations.literal: " At that time the emperor had already sent an envoy to give Empress Zhen the edict-jade document; hearing Xuan's words he repented, sent men to pursue the envoy but could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: He had already dispatched an agent with the rescript that would force Lady Zhen to suicide; when he heard Zhou's gloss he regretted it, but couriers could not catch the first messenger."

sentences.zh: 帝復問曰：「吾夢摩錢文，欲令滅而更愈明，此何謂邪？

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "I dreamed I rubbed the coin inscription wishing to extinguish it yet it grew brighter — what means this?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "I rubbed the legend on a coin trying to wear it away, yet the characters shone clearer — what of that?"

sentences.zh: 」宣悵然不對。

translations.literal: " Xuan was frustrated and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou fell silent, unwilling to reply."

sentences.zh: 帝重問之，宣對曰：「此自陛下家事，雖意欲爾而太后不聽，是以文欲滅而明耳。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed again; Xuan replied: "This is Your Majesty's own household matter; although you wish it so, the Empress Dowager will not listen, therefore the inscription wished to fade yet grew bright.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again he said, "It is the affair of your own house: though you wish one thing, the empress dowager forbids it — the legend would vanish but obduracy keeps it bright."

sentences.zh: 」時帝欲治弟植之罪，偪於太后，但加貶爵。

translations.literal: " At that time the emperor wished to punish his brother Zhi's crime, pressed by the Empress Dowager, only degraded his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to punish Prince Zhi but the empress dowager blocked him, so he only degraded the prince's fief."

sentences.zh: 以宣為中郎，屬太史。

translations.literal: Appointed Xuan Gentleman of the Household, subordinate to the Grand Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhou Xuan a gentleman of the household and attached him to the grand astrologer.

sentences.zh: 嘗有問宣曰：「吾昨夜夢見芻狗，其占何也？

translations.literal: Someone once asked Xuan: "Last night I dreamed a straw dog; what is its omen?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked once, "I dreamed of a straw dog — what does it portend?"

sentences.zh: 」宣答曰：「君欲得美食耳！

translations.literal: " Xuan answered: "You are about to obtain fine food!
translations.idiomatic: "You are in for a splendid meal!"

sentences.zh: 」有頃，出行，果遇豐膳。

translations.literal: " After a while he went out traveling and indeed met a rich feast.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he went abroad and stumbled on a lavish banquet."

sentences.zh: 後又問宣曰：「昨夜復夢見芻狗，何也？

translations.literal: Later again asked Xuan: "Last night again I dreamed a straw dog; what of it?
translations.idiomatic: He returned: "I dreamed the straw dog again last night — why?"

sentences.zh: 」宣曰：「君欲墮車折腳，宜戒慎之。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "You are about to fall from a carriage and break your foot; ought to guard carefully.
translations.idiomatic: "You will tumble from a cart and break a leg — take care."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，果如宣言。

translations.literal: " In a while it was indeed as Xuan declared.
translations.idiomatic: It happened exactly as Zhou said."

sentences.zh: 後又問宣：「昨夜復夢見芻狗，何也？

translations.literal: Later again asked Xuan: "Last night again I dreamed a straw dog; what of it?
translations.idiomatic: Again he pressed Zhou: "The straw dog again — what now?"

sentences.zh: 」宣曰：「君家失火，當善護之。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "Your household will lose fire; ought to guard it well.
translations.idiomatic: "Fire will threaten your house — watch your hearths."

sentences.zh: 」俄遂火起。

translations.literal: " Soon thereafter fire indeed rose.
translations.idiomatic: A blaze broke out almost at once."

sentences.zh: 語宣曰：「前後三時，皆不夢也。

translations.literal: He told Xuan: "The three times before, I did not dream at all.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed to Zhou, "Those three dreams I feigned — I never slept to them."

sentences.zh: 聊試君耳，何以皆驗邪？

translations.literal: Merely tested you; how could they all be verified?
translations.idiomatic: "I was testing you — how could every fiction prove true?"

sentences.zh: 」宣對曰：「此神靈動君使言，故與眞夢無異也。

translations.literal: " Xuan replied: "Spirit and numen moved you to speak; therefore it is no different from a true dream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "Spirits moved your tongue; lies told under such prompting count as true dreams."

sentences.zh: 」又問宣曰：「三夢芻狗而其占不同，何也？

translations.literal: Again asked Xuan: "Three times dreaming straw dog yet their divinations differed — why?
translations.idiomatic: "Three straw dogs, three different readings — how is that possible?"

sentences.zh: 」宣曰：「芻狗者，祭神之物。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "Straw dog is the thing used in sacrificing to gods.
translations.idiomatic: "A straw dog is sacrificial gear offered to the gods."

sentences.zh: 故君始夢，當得餘食也。

translations.literal: Therefore your first dream, you ought to obtain leftover food.
translations.idiomatic: Your first dream meant you would eat ritual leftovers — the priests' leavings."

sentences.zh: 祭祀既訖，則芻狗為車所轢，故中夢當墮車折腳也。

translations.literal: Sacrifice already finished, then the straw dog is crushed by carts; therefore the middle dream meant you would fall from cart and break foot.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites the dog is trampled under chariot wheels — hence the second dream foretold your broken leg."

sentences.zh: 芻狗既車轢之後，必載以為樵，故後夢憂失火也。

translations.literal: After the straw dog has been crushed by carts, it must be loaded as firewood; therefore the later dream worried of losing fire.
translations.idiomatic: Once trampled, the effigy becomes fuel — hence the third dream warned of fire."

sentences.zh: 」宣之敘夢，凡此類也。

translations.literal: " Xuan's recounting of dreams was all of such kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan's oneiric glosses ran to this pattern."

sentences.zh: 十中八九，世以比建平之相矣。

translations.literal: Nine or ten hits in ten, the age compared him to Jianping's physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: He was right eight or nine times in ten, and men ranked him with Zhu Jianping's face-reading."

sentences.zh: 其餘效故不次列。

translations.literal: The rest of his verifications for that reason are not listed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Further hits are too many to list seriatim."

sentences.zh: 明帝末卒。

translations.literal: Died at the end of Emperor Ming's reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the close of Ming-di's reign.

sentences.zh: 管輅字公明，平原人也。

translations.literal: Guan Lu, courtesy name Gongming, man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu, styled Gongming, hailed from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 容貌粗醜，無威儀而嗜酒，飲食言戲，不擇非類，故人多愛之而不敬也。

translations.literal: His appearance was coarse and ugly, lacked dignified bearing yet loved wine; eating, drinking, speech and jest did not pick proper company; therefore people mostly loved him but did not respect him.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain, slovenly, and fond of wine, bantering with high and low without discrimination — men liked him but seldom honored him.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅年八九歲，便喜仰視星辰，得人輒問其名，夜不肯寐。

translations.literal: Separate biography of Lu says: Lu at age eight or nine then liked to look up at the stars; meeting people asked their names; at night would not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: His separate biography records that at eight or nine he loved to watch the stars, demanded every stranger's name, and refused sleep at night.

sentences.zh: 父母常禁之，猶不可止。

translations.literal: Parents constantly forbade him, still could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: His parents forbade him in vain.

sentences.zh: 自言「我年雖小，然眼中喜視天文。

translations.literal: He said himself: "Though my years are small, yet in my eyes I delight to view astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: "I am young," he said, "but my gaze is already fixed on the sky."

sentences.zh: 」常云：「家雞野鵠，猶尚知時，況於人乎？

translations.literal: " Often said: "House chicken and wild swan, still know the hour — how much more man?
translations.idiomatic: "Domestic fowl and wild geese keep the hours — should not men do better?"

sentences.zh: 」與鄰比兒共戲土壤中，輒畫地作天文及日月星辰。

translations.literal: " With neighborhood boys playing in the soil, always drew on the ground astronomy and sun moon stars.
translations.idiomatic: With village playmates he scratched constellations, sun, moon, and stars in the dust."

sentences.zh: 每答言說事，語皆不常，宿學耆人不能折之，皆知其當有大異之才。

translations.literal: Whenever he answered and spoke of matters, his words were all uncommon; long-studied elders could not refute him, all knew he would certainly have a greatly unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke, even seasoned scholars could not trip him up; everyone sensed a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 及成人，果明周易，仰觀、風角、佔、相之道，無不精微。

translations.literal: When grown to man, indeed he understood the Zhou Changes, the way of looking up, wind-horns, divination and physiognomy — none was not subtle and refined.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered the Zhou yi, astrology, wind-angles, tortoise oracle, and physiognomy with equal finesse.

sentences.zh: 體性寬大，多所含受；

translations.literal: His nature broad and large, much contained and received;
translations.idiomatic: He was tolerant and slow to take offense;

sentences.zh: 憎己不讎，愛己不褒，每欲以德報怨。

translations.literal: hating himself did not bear grudge, loving himself did not praise; often wished to repay injury with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he nursed no vendetta against critics nor flattery for admirers, preferring to return injury with kindness.

sentences.zh: 常謂：「忠孝信義，人之根本，不可不厚；

translations.literal: He often said: "Loyalty, filial piety, trust, righteousness — these are man's root; they cannot but be thick;
translations.idiomatic: "Loyalty, filial duty, trust, and right are the taproot of character and must be cultivated deep,"

sentences.zh: 廉介細直，士之浮飾，不足為務也。

translations.literal: incorrupt stubborn punctilious straightness is the gentleman's superficial adornment, not worth making one's task."
translations.idiomatic: petty frugal rigidity is tinsel on the gentleman — not worth pursuing."

sentences.zh: 」自言：「知我者稀，則我貴矣，安能斷江、漢之流，為激石之清？

translations.literal: " Said himself: "Those who know me are few, then I am noble; how could I cut off the Yangzi and Han flows to make rapids over stones clear?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Few understand me — that is my distinction. Am I to dam the Han and Yangzi into Alpine torrents?"

sentences.zh: 樂與季主論道，不欲與漁父同舟，此吾志也。

translations.literal: I delight to discuss the Way with Jizhu, I do not wish to share a boat with the Fisher — this is my aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: I would argue metaphysics with Sima Jizhu rather than drift downstream with the recluse — that is my bent."

sentences.zh: 」其事父母孝，篤兄弟，順愛士友，皆仁和發中，終無所闕。

translations.literal: " In serving parents he was filial, solid with brothers, compliant and loving to scholar friends — all humane kindness issuing from within, in the end without lack.
translations.idiomatic: He honored parents, cherished brothers, and was gentle to friends — kindness welled from within without stint."

sentences.zh: 臧否之士，晚亦服焉。

translations.literal: Critic-praise gentlemen, in the end also submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Even carping scholars saluted him in his later years.

sentences.zh: 父為琅邪即丘長，時年十五，來至官舍讀書。

translations.literal: Father was Magistrate of Jiju in Langya; at that time age fifteen, came to the government residence to read books.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was magistrate at Jiju in Langya, fifteen-year-old Guan Lu came to the yamen to study.

sentences.zh: 始讀詩、論語及易本，便開淵布筆，辭義斐然。

translations.literal: Beginning to read the Odes, Analects, and the basic Changes, then opened deep and spread brush; diction and meaning were splendid.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Shijing, Analects, and primer Zhou yi and wrote essays already lucid and graceful.

sentences.zh: 於時黌上有遠方及國內諸生四百餘人，皆服其才也。

translations.literal: At that time in the school hall were more than four hundred students from distant regions and within the state; all submitted to his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Over four hundred students in the academy bowed to his precocity.

sentences.zh: 琅邪太守單子春雅有材度，聞輅一黌之俊，欲得見，輅父即遣輅造之。

translations.literal: Langya Administrator Shan Zichun had refined capacity and bearing, hearing Lu was the school's outstanding talent, wished to meet him; Lu's father immediately sent Lu to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shan Zichun of Langya, a man of parts, heard of the school's star pupil and summoned him; Guan Lu's father sent the boy to call.

sentences.zh: 大會賓客百餘人，坐上有能言之士，輅問子春：「府君名士，加有雄貴之姿，輅既年少，膽未堅剛，若欲相觀，懼失精神，請先飲三升清酒，然後言之。

translations.literal: Grand gathering of more than a hundred guests; on the seat were articulate gentlemen; Lu asked Zichun: "My lord is a famous gentleman, moreover possessing heroic noble bearing; Lu is still young, courage not yet firm and strong; if you wish to observe me, I fear losing spirit — please first drink three sheng of clear wine, then speak.
translations.idiomatic: He received Lu at a banquet of a hundred guests. The boy said, "You are a famous magistrate of heroic mien, while I am still green and easily rattled. If you mean to examine me, give me three measures of wine first — then I can speak without losing my composure."

sentences.zh: 」子春大喜，便酌三升清酒，獨使飲之。

translations.literal: " Zichun greatly pleased, then poured three sheng clear wine, alone made him drink it.
translations.idiomatic: Shan delightedly poured three cups and made him drain them alone."

sentences.zh: 酒盡之後，問子春：「今欲與輅為對者，若府君四坐之士邪？

translations.literal: " After wine finished, asked Zichun: "Now if you wish to contend with Lu as opponent, is it the gentlemen seated throughout the hall?
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was gone he asked, "Shall I debate everyone in your hall, or only you, my lord?"

sentences.zh: 」子春曰：「吾欲自與卿旗鼓相當。

translations.literal: " Zichun said: "I wish myself with you to match spear and shield evenly.
translations.idiomatic: Shan replied, "I will face you myself on equal terms."

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「始讀詩、論、易本，學問微淺，未能上引聖人之道，陳秦、漢之事，但欲論金木水火土鬼神之情耳。

translations.literal: " Lu said: "I have begun to read the Odes, Analects, and basic Changes; learning is still shallow and thin, unable to ascend to cite the sages' Way or array Qin and Han affairs — I only wish to discuss metal, wood, water, fire, earth, ghosts and spirits' circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "I have touched only the Shijing, Lunyu, and primer Yi; I cannot yet expound the sages' full doctrine or rehearse Qin and Han history — I can merely discourse on the five phases and the nature of ghosts and spirits."

sentences.zh: 」子春言；

translations.literal: " Zichun spoke:
translations.idiomatic: Shan Zichun took the floor and said,

sentences.zh: 「此最難者，而卿以為易邪？

translations.literal: "This is the hardest thing; yet you think it easy?
translations.idiomatic: That is the subtlest topic, and you treat it lightly?"

sentences.zh: 」於是唱大論之端，遂經於陰陽，文采葩流，枝葉橫生，少引聖籍，多發天然。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sang the beginning of a great disquisition, then threaded through yin and yang, literary color blossoming and flowing, branches and leaves sprawling horizontally, little citing sage texts, much issuing from nature.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he launched a brilliant disquisition that ranged through yin and yang, sparkled with figures, sparsely cited classics, and sprang from spontaneous wit."

sentences.zh: 子春及眾士互共攻劫，論難鋒起，而輅人人答對，言皆有餘。

translations.literal: Zichun and the host of gentlemen together attacked and pressed; disputing points rose sharp as spear points, yet Lu to each person answered, and words all had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Shan and his guests pressed him from every side; Guan Lu rejoined each thrust with ease.

sentences.zh: 至日向暮，酒食不行。

translations.literal: When the day turned toward evening, wine and food did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk fell and the feast stalled unfinished.

sentences.zh: 子春語眾人曰：「此年少盛有才器，聽其言論，正似司馬犬子遊獵之賦，何其磊落雄壯，英神以茂，必能明天文地理變化之數，不徒有言也。

translations.literal: Zichun told the crowd: "This youth in his prime has great talent and capacity; hearing his discourse, it is just like Sima Xiangru's hunting rhapsody — how lofty and heroic, spirit and brilliance lush — he must be able to clarify astronomy, geography, and the numbers of change; not merely having words.
translations.idiomatic: Shan told the guests, "This boy is a marvel: listening to him is like hearing Sima Xiangru's hunting ode — bold, ample, luminous. He will read heaven and earth, yin and yang, and more than mere words."

sentences.zh: 」於是發聲徐州，號之神童。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon his name sounded in Xu province, styled divine child.
translations.idiomatic: From that hour his name rang through Xu province as the "divine lad.""

sentences.zh: 父為利漕，利漕民郭恩兄弟三人，皆得躄疾，使輅筮其所由。

translations.literal: Father was magistrate of Licao; the Licao commoner Guo En's three brothers all obtained lame illness; had Lu divine the cause.
translations.idiomatic: His father governed Licao, where the brothers Guo En all fell lame; they asked Guan Lu to cast yarrow for the cause.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「卦中有君本墓，墓中有女鬼，非君伯母，當叔母也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "In the hexagram there is your family's old tomb; in the tomb is a female ghost — not your elder uncle's wife, then it ought to be your younger uncle's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "The lines show your ancestral grave haunted by a woman — either your uncle's widow or your aunt by marriage.

sentences.zh: 昔飢荒之世，當有利其數升米者，排著井中，嘖嘖有聲，推一大石，下破其頭，孤魂冤痛，自訴於天。

translations.literal: In a past age of famine, someone must have coveted her few sheng of rice, pushed her into the well — tsik-tsik there was sound — pushed a great stone, below broke her head; lone soul wronged and pained, herself complained to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year someone robbed her of a few measures of grain, shoved her into a well with a grinding noise, then dropped a boulder that crushed her skull; her lonely ghost appealed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」於是恩涕泣服罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon En wept tears and acknowledged guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Guo En wept and confessed.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：利漕民郭恩，字義博，有才學，善周易、春秋，又能仰觀。

translations.literal: Separate biography of Lu says: Licao commoner Guo En, courtesy name Yibo, had talent and learning, was good at Zhou Changes and Spring and Autumn, also could look up at the stars.
translations.idiomatic: The separate biography adds that Guo En, styled Yibo, was a scholar of the Yi and Chunqiu and practiced astrology.

sentences.zh: 輅就義博讀易，數十日中，意便開發，言難逾師。

translations.literal: Lu went to Yibo to read Changes; within several tens of days, meaning then opened and developed; words of difficulty exceeded the teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu studied the Yi under him; within weeks his insight outstripped his teacher's.

sentences.zh: 於此分蓍下卦，用思精妙，佔黌上諸生疾病死亡貧富喪衰，初無差錯，莫不驚怪，謂之神人也。

translations.literal: Here dividing yarrow and casting hexagrams, using thought subtle and refined, divining the school's many students' illness, death, poverty, wealth, mourning, decline — at first without error; none was not startled and amazed, calling him divine man.
translations.idiomatic: He split milfoil for the academy students and foretold sickness, death, and fortune without a miss; everyone called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 又從義博學仰觀，三十日中通夜不臥，語義博：「君但相語墟落處所耳，至於推運會，論災異，自當出吾天分。

translations.literal: Also from Yibo learned looking up; thirty days through the night without sleeping, told Yibo: "You only need tell me the locations of ruins and hamlets; as for pushing fate's revolutions, discussing disasters and prodigies, that will come out of my natural allotment.
translations.idiomatic: He studied star lore thirty sleepless nights and told Guo En, "Teach me only the lay of ruins and villages — cosmic cycles and omens I shall read by native gift.

sentences.zh: 」學未一年，義博反從輅問易及天文事要。

translations.literal: " Learning not yet one year, Yibo in turn from Lu asked about Changes and astronomy's essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Guo En was asking Guan Lu for the marrow of Yi and sky lore.

sentences.zh: 義博每聽輅語，未嘗不推幾慷慨。

translations.literal: Yibo every time heard Lu's words, never did not push the table and sigh with generous ardor.
translations.idiomatic: Every lecture left Guo En pounding the table in excitement.

sentences.zh: 自言「登聞君至論之時，忘我篤疾，明闇之不相逮，何其遠也」！

translations.literal: Said himself: "When ascending to hear your supreme discourse, I forget my severe illness — how far apart bright and dark that do not reach!
translations.idiomatic: He cried, "When I hear you speak I forget my crippling pain — what a gulf between your light and my darkness!"

sentences.zh: 義博設主人，獨請輅，具告辛苦，自說：「兄弟三人俱得躄疾，不知何故？

translations.literal: Yibo set up as host, alone invited Lu, fully told hardship and toil, himself said: "We three brothers all obtained lame illness — do not know what cause?
translations.idiomatic: Hosting Guan Lu alone, he poured out his family's trouble: all three brothers lame — why?

sentences.zh: 試相為作卦，知其所由。

translations.literal: Try for me make hexagram, know its cause.
translations.idiomatic: Please cast the stalks and find the reason.

sentences.zh: 若有咎殃者，天道赦人，當為吾祈福於神明，勿有所愛。

translations.literal: If there is guilt and calamity, Heaven's way pardons men; ought for me pray blessing to the spirits and gods, not sparing anything.
translations.idiomatic: If we have sinned, Heaven forgives those who atone — I will offer anything to the spirits for relief.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱行，此為更生。

translations.literal: Brothers all walking — this is again living.
translations.idiomatic: If we brothers can walk again, it will be a new life for us."

sentences.zh: 」輅便作卦，思之未詳。

translations.literal: " Lu then made hexagram, pondered it not yet in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu cast the hexagram but hesitated over the reading.

sentences.zh: 會日夕，因留宿，至中夜，語義博曰：「吾以此得之。

translations.literal: It happened to be evening, therefore stayed overnight; reaching midnight, told Yibo: "I by this obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed till midnight, then said, "I have it now.

sentences.zh: 」既言其事，義博悲涕沾衣，曰：「皇漢之末，實有斯事。

translations.literal: " Having spoken the matter, Yibo sad tears soaked robe, said: "At the end of august Han, indeed there was this affair.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke, Guo En sobbed, "Late Han saw exactly such a crime.

sentences.zh: 君不名主，諱也。

translations.literal: You did not name the master — taboo.
translations.idiomatic: You spared the culprit — tact.

sentences.zh: 我不得言，禮也。

translations.literal: I could not speak — ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I may not speak — decency.

sentences.zh: 兄弟躄來三十餘載，腳如棘子，不可復治，但原不及子孫耳。

translations.literal: Brothers lame coming thirty-odd years, feet like thorns, cannot again be cured, only pray it does not reach descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years our legs have been like briars beyond cure; I only hope the curse stops with us.

sentences.zh: 」輅言火形不絕，水形無餘，不及後也。〉

translations.literal: " Lu said fire form not cut off, water form without remainder, does not reach later generations.〉
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said the fire line is unbroken, the water line ends — the harm will not pass to your children.〉

sentences.zh: 廣平劉奉林婦病困，已買棺器。

translations.literal: Guangping Liu Fenglin's wife ill in extremity, already bought coffin and gear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fenglin of Guangping bought a coffin for his dying wife.

sentences.zh: 時正月也，使輅佔，曰：「命在八月辛卯日日中之時。

translations.literal: It was first month; had Lu divine; said: "Life ends on the xinmao day of the eighth month at noon.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month he asked Guan Lu, who said she would die at noon on xinmao in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 」林謂必不然，而婦漸差，至秋發動，一如輅言。

translations.literal: " Lin said it surely would not be so, yet the woman gradually improved; reaching autumn the illness stirred, exactly as Lu said.
translations.idiomatic: Liu doubted it, she rallied, then in autumn relapsed and died on the day named.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：鮑子春為列人令，有明思才理，與輅相見，曰：「聞君為劉奉林卜婦死亡日，何其詳妙，試為論其意義。

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Bao Zichun was magistrate of Lieren, had clear thought and talent in principle, met Lu and said: "I heard you for Liu Fenglin divined his wife's death day — how detailed and subtle; try to explain its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zichun of Lieren asked Guan Lu to unpack that prediction.

sentences.zh: 」輅論爻象之旨，說變化之義，若規圓矩方，無不合也。

translations.literal: " Lu discussed the hexagram lines' aim, explained change and transformation's meaning; like compass round and square rule square, none did not fit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu explained the moving lines with compass-true logic.

sentences.zh: 子春自言：「吾少好譚易，又喜分蓍，可謂盲者欲視白黑，聾者欲聽清濁，苦而無功也。

translations.literal: Zichun said himself: "I in youth loved discussing Changes, also liked dividing yarrow — it may be called a blind man wishing to see black and white, a deaf man wishing to hear clear and muddy — bitter yet without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bao confessed he had wasted years on the Yi like a blind man chasing color.

sentences.zh: 聽君語後，自視體中，真為憒憒者也。」〉

translations.literal: After hearing your words, viewing inside my body, truly it is muddled."〉
translations.idiomatic: After your lecture I see only confusion within myself."〉

sentences.zh: 輅往見安平太守王基，基令作卦，輅曰：「當有賤婦人，生一男兒，墮地便走入灶中死。

translations.literal: Lu went to see Anping Administrator Wang Ji; Ji ordered him make hexagram; Lu said: "There ought to be a low-born woman who bears one male child; falling to earth then runs into the stove and dies.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu visited Prefect Wang Ji and foretold a base-born woman bearing a boy who would crawl into the kitchen hearth and die.

sentences.zh: 又床上當有一大蛇銜筆，小大共視，須臾去之也。

translations.literal: Also on the bed ought to be one great snake holding a brush; small and great together viewing; in a moment it will depart.
translations.idiomatic: A great snake will coil on the bed with a brush in its jaws while the household watches; then it will vanish.

sentences.zh: 又烏來入室中，與燕共鬥，燕死，烏去。

translations.literal: Also a crow will enter the chamber and fight with the swallow; the swallow dies, the crow departs.
translations.idiomatic: A crow will fight the chamber swallow to the swallow's death, then fly away.

sentences.zh: 有此三怪。

translations.literal: There are these three marvels.
translations.idiomatic: You will see these three prodigies.

sentences.zh: 」基大驚，問其吉凶。

translations.literal: " Ji greatly startled, asked their good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji asked whether they boded good or ill.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「直客舍久遠，魑魅魍魎為怪耳。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Straight — the guest quarters long unused; chimei wangliang make marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said they were sprites haunting an old lodging, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 兒生便走，非能自走，直宋無忌之妖將其入灶也。

translations.literal: The child born then runs — not able itself to run; straight — Song Wuji's demon carried it into the stove.
translations.idiomatic: The infant did not walk of its own; the hearth-spirit Song Wuji dragged it in.

sentences.zh: 大蛇銜筆，直老書佐耳。

translations.literal: The great snake holding brush — straight — an old clerk assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The snake with the brush was an old clerk's ghost.

sentences.zh: 烏與燕鬥，直老鈴下耳。

translations.literal: The crow fighting swallow — straight — an old bell-ringer.
translations.idiomatic: The crow and swallow were old retainers taking animal form.

sentences.zh: 今卦中見象而不見其凶，知非妖咎之徵，自無所憂也。

translations.literal: Now in the hexagram one sees images but does not see their bale; knowing it is not an omen of demon calamity, naturally there is nothing to worry.
translations.idiomatic: The hexagrams show images, not disaster — you need not fear.

sentences.zh: 」後卒無患。

translations.literal: " Later in the end without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: None of the omens brought harm.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：基與輅共論易，數日中，大以為喜樂，語輅言：「俱相聞善卜，定共清論。

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Ji with Lu together discussed Changes; within several days greatly took joy; told Lu: "We have heard each other good at divination; ought together have pure discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji studied the Yi with Guan Lu for days and urged a joint symposium.

sentences.zh: 君一時異才，當上竹帛也。

translations.literal: You are a singular talent of the age; ought ascend bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: You are a rare genius who should win a place in the histories.

sentences.zh: 」輅為基出卦，知其無咎，因謂基曰：「昔高宗之鼎，非雉所鴝，殷之階庭，非木所生，而野鳥一鴝，武丁為高宗，桑谷暫生，太戊以興焉。

translations.literal: " Lu for Ji produced hexagram, knew it had no fault, therefore told Ji: "Formerly at Gaozong's cauldron it was not pheasants that crowed; Yin dynasty's courtyard steps, it was not trees that grew — yet wild birds one crow, Wu Ding became Gaozong; mulberry and grain briefly sprang, Taiwu thereby rose.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu cast for him and said, "Strange birds and mulberry omens troubled Shang kings yet brought sage rule — three odd signs need not frighten you if you cultivate virtue.

sentences.zh: 知三事不為吉祥，原府君安身養德，從容光大，勿以知神姦汙累天真。」〉

translations.literal: Knowing the three matters are not auspicious signs, I pray my lord settle body and nurture virtue, at ease enlarge your radiance, do not let knowledge of spirit treachery stain pure truth."〉
translations.idiomatic: Take these marvels as Heaven's nudge to deepen your virtue, not as filth upon your nature."〉

sentences.zh: 時信都令家婦女驚恐，更互疾病，使輅筮之。

translations.literal: At that time the Xindu magistrate's household womenfolk were frightened and alarmed, alternately fell ill; had Lu divine.
translations.idiomatic: Women in the Xindu magistrate's house fell sick in turns; Guan Lu was summoned.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「君北堂西頭，有兩死男子，一男持矛，一男持弓箭，頭在壁內，腳在壁外。

translations.literal: Lu said: "At the north hall west end are two dead men — one male holds a spear, one male holds bow and arrows; heads inside the wall, feet outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He said two corpses lay under the north hall's west wall — one with a spear, one with a bow — heads inward, feet outward.

sentences.zh: 持矛者主刺頭，故頭重痛不得舉也。

translations.literal: The spear-holder governs stabbing heads; therefore head heavy pain cannot be raised.
translations.idiomatic: The spearman causes splitting headaches.

sentences.zh: 持弓箭者主射肫腹，故心中縣痛不得飲食也。

translations.literal: The bow-and-arrow holder governs shooting the belly and flanks; therefore heart inside suspended pain cannot eat or drink.
translations.idiomatic: The archer causes gnawing pain in the gut that blocks eating.

sentences.zh: 晝則浮游，夜來病人，故使驚恐也。

translations.literal: By day they float and roam; by night they come sickening people; therefore they cause fright and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: They roam by day and torment the women at night.

sentences.zh: 」於是掘徙骸骨，家中皆愈。

translations.literal: " Thereupon dug and moved the bones; all in the household were cured.
translations.idiomatic: The bones were dug up and reburied; the household recovered.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：王基即遣信都令遷掘其室中，入地八尺，果得二棺，一棺中有矛，一棺中有角弓及箭，箭久遠，木皆消爛，但有鐵及角完耳。

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Wang Ji immediately sent Xindu magistrate to move dig in his chamber; entering earth eight chi, indeed obtained two coffins — one coffin inside had a spear, one coffin inside had horn bow and arrows; the arrows long old, wood all rotted away, only iron and horn remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji had the site excavated eight chi down; two coffins held a spear and a horn bow with iron heads still sound.

sentences.zh: 及徙骸骨，去城一十里埋之，無復疾病。

translations.literal: When moved the bones, buried them ten li from the city; no more illness.
translations.idiomatic: Reburial ten li outside the city ended the sickness.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「吾少好讀易，玩之以久，不謂神明之數，其妙如此。

translations.literal: Ji said: "I in youth loved reading Changes, played with it long — did not think the numinous numbers' subtlety reached thus.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji marveled that the Book's numbers could be so subtle.

sentences.zh: 」便從輅學易，推論天文。

translations.literal: " Then followed Lu learning Changes, pushed and discussed astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Yi and stars under Guan Lu thereafter.

sentences.zh: 輅每開變化之象，演吉凶之兆，未嘗不纖微委曲，盡其精神。

translations.literal: Lu every time opened images of change, unfolded omens of good and ill, never did not fine and detailed exhaust his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu's readings were always minute and exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「始聞君言，如何可得，終以皆亂，此自天授，非人力也。

translations.literal: Ji said: "At first hearing your words, how could one obtain them; in the end all was confusion — this is Heaven's grant, not human power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said at first the doctrine seemed impossible, then all‑consuming — clearly heaven-sent, not human craft.

sentences.zh: 」於是藏周易，絕思慮，不復學卜筮之事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon stored away Zhou Changes, cut off thought and pondering, no longer studied divination matters.
translations.idiomatic: He shelved the classic and gave up casting stalks himself.

sentences.zh: 輅鄉里乃太原問輅：「君往者為王府君論怪，云老書佐為蛇，老鈴下為烏，此本皆人，何化之微賤乎？

translations.literal: Lu's fellow townsman Nai Taiyuan asked Lu: "Formerly you for Lord Wang discussed marvels, saying old clerk became snake, old bell-ringer became crow — these originally were men; why transform to such base things?
translations.idiomatic: A townsman asked why lowly snakes and crows stood for human clerks?

sentences.zh: 為見於爻象，出君意乎？

translations.literal: Was it appearing in hexagram images, issuing from your mind?
translations.idiomatic: Did the images force that reading or did you invent it?

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「苟非性與天道，何由背爻象而任胸心者乎？

translations.literal: " Lu said: "If not nature and Heaven's Way, how could one turn back on hexagram images and trust chest and heart?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu replied, "Without the Dao of heaven and nature, who could ignore the lines and invent freely?

sentences.zh: 夫萬物之化，無有常形，人之變異，無有常體，或大為小，或小為大，固無優劣。

translations.literal: Myriad things' transformation has no constant form; men's shifting shapes have no constant body; sometimes large becomes small, or small becomes large — firmly there is no superiority or inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Forms shift without rank — size is no measure of worth.

sentences.zh: 夫萬物之化，一例之道也。

translations.literal: Myriad things' transformation — one pattern's way.
translations.idiomatic: All transformations follow one pattern.

sentences.zh: 是以夏鯀，天子之父，趙王如意，漢祖之子，而鯀為黃熊，如意為蒼狗，斯亦至尊之位而為黔喙之類也。

translations.literal: Therefore Xia Gun, Son of Heaven's father; Prince Liu Ruyi, Han Founder's son — yet Gun became yellow bear, Ruyi became blue dog; these too are most honored positions yet became snouted creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Gun became a bear and Liu Ruyi a dog — the highest may take vile shapes.

sentences.zh: 況者協辰巳之位，烏者棲太陽之精，此乃騰黑之明象，白日之流景，如書佐、鈴下，各以微軀化為蛇、烏，不亦過乎！」〉

translations.literal: Moreover xie harmonizes chen-si position; crow perches the great sun's essence — this then is soaring black's bright image, white day's flowing radiance; if clerk assistants and bell-ringers each by slight bodies transform to snake and crow — is it not excessive!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Birds and serpent‑omens are sun and season emblems; petty shapes can image great offices without shame."〉

sentences.zh: 清河王經去官還家，輅與相見。

translations.literal: Qinghe Wang Jing left office and returned home; Lu met with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing of Qinghe resigned and met Guan Lu at home.

sentences.zh: 經曰：「近有一怪，大不喜之，欲煩作卦。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Recently there was one marvel, greatly disliked it; wish to trouble you to make hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: He said a recent marvel troubled him and asked for a reading.

sentences.zh: 」卦成，輅曰：「爻吉，不為怪也。

translations.literal: " Hexagram completed; Lu said: "The lines are auspicious — it is not a marvel.
translations.idiomatic: The cast came auspicious — no baleful portent."

sentences.zh: 君夜在堂戶前，有一流光如燕爵者，入君懷中，殷殷有聲，內神不安，解衣彷徉，招呼婦人，覓索餘光。

translations.literal: You at night before the hall door had one flowing light like swallow sparrow, entered your bosom, murmuring murmuring had sound; inner spirit not at peace; you undressed clothes and wandered; called wife and women, searched for the remaining light.
translations.idiomatic: He described a swallow‑like light that flew into Wang's breast with a hum, unsettling him until he searched his robes with his wife.

sentences.zh: 」經大笑曰：「實如君言。

translations.literal: " Jing greatly laughed saying: "Indeed as you said.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing laughed, "Just as you said.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「吉，遷官之徵也，其應行至。

translations.literal: " Lu said: "Auspicious — sign of transferred office; its response will arrive soon.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said it foretold promotion — the proof would come quickly."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，經為江夏太守。

translations.literal: " In a while Jing became Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named governor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：經欲使輅卜，而有疑難之言，輅笑而咎之曰：「君侯州里達人，何言之鄙！

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Jing wished to make Lu divine but had doubtful difficult words; Lu smiled and reproached him: "You, sir, are a worthy of your district — how vulgar your words!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jing hesitated to ask, Guan Lu scolded him for scruples unworthy of a gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 昔司馬季主有言，夫卜者必法天地，象四時，順仁義。

translations.literal: Formerly Sima Jizhu had words: diviners must model Heaven and earth, image the four seasons, follow benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Sima Jizhu: true diviners mirror heaven, earth, and the seasons in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 伏羲作八卦，周文王三百八十四爻，而天下治。

translations.literal: Fuxi made eight trigrams, King Wen three hundred sixty-four lines, and all under Heaven was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi's eight trigrams to King Wen's 384 lines the realm was governed.

sentences.zh: 病者或以愈，且死或以生，患或以免，事或以成，嫁女娶妻或以生長，豈直數千錢哉？

translations.literal: The sick sometimes thereby recover, the dying sometimes thereby live, disaster sometimes thereby avoided, affairs sometimes thereby completed; marrying daughters and taking wives sometimes thereby grow and thrive — is it only several thousand cash?
translations.idiomatic: Divination heals, saves, marries, and builds states — worth more than a few coins?"

sentences.zh: 以此推之，急務也。

translations.literal: By this pushing it, urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: It is urgent business, not vulgar trade.

sentences.zh: 苟道之明，聖賢不讓，況吾小人，敢以為難！

translations.literal: If the Way is clear, sages and worthies do not yield — how much more we petty men, dare think it difficult!
translations.idiomatic: If the Way is clear, sages do not disdain divination — how dare I refuse!"

sentences.zh: 」彥緯斂手謝輅：「前言戲之耳。

translations.literal: " Yanwei gathered hands and apologized to Lu: "Former words were jest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing apologized for his flippancy."

sentences.zh: 」於是輅為作卦，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Lu for him made hexagram; his words all verified.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu cast again; every word proved true.

sentences.zh: 經每論輅，以為得龍雲之精，能養和通幽者，非徒合會之才也。〉

translations.literal: Jing every time discussed Lu, thought he obtained dragon-cloud essence, able to nurture harmony and penetrate the hidden — not merely combining-meeting talent."〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing said Guan Lu had dragon‑cloud genius — harmonizing yin and penetrating mystery, not mere cleverness."〉

sentences.zh: 輅又至郭恩家，有飛鳩來在梁頭，鳴甚悲。

translations.literal: Lu again went to Guo En's house; there was flying turtle-dove that came on the beam head, crying very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: At Guo En's a turtle dove alighted on a beam, wailing.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「當有老公從東方來，攜豚一頭，酒一壺。

translations.literal: Lu said: "There ought to be an old man coming from the east, carrying one piglet, one flask of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu predicted an eastern visitor with a piglet and wine.

sentences.zh: 主人雖喜，當有小故。

translations.literal: Though the host will rejoice, there ought to be a small mishap.
translations.idiomatic: The host would rejoice yet suffer a small mishap.

sentences.zh: 」明日果有客，如所佔。

translations.literal: " Next day indeed there was a guest, as divined.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the guest arrived as foretold.

sentences.zh: 恩使客節酒、戒肉、慎火，而射雞作食，箭從樹間激中數歲女子手，流血驚怖。

translations.literal: En made the guest moderate wine, abstain from meat, guard against fire; yet shot chicken to make food; arrow from between trees shot and hit a several-sui girl's hand; blood flowed, fright and terror.
translations.idiomatic: Guo En bade him spare wine and fire yet served chicken; a stray arrow from the trees wounded a girl's hand.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傅曰：義博從輅學鳥鳴之候，輅言君雖好道，天才既少，又不解音律，恐難為師也。

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Yibo from Lu learned bird-cry signs; Lu said though you love the Way, natural talent is already little, moreover do not understand pitch pipes — fear hard to be teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu told Guo En he lacked ear for bird augury.

sentences.zh: 輅為說八風之變，五音之數，以律呂為眾鳥之商，六甲為時日之端，反覆譴曲，出入無窮。

translations.literal: Lu for him explained eight winds' changes, five tones' numbers, using pitch pipes as many birds' pitch, using six jia as day-hour's tip, turning and returning intricate, in-out without end.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on winds, tones, liu jia, and bird calls until Guo En's head spun.

sentences.zh: 義博靜然沈思，馳精數日，卒無所得。

translations.literal: Yibo silently pondered, raced spirit several days, in the end obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo En pondered days and grasped nothing.

sentences.zh: 義博言：「才不出位，難以追徵於此。

translations.literal: Yibo said: "Talent does not step beyond its rank; hard to pursue verification here.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted his talent could not reach the art.

sentences.zh: 」遂止。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon stopped."〉
translations.idiomatic: He gave up the study."〉

sentences.zh: 輅至安德令劉長仁家，有鳴鵲來在閤屋上，其聲甚急。

translations.literal: Lu went to Magistrate of Ande Liu Changren's house; there was calling magpie that came on the chamber roof, its cry very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Changren's a magpie shrieked on the roof.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「鵲言東北有婦昨殺夫，牽引西家人夫離婁，候不過日在虞淵之際，告者至矣。

translations.literal: Lu said: "The magpie says northeast there is a woman yesterday killed husband, dragging in west neighbor's man — Li Lou could not spy it sooner — before the sun sinks into Yu abyss the accuser will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said a northeastern woman had murdered her husband and would blame the western neighbor; the informer would come before sunset.

sentences.zh: 」到時，果有東北同伍民來告，鄰婦手殺其夫，詐言西家人與夫有嫌，來殺我婿。

translations.literal: " When the time came, indeed there was northeast same-ward commoner who came to report — neighboring woman by hand killed her husband, falsely said west household people had grudge with husband, came killed my son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a neighbor denounced the wife for killing her husband and framing the west family.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：勃海劉長仁有辯才，初雖聞輅能曉鳥鳴，後每見難輅曰：「夫生民之音曰言，鳥獸之聲曰鳴，故言者則有知之貴靈，鳴者則無知之賤名，何由以鳥鳴為語，亂神明之所異也？

translations.literal: Separate biography says: Bohai Liu Changren had disputing eloquence; at first though heard Lu could understand bird cries, afterward every meeting challenged Lu: "The sound of living people is called speech; bird and beast sounds are called cries — therefore speech has the noble intelligence of knowing, cries have the base name of not knowing — how can you take bird cries as language, confusing what spirits and gods differentiate?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changren challenged the notion that bird calls are language?"

sentences.zh: 孔子曰』吾不與鳥獸同群'，明其賤也。

translations.literal: Confucius said 'I do not herd with birds and beasts' — clarifying their baseness.
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Confucius: I do not herd with birds and beasts — marking their baseness.

sentences.zh: 」輅答曰：「夫天雖有大象而不能言，故運星精於上，流神明於下，驗風雲以表異，役鳥獸以通靈。

translations.literal: " Lu answered: "Though Heaven has great images yet cannot speak, therefore it moves star essences above, flows numinous intelligence below, tests wind and cloud to show strangeness, employs birds and beasts to communicate spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu answered, "Heaven speaks through stars, winds, and birds as emissaries."

sentences.zh: 表異者必有浮沈之候，通靈者必有宮商之應，是以宋襄失德，六鶂並退，伯姬將焚，鳥唱其災，四國未火，融風已發，赤鳥夾日，殃在荊楚。

translations.literal: Those who show strangeness must have floating-sinking signs; those who communicate spirit must have gong-shang responses; therefore Duke Song lost virtue, six yi-birds together retreated; Bo Ji about to burn, birds sang her disaster; four states not yet afire, Rong wind already rose; red birds flanked the sun, disaster in Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He listed classical bird omens from Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 此乃上天之所使，自然之明符。

translations.literal: This then is what Heaven above sends, natural bright tally.
translations.idiomatic: These are heaven's own signals, not human fancy.

sentences.zh: 考之律呂則音聲有本，求之人事則吉凶不失。

translations.literal: Examining in pitch pipes then sounds have root; seeking in human affairs then good and ill do not miss.
translations.idiomatic: Match the tones to the calendar and the omen never misses human events.

sentences.zh: 昔在秦祖，以功受封，葛盧聽音，著在春秋，斯皆典謨之實，非聖賢之虛名也。

translations.literal: Formerly at Qin ancestor, by merit received enfeoffment; Gelu listened to sounds, recorded in Spring and Autumn — these are canonical pattern's substance, not sages' empty names.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Qin's ancestor and Gelu's ear for bird speech in the classics — real precedent, not empty lore.

sentences.zh: 商之將興，由一燕卵也。

translations.literal: Shang's rise to power began with a single swallow's egg.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of Shang hinged, it is said, on a swallow's egg.

sentences.zh: 文王受命，丹鳥銜書，此乃聖人之靈祥，周室之休祚，何賤之有乎？

translations.literal: King Wen received the Mandate when a red bird brought a writ — this was the sage's numinous omen and the Zhou house's blessing — what is base in that?
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen received Heaven's charge, a vermilion bird bore a writ to him — a sage's auspice and the fortune of Zhou — nothing lowly in that.

sentences.zh: 夫鳥鳴之聽，精在鶉火，妙在八神，自非斯倫，猶子路之於死生也。

translations.literal: As for listening to bird cries, its essence lies in the Chunhuo lodge and its subtlety in the Eight Spirits; unless one belongs to that order, it is like Zilu discoursing on life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Bird augury turns on the Chunhuo asterism and the Eight Spirits; without that training it is as futile as Zilu debating fate.

sentences.zh: 」長仁言：「君辭雖茂，華而不實，未敢之信。

translations.literal: Changren said: "Your rhetoric is lush, yet flowery and hollow — I dare not trust it."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changren said, "Your words bloom without fruit — I cannot trust them yet."

sentences.zh: 」須臾有鳴鵲之驗，長仁乃服。〉

translations.literal: In a moment there was the magpie's verification, and Changren submitted.〉
translations.idiomatic: Moments later the magpie proved him right, and Liu conceded.〉

sentences.zh: 輅至列人典農王弘直許，有飄風高三尺餘，從申上來，在庭中幢幢迴轉，息以復起，良久乃止。

translations.literal: Lu went to the household of Wang Hongzhi, the agricultural director at Lieren; there was a drifting wind more than three chi high, rising from the west, wheeling in the courtyard, resting then rising again, and long after it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu visited Wang Hongzhi at Lieren; a whirlwind over three feet high blew in from the west, spun through the yard, fell still, rose again, and at last died away.

sentences.zh: 直以問輅，輅曰：「東方當有馬吏至，恐父哭子，如何！

translations.literal: Hongzhi asked Lu; Lu said: "From the east a horse courier ought to arrive — I fear a father will mourn a son — what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked him; Guan Lu said, "A mounted messenger will come from the east, and a father will weep for his son."

sentences.zh: 」明日膠東吏到，直子果亡。

translations.literal: Next day a clerk from Jiaodong arrived, and Hongzhi's son had indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an eastern courier came, and Wang's son was dead.

sentences.zh: 直問其故，輅曰：「其日乙卯，則長子之候也。

translations.literal: Hongzhi asked the reason; Lu said: "That day was yimao — the sign of the eldest son."
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked why; Guan Lu said the day-branch yimao marked the firstborn.

sentences.zh: 木落於申，鬥建申，申破寅，死喪之候也。

translations.literal: Wood falls in shen, the Dipper stands at shen, shen breaks yin — the omen of death and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wood wanes in shen, the dipper rests on shen, shen breaks yin — the pattern of mourning.

sentences.zh: 日加午而風發，則馬之候也。

translations.literal: When the sun reached wu and the wind rose, that was the horse omen.
translations.idiomatic: Wind at the hour wu marked the horse courier.

sentences.zh: 離為文章，則吏之候也。

translations.literal: Li means pattern — the omen of a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The trigram Li betokened documents — the clerk.

sentences.zh: 申未為虎，虎為大人，則父之候也。

translations.literal: Between shen and wei lies the tiger, and the tiger is the great man — the omen of a father.
translations.idiomatic: Shen-wei is the tiger hour, and the tiger is the father figure.

sentences.zh: 」有雄雉飛來，登直內鈴柱頭，直大以不安，令輅作卦，輅曰：「到五月必遷。

translations.literal: A cock pheasant flew and perched on the inner bell-post; Hongzhi was greatly uneasy and ordered Lu to cast; Lu said: "By the fifth month you will be transferred."
translations.idiomatic: A cock landed on the house bell; Wang grew afraid until Guan Lu promised a promotion in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 」時三月也，至期，直果為勃海太守。

translations.literal: It was the third month; when the time came, Hongzhi indeed became grand administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: It was the third month; when the date came Wang Hongzhi was named governor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅又曰：「夫風以時動，爻以像應，時者神之驅使，象者時之形表，一時其道，不足為難。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Lu also said: "Wind moves with the season and lines answer the image; seasons are what spirits drive, images are the face of the hour — grasp one moment's pattern and the rest is not hard."
translations.idiomatic: The appendix records Guan Lu's gloss: time drives the hexagrams, and images are the skin of the moment — once you see that, the reading is easy."

sentences.zh: 」王弘直亦大學問，有道術，皆不能精。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhi was also broadly learned and had dao arts, yet could not master the subtle points.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhi was lettered and dabbled in occult arts, but never reached Guan Lu's depth.

sentences.zh: 問輅：「風之推變，乃可爾乎？

translations.literal: He asked Lu: "Can wind's transformations really be pushed so far?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether wind lore could truly be pushed that far.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「此但風之毛髮，何足為異？

translations.literal: Lu said: "This is only the wind's down — what is worth marveling at?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu replied, "That gust was mere fluff on the breeze — nothing wonderful."

sentences.zh: 若夫列宿不守，眾神亂行，八風橫起，怒氣電飛，山崩石飛，樹木摧傾，揚塵萬里，仰不見天，鳥獸藏竄，兆民駭驚，於是使梓慎之徒，登高台，望風氣，分災異，刻期日，然後知神思遐幽，靈風可懼。」〉

translations.literal: When constellations slip, gods run riot, the eight winds cross, wrath rides lightning, mountains fall and stones fly, forests snap, dust blinds the sky for myriad li, one cannot look up to heaven, birds and beasts hide and bolt, the myriad people panic — then you set a Zishen on a high tower to read the qi, sort disasters, and fix the day; only then do you know how deep spirit thought runs and how terrible numinous wind can be."〉
translations.idiomatic: Only when heaven's messengers riot across the sky do you need a court astrologer on a high terrace — then you learn how awesome the wind truly is."〉

sentences.zh: 館陶令諸葛原遷新興太守，輅往祖餞之，賓客並會。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhuge Yuan of Guantao was promoted to grand administrator of Xinxing; Lu went to his farewell feast with all guests assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Yuan left Guantao for Xinxing, Guan Lu joined his parting banquet.

sentences.zh: 原自起取燕卵、蜂窠、蜘蛛著器中，使射覆。

translations.literal: Yuan himself took a swallow's egg, hornet nest, and spider, placed them in a vessel, and had him shoot the covered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge hid a swallow egg, a wasp nest, and a spider for the guessing game.

sentences.zh: 卦成，輅曰：「第一物，含氣須變，依乎宇堂，雄雌以形，翅翼舒張，此燕卵也。

translations.literal: When the hexagram was complete, Lu said: "The first object holds breath and must change; it dwells under the eaves in male and female form with spreading wings — this is a swallow's egg."
