translations.idiomatic: The first sign was a swallow egg sheltered under the rafters.

sentences.zh: 第二物，家室倒縣，門戶眾多，藏精育毒，得秋乃化，此蜂窠也。

translations.literal: The second hangs the house upside down, many doors, hoards essence and breeds poison, maturing in autumn — this is a hornet nest.
translations.idiomatic: The second was a hornet comb hung like an inverted chamber, venomous and ripening in autumn.

sentences.zh: 第三物，觳觫長足，吐絲成羅，尋網求食，利在昬夜，此蜘蛛也。

translations.literal: The third trembles on long legs, spins silk into nets, seeks food along the mesh — profit lies in dusk and night — this is a spider."
translations.idiomatic: The third was a long-legged spider weaving its night snare."

sentences.zh: 」舉坐驚喜。

translations.literal: The whole company was startled and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The company broke into applause.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：諸葛原字景春，亦學士。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Zhuge Yuan, styled Jingchun, was also a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The note identifies Zhuge Yuan as Jingchun, a man of letters.

sentences.zh: 好卜筮，數與輅共射覆，不能窮之。

translations.literal: He loved divination and several times shot the covered with Lu without exhausting him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved stalk-casting but could never stump Guan Lu.

sentences.zh: 景春與輅有榮辱之分，因輅餞之，大有高譚之客。

translations.literal: Jingchun and Lu had a rivalry, yet because of Lu's farewell he gathered lofty debaters.
translations.idiomatic: Though rivals, Zhuge gathered famous talkers for Guan Lu's send-off.

sentences.zh: 諸人多聞其善卜、仰觀，不知其有大異之才，於是先與輅共論聖人著作之原，又敘五帝、三王受命之符。

translations.literal: Most had heard of his skill at divination and looking up, not knowing he had a vastly unusual talent; therefore they first with Lu discussed the origins of the sages' writings, then rehearsed the talismans by which the Five Emperors and Three Kings received the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They opened with high Confucian talk — the classics and the cosmic signs of ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 輅解景春微旨，遂開張戰地，示以不固，藏匿孤虛，以待來攻。

translations.literal: Lu parsed Jingchun's subtle intent, then opened a battlefield of argument, showed apparent weakness, hid the orphan-empty stratagem, and waited for the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu read his opponent, feigned gaps, and laid a rhetorical ambush.

sentences.zh: 景春奔北，軍師摧衄，自言吾睹卿旌旗，城池已壞也。

translations.literal: Jingchun broke north, his staff crushed, himself saying he saw your banners and his city walls already ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge retreated in disorder, confessing that Guan Lu's banners had already stormed his citadel.

sentences.zh: 其欲戰之士，於此鳴鼓角，舉雲梯，弓弩大起，牙旗雨集。

translations.literal: Those who wished to fight there beat drums and horns, raised cloud-ladders, crossbows sprang up, yak-tail banners gathered like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Would-be champions sounded the charge, raised ladders, and bristled with arrows and banners.

sentences.zh: 然後登城曜威，開門受敵，上論五帝，如江如漢，下論三王，如翮如翰；

translations.literal: Then he mounted the wall to display might, opened the gates to receive the foe, discoursing upward on the Five Emperors like the Yangzi and Han rivers, downward on the Three Kings like soaring pinions.
translations.idiomatic: Then he mounted the rhetorical wall, flung open the gates, and praised the Five Emperors like great rivers and the Three Kings like beating wings.

sentences.zh: 其英者若春華之俱發，其攻者若秋風之落葉。

translations.literal: The brilliant passages bloomed like spring blossoms together; the assaults fell like autumn wind's leaves.
translations.idiomatic: His flourishes opened like spring flowers; his rebuttals dropped like autumn leaves.

sentences.zh: 聽者眩惑，不達其義，言者收聲，莫不心服，雖白起之坑趙卒，項羽之塞濉水，無以尚之。

translations.literal: Listeners were dazzled and could not grasp the sense; speakers fell silent — none failed to submit inwardly; though Bai Qi's pitting of Zhao troops or Xiang Yu's damming of the Sui could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: The audience was dizzied into silence — a rout worse than Bai Qi's massacre or Xiang Yu's flood at Sui.

sentences.zh: 於時客皆欲面縛銜璧，求束手於軍鼓之下。

translations.literal: Then the guests all wished to bind themselves with jade in their mouths and beg to have hands tied beneath the army drum.
translations.idiomatic: They would gladly have bound themselves with surrender jades under his war drum.

sentences.zh: 輅猶總干山立，未便許之。

translations.literal: Yet Lu still grasped his shield and stood like a mountain, not readily granting it.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu stood like a cliff and refused their instant surrender.

sentences.zh: 至明日，離別之際，然後有腹心始終。

translations.literal: Only on the morrow at the moment of parting did he then speak heart-to-heart to the end.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day of leave-taking he spoke in earnest to his closest hearers.

sentences.zh: 一時海內俊士，八九人矣。

translations.literal: In one gathering there were eight or nine of the realm's finest minds.
translations.idiomatic: The room held eight or nine of the empire's sharpest younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 蔡元才在朋友中最有清才，在眾人中言：「本聞卿作狗，何意為龍？

translations.literal: Cai Yuancai, among friends the clearest talent, said before the crowd: "We had heard you were a dog — how did you become a dragon?"
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yuancai cried, "We took you for a cur — when did you turn dragon?"

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「潛陽未變，非卿所知，焉有狗耳，得聞龍聲乎！

translations.literal: Lu said: "The hidden yang has not yet changed — not what you know — how should dog ears hear the dragon's voice!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu retorted, "The submerged yang has not yet risen — dog ears cannot catch a dragon's roar."

sentences.zh: 」景春言：「今當遠別，後會何期？

translations.literal: Jingchun said: "Now we part far — when shall we meet again?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge said, "We part for a long road — when shall we meet again?"

sentences.zh: 且復共一射覆。

translations.literal: Let us again together shoot the covered once.
translations.idiomatic: Let us try one more round of shoot-the-covered."

sentences.zh: 」輅佔既皆中。

translations.literal: Lu's divinations all hit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu named every hidden object.

sentences.zh: 景春大笑，「卿為我論此卦意，紓我心懷」。

translations.literal: Jingchun greatly laughed: "Explain this hexagram for me and ease my mind."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge laughed and begged him to unpack the reading.

sentences.zh: 輅為開爻散理，分賦形象，言徵辭合，妙不可述。

translations.literal: Lu opened the lines and scattered the argument, assigning images; phrase matched verification — the subtlety could not be described.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu unfolded the lines with uncanny precision.

sentences.zh: 景春及眾客莫不言聽後論之美，勝於射覆之樂。

translations.literal: Jingchun and the guests all said that hearing the later discourse was finer than the joy of shooting the covered.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed the commentary outshone the parlor trick.

sentences.zh: 景春與輅別，戒以二事，言；

translations.literal: When Jingchun parted from Lu he warned him with two matters, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At parting Zhuge Yuan offered two cautions:

sentences.zh: 「卿性樂酒，量雖溫克，然不可保，寧當節之。

translations.literal: "You love wine; though your measure is temperate, nothing is certain — you ought to temper it."
translations.idiomatic: "You love wine; though you carry it well, ration yourself."

sentences.zh: 卿有水鏡之才，所見者妙，仰觀雖神，禍如膏火，不可不慎。

translations.literal: You have water-mirror talent; what you see is subtle; though looking up at the stars is divine, the bale is like grease feeding fire — you cannot but be careful."
translations.idiomatic: "Your sight is limpid as still water, yet star lore burns like grease on a flame — beware."

sentences.zh: 持卿叡才，遊於雲漢之聞，不憂不富貴也。

translations.literal: With such keen gifts, roaming amid the Milky Way's renown, you need not worry about wealth or nobility.
translations.idiomatic: "With genius like yours you will not lack wealth or station."

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「酒不可極，才不可盡，吾欲持酒以禮，持才以愚，何患之有也？」〉

translations.literal: Lu said: "Wine cannot be exhausted, talent cannot be spent — I wish to hold wine by ritual and hold talent by foolishness — what then is there to fear?""〉
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu answered, "I will not drain the cup nor exhaust my wit — I keep wine by rite and hide genius behind folly — what have I to fear?""〉

sentences.zh: 輅族兄孝國，居在斥丘，輅往從之，與二客會。

translations.literal: Lu's clansman Xiaoguo lived at Chiqu; Lu went to join him and met two guests.
translations.idiomatic: He visited his kinsman Guo Xiaoguo at Chiqu and met two travelers.

sentences.zh: 客去後，輅謂孝國曰：「此二人天庭及口耳之間同有凶氣，異變俱起，雙魂無宅，

translations.literal: After the guests left, Lu told Xiaoguo: "Between brow and mouth those two share baleful qi; strange signs will strike together; paired souls will have no home —
translations.idiomatic: When they had gone he whispered, "Those two carry death between brow and lip — twin omens — their souls will soon be homeless —

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅又曰：「厚味臘毒，天精幽夕，坎為棺槨，兌為喪車。」〉

translations.literal: Separate biography: Lu also said: "Rich flavors are waxy poison; heaven's essence hides at night; Kan is the coffin and inner shell, Dui the hearse."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The note adds: rich fare is slow poison; Kan is the coffin and Dui the bier."〉

sentences.zh: 流魂於海，骨歸於家，少許時當並死也。

translations.literal: Drifting souls to the sea, bones returning home — within a short while they will die together."
translations.idiomatic: their shades will wash downriver while their bones go home — they will die together very soon."

sentences.zh: 」復數十日，二人飲酒醉，夜共載車，牛驚下道入漳河中，皆即溺死也。

translations.literal: Several tens of days later the two drank to drunkenness, rode together in a cart by night; the ox bolted off the road into the Zhang River and both drowned at once.
translations.idiomatic: A few weeks later the pair got drunk, shared a cart at night, ran off the dike into the Zhang, and drowned together.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，輅之鄰裡，外戶不閉，無相偷竊者。

translations.literal: At that time in Lu's village outer doors were not closed and none stole from one another.
translations.idiomatic: In his village at that time people left doors unbarred and nothing was stolen.

sentences.zh: 清河太守華表，召輅為文學掾。

translations.literal: Hua Biao, grand administrator of Qinghe, summoned Lu as literary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Hua Biao of Qinghe named him a literary clerk.

sentences.zh: 安平趙孔曜薦輅於冀州刺史裴徽曰：「輅雅性寬大，與世無忌，仰觀天文則同妙甘公、石申，俯覽周易則齊思季主。

translations.literal: Zhao Kongyao of Anping recommended Lu to Ji Province's inspector Pei Hui, saying: "Lu is broad in nature and jealous of none; looking up at astronomy he matches Gan Gong and Shi Shen in subtlety; bending to the Zhou yi he equals Sima Jizhu in thought."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kongyao told Inspector Pei Hui that Guan Lu rivaled Gan Gong and Shi Shen above and Sima Jizhu below.

sentences.zh: 今明使君方垂神幽藪，留精九皋，輅宜蒙陰和之應，得及羽儀之時。

translations.literal: Now that the enlightened envoy lets spirit sink into hidden thickets and thought linger in the nine marshes, Lu ought to receive Heaven's harmonizing response and reach the hour when phoenix feathers adorn the court."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Pei to draw Guan Lu into service before the phoenix court."

sentences.zh: 」徽於是辟為文學從事，引與相見，大善友之。

translations.literal: Pei thereupon summoned him as literary attendant, led him in to meet, and befriended him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui summoned him as literary attendant and treated him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 徙部鉅鹿，遷治中別駕。

translations.literal: The headquarters moved to Julu; he was promoted administrative aide and chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the yamen to Julu and rose to senior staff.

sentences.zh: 初應州召，與弟季儒共載，至武城西，自卦吉凶，語儒云：「當在故城中見三貍，爾者乃顯。

translations.literal: When he first answered the provincial summons he rode with his younger brother Jiru west of Wucheng, cast his own oracle for good or ill, and told Ru: "We ought to see three wildcats in the old city — then it will appear."
translations.idiomatic: Riding with his brother toward the capital, he divined that three wildcats in a ruined fort would confirm the omen.

sentences.zh: 」前到河西故城角，正見三貍共踞城側，兄弟並喜。

translations.literal: Going forward to the ruined corner west of the river, they indeed saw three raccoon dogs crouching together by the city wall; both brothers rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: West of the ford three wildcats crouched on the ruin — the brothers cheered.

sentences.zh: 正始九年舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengshi he was recommended as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 9 he passed the xiucai examination.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅為華清河所召，為北黌文學，一時士友無不嘆慕。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Because Hua of Qinghe summoned him as northern-school scholar, gentlemen of the time all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The note says his Qinghe post made every scholar jealous.

sentences.zh: 安平趙孔曜，明敏有思識，與輅有管、鮑之分，故從發干來，就郡黌上與輅相見，言：「卿腹中汪汪，故時死人半，今生人無雙，當去俗騰飛，翱翔昊蒼，云何在此？

translations.literal: Zhao Kongyao of Anping, clear and quick with reflective judgment, had with Lu the friendship of Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; therefore he came from Fagan to the county school to meet Lu and said: "Your belly holds a sea — half the men of the age are dead and none living can match you — you ought to leave the vulgar world and soar in the blue sky — why stay here?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kongyao, his sworn friend, rode from Fagan to say, "You carry an ocean in your breast while half the world lies in the grave — leave this backwater and mount the sky."

sentences.zh: 聞卿消息，使吾食不甘味也。

translations.literal: Hearing news of you makes my food tasteless.
translations.idiomatic: News of you wasting here steals my appetite.

sentences.zh: 冀州裴使君才理清明，能釋玄虛，每論易及老、莊之道，未嘗不注精於嚴、瞿之徒也。

translations.literal: Inspector Pei of Ji Province is lucid in principle and can unlock dark mysteries; whenever he discusses the Yi, Laozi, or Zhuang he rivets the subtlest minds like Yan and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui plumbs the Yi, Laozi, and Zhuang as few can.

sentences.zh: 又眷吾意重，能相明信者。

translations.literal: He also esteems my intent deeply and can trust and make clear to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He esteems me and trusts true talent.

sentences.zh: 今當故往，為卿陳感虎開石之誠。

translations.literal: Now I go expressly to lay before him the sincerity that moved the tiger and split the stone.
translations.idiomatic: I go to plead with the sincerity that moved beasts and stone."

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「吾非四淵之龍，安能使白日晝陰？

translations.literal: Lu said: "I am not the dragon of the four deeps — how could I make the noon sun turn dark?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu answered, "I am no dragon of the four seas — I cannot darken the noon sun."

sentences.zh: 卿若能動東風、興朝雲，吾志所不讓也。

translations.literal: If you can stir the east wind and raise morning clouds, my ambition will not yield to yours."
translations.idiomatic: Stir an east wind and morning mist yourself, and I will match you."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂至冀州見裴使君。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Ji Province and met Inspector Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled to Ye to meet Pei Hui.

sentences.zh: 使君言：「君顏色何以消減故邪？

translations.literal: The inspector said: "Why has your color grown so thin?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei asked why he looked haggard.

sentences.zh: 」孔曜言：「體中無藥石之疾，然見清河郡內有一騏驥，拘縶後厩歷年，去王良、伯樂百八十里，不得騁天骨，起風塵，以此憔悴耳。

translations.literal: Kongyao said: "In his body there is no mineral-drug illness — yet within Qinghe commandery there is a thoroughbred tethered in a rear stable for years, one hundred eighty li from Wang Liang and Bole, unable to stretch his heavenly bones or raise wind and dust — by this he is wasted."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered, "No drug ails him — but Qinghe pens a stallion a hundred eighty li from any true judge, so his bones never stretch and his dust never rises."

sentences.zh: 」使君言：「騏驥今何在也？

translations.literal: The inspector said: "Where is this thoroughbred now?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei asked where the horse was.

sentences.zh: 」孔曜言：「平原管輅字公明，年三十六，雅性寬大，與世無忌，可謂士雄。

translations.literal: Kongyao said: "Guan Lu of Pingyuan, styled Gongming, thirty-six years old, broad in nature and jealous of none — he may be called a hero among scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao named Guan Lu of Pingyuan, thirty-six, a hero among scholars.

sentences.zh: 仰觀天文則能同妙甘公、石申，俯覽周易則能思齊季主，遊步道術，開神無窮，可謂士英。

translations.literal: Looking up at astronomy he can match Gan Gong and Shi Shen in subtlety; bending to the Zhou yi he can equal Jizhu in thought; roaming the arts of the Way he opens spirit without end — he may be called the elite among scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In stars he equals Gan and Shi; in the Yi he rivals Jizhu; in dao arts he is inexhaustible — the elite of his generation.

sentences.zh: 抱荊山之璞，懷夜光之寶，而為清河郡所錄北黌文學，可為痛心疾首也。

translations.literal: He hugs the jade of Jing Mountain and the pearl that gleams at night, yet Qinghe commandery records him as northern-school clerk — enough to tear one's hair and strike one's head.
translations.idiomatic: He holds uncut jade from Jing yet is filed as a petty instructor — a scandal.

sentences.zh: 使君方欲流精九皋，垂神幽藪，欲令明主不獨治，逸才不久滯，高風遐被，莫不草靡，宜使輅特蒙陰和之應，得及羽儀之時，必能翼宣隆化，揚聲九圍也。

translations.literal: Your Honor now means to pour spirit into the nine marshes and sink thought into hidden thickets, wishing the enlightened ruler not to govern alone and stray talent not to stagnate long — when your high wind spreads far, none will fail to bend like grass; you ought to let Lu specially receive Heaven's harmonizing response and reach the hour of phoenix feathers, so he may wing-spread your grand transformation and raise his name in the nine circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Let him join your retinue so his wind can carry your rule through the nine domains."

sentences.zh: 」裴使君聞言，則慷慨曰：「何乃爾邪！

translations.literal: Hearing the words, Inspector Pei said indignantly: "How can that be!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Pei cried, "Can this be true?"

sentences.zh: 雖在大州，未見異才可用釋人鬱悶者，思還京師，得共論道耳，況草間自有清妙之才乎？

translations.literal: Though I hold a great province I have not seen unusual talent able to dispel men's gloom — I thought of returning to the capital to discuss the Way — could the weeds hide such a clear and subtle talent?"
translations.idiomatic: Though I govern a great province I have met no genius to lift my gloom — I meant to return to the capital to seek the Way — could the grass conceal such a jewel?"

sentences.zh: 如此便相為取之，莫使騏驥更為凡馬，荊山反成凡石。

translations.literal: If so, then let us fetch him for each other — do not let the thoroughbred become a common horse again or Jing Mountain jade turn back to common stone.
translations.idiomatic: Then fetch him — do not let the steed become a nag or the jade revert to stone."

sentences.zh: 」即檄召輅為文學從事。

translations.literal: Immediately he issued a summons appointing Lu literary attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a commission as literary attendant at once.

sentences.zh: 一相見，清論終日，不覺罷倦。

translations.literal: At the first meeting they discoursed purely all day without feeling weariness.
translations.idiomatic: They talked a full day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 天時大熱，移床在庭前樹下，乃至雞向晨，然後出。

translations.literal: The weather was fiercely hot; they moved the couch beneath a tree in the courtyard until the cock crew toward dawn, then went out.
translations.idiomatic: They moved their seats under a tree and talked until cockcrow in the heat.

sentences.zh: 再相見，便轉為鉅鹿從事。

translations.literal: At the second meeting he was transferred to Julu attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A second audience made him Julu staff.

sentences.zh: 三見，轉治中。

translations.literal: At the third meeting he was transferred administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: A third raised him to administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 四見，轉為別駕。

translations.literal: At the fourth meeting he was transferred chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: A fourth made him chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 至十月，舉為秀才。

translations.literal: By the tenth month he was recommended xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he passed xiucai again.

sentences.zh: 輅辭裴使君，使君言：「

translations.literal: Lu took leave of Inspector Pei; the inspector said: "
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Lu prepared to leave for Luoyang, Pei warned him: "

translations.literal: (Ding)
translations.idiomatic: (Ding)

sentences.zh: 、鄧二尚書，有經國才略，於物理不精也。

translations.literal: and Deng — the two grandees have statecraft and strategy but are not refined in physical principles.
translations.idiomatic: the two Deng ministers are statesmen, not natural philosophers,

sentences.zh: 何尚書神明精微，言皆巧妙，巧妙之志，殆破秋毫，君當慎之！

translations.literal: Grandee He is spirit-like and subtle; his words are all ingenious — that ingenuity can split an autumn hair — you must be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: but Minister He Yan is razor-keen — beware his barbed questions."

sentences.zh: 自言不解易九事，必當以相問。

translations.literal: He says himself he does not understand nine matters in the Yi — he will surely question you on them.
translations.idiomatic: He admits he cannot solve nine Yi puzzles and will test you.

sentences.zh: 比至洛，宜善精其理也。

translations.literal: By the time you reach Luo, you ought to sharpen those principles well."
translations.idiomatic: Polish your answers before you reach Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「何若巧妙，以攻難之才，遊形之表，未入於神。

translations.literal: Lu said: "As for He — if he is ingenious, with talent for attacking difficulties yet roaming outside form — he has not yet entered spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu answered, "He Yan is clever at riddling the surface — he has not touched the spirit of the classic."

sentences.zh: 夫入神者，當步天元，推陰陽，探玄虛，極幽明，然後覽道無窮，未暇細言。

translations.literal: Those who enter spirit ought to pace the celestial origin, push yin and yang, probe dark void, exhaust hidden and manifest, then view the Way without limit — there is no leisure for petty words.
translations.idiomatic: To touch the spirit of the classic you must walk the sky's pivot, work yin and yang, sound the depths, and read the whole Dao — not bandy small talk.

sentences.zh: 若欲差次老、莊而參爻、象，愛微辯而興浮藻，可謂射侯之巧，非能破秋毫之妙也。

translations.literal: If you wish to rank Laozi and Zhuangzi beside the lines and images, dote on hair-splitting debate and spin pretty phrases, you may hit the target like an archer — you will not split the finest autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: Juggling Laozi and Zhuangzi against the hexagrams while chasing clever words is target practice, not the hair's-breadth insight the Yi demands.

sentences.zh: 若九事皆至義者，不足勞思也。

translations.literal: If the nine topics all reach their plain meaning, they are not worth taxing your mind over.
translations.idiomatic: If those nine puzzles are only common doctrine, they hardly need deep thought.

sentences.zh: 若陰陽者，精之以久。

translations.literal: As for yin and yang, refine them over a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang repay long study, not a night's cramming.

sentences.zh: 輅去之後，歲朝當有時刑大風，風必摧破樹木。

translations.literal: After Lu departs, at the new year there ought to be a seasonal-punishment gale; the wind will surely snap trees.
translations.idiomatic: After I leave, the New Year will bring a punishing wind that tears the woods.

sentences.zh: 若發於乾者，必有天威，不足共清譚者。」〉

translations.literal: If it arises from Qian, there will surely be Heaven's majesty — not something to thrash out in idle talk."〉
translations.idiomatic: If the omen rises in Qian, Heaven itself will thunder — no room for salon chatter."〉

sentences.zh: 十二月二十八日，吏部尚書何晏請之，鄧颺在晏許。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, Minister of Personnel He Yan invited him; Deng Yang was present at Yan's house.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth of the twelfth month He Yan, minister of personnel, summoned him; Deng Yang sat in.

sentences.zh: 晏謂輅曰：「聞君著爻神妙，試為作一卦，知位當至三公不？

translations.literal: Yan said to Lu: "I have heard your line readings are divine; try casting a hexagram for me — will my rank reach the Three Dukes?"
translations.idiomatic: He Yan said, "Cast for me — will I rise to the three dukes?"

sentences.zh: 」又問：「連夢見青蠅數十頭，來在鼻上，驅之不肯去，有何意故？

translations.literal: He also asked: "I have repeatedly dreamed of dozens of green flies on my nose; driving them off they will not go — what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I dream of green flies swarming my nose and I cannot brush them away — what does it mean?"

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「夫飛鴞，天下賤鳥，及其在林食椹，則懷我好音，況輅心非草木，敢不盡忠？

translations.literal: Lu said: "The flying owl is the basest bird under Heaven; yet when it is in the forest eating mulberries it brings us a fair cry — how much more, since Lu's heart is not grass or wood, would I dare withhold full loyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "The owl is a low bird, yet in the mulberry grove it sings sweetly to us; I am no stick or stone — I shall speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 昔元、凱之弼重華，宣惠慈和，周公之翼成王，坐而待旦，故能流光六合，萬國咸寧。

translations.literal: In old days Yuan and Kai aided Chonghua, spreading kindness and harmony; the Duke of Zhou aided the King of Cheng, sitting till dawn — therefore their light flowed through the six directions and the myriad states were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the ministers who aided sage kings until their virtue lit the realm.

sentences.zh: 此乃履道休應。

translations.literal: This is the auspicious response of walking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: That is the reward of treading the true path.

sentences.zh: 非卜筮之所明也。

translations.literal: It is not what tortoise-and-milfoil divination can clarify.
translations.idiomatic: No stalk oracle can teach that lesson.

sentences.zh: 今君侯位重山岳，勢若雷電，而懷德者鮮，畏威者眾，殆非小心翼翼多福之仁。

translations.literal: Now, my lord, your position weighs like mountains, your power is like thunder and lightning, yet few cherish your virtue while many fear your awe — hardly the careful, many-blessed benevolence of old.
translations.idiomatic: You stand as high as a peak and strike like lightning, yet few love you and many only fear you — far from the humble mercy that wins Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 又鼻者艮，此天中之山，

translations.literal: Moreover the nose is Gen — this is the 'mountain in the center of heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The nose is the Gen trigram — the mountain at heaven's center.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：相書謂鼻之所在為天中。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi submits: Physiognomy texts call the place of the nose the 'center of heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: face-readers call the nose the "heaven's pivot."

sentences.zh: 鼻有山象，故曰：「天中之山」也。〉

translations.literal: The nose has a mountain image; therefore it is said: 'mountain in the center of heaven.'〉
translations.idiomatic: The nose is shaped like a peak, hence the phrase "mountain at heaven's center."〉

sentences.zh: 高而不危，所以長守貴也。

translations.literal: High yet without peril — that is how one long keeps nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Tall but never tottering — that is how rank endures.

sentences.zh: 今青蠅臭惡，而集之焉。

translations.literal: Now foul green flies gather there.
translations.idiomatic: Now stinking green flies cluster on that height.

sentences.zh: 位峻者顛，輕豪者亡，不可不思害盈之數，盛衰之期。

translations.literal: Where rank is steep, there is overturn; where arrogance is light, there is ruin — you cannot fail to ponder the reckoning of harm from fullness and the term of rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Sheer eminence invites a fall; swagger invites ruin — weigh the lesson of a brimming cup and the turn of fortune.

sentences.zh: 是故山在地中曰謙，雷在天上曰壯；

translations.literal: Therefore a mountain in the earth is called Modesty; thunder in the sky is called Strength.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the classic pairs Modesty — mountain under earth — with Strength — thunder above heaven.

sentences.zh: 謙則裒多益寡，壯則非禮不履。

translations.literal: Modesty trims the great and augments the small; Strength does not tread what ritual forbids.
translations.idiomatic: Modesty cuts the swollen and feeds the lean; Strength refuses unrighteous steps.

sentences.zh: 未有損己而不光大，行非而不傷敗。

translations.literal: Never has anyone harmed himself without bright enlargement, nor walked wrong without hurt and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: No man pares his pride without growing; none walks crooked without breaking.

sentences.zh: 原君侯上追文王六爻之旨，下思尼父彖象之義，然後三公可決，青蠅可驅也。

translations.literal: I pray you, my lord, look upward to King Wen's meaning in the six lines and downward to the Master Kong's gloss on the images — then the Three Dukes may be decided and the green flies may be driven off."
translations.idiomatic: Look up to King Wen's six lines and down to Confucius's images — then you will know your dukedom and shake the flies."

sentences.zh: 」颺曰：「此老生之常譚。

translations.literal: Deng Yang said: "This is the old pedants' worn talk."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang sneered, "Old scholars' platitudes."

sentences.zh: 」輅答曰：「夫老生者見不生，常譚者見不譚。

translations.literal: Lu answered: "The old pedant sees no birth; the worn talk sees no freshness."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu shot back, "The 'old pedant' never sees life renewed; the 'platitude' never sees a fresh word."

sentences.zh: 」晏曰：「過歲更當相見。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "After the new year we shall meet again."
translations.idiomatic: He Yan said, "We shall speak again after New Year."

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅為何晏所請，果共論易九事，九事皆明。

translations.literal: Separate biography: He Yan summoned Lu and they indeed debated nine topics in the Yi; Lu clarified all nine.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The note records the nine Yi puzzles He Yan posed — Guan Lu answered every one.〉

sentences.zh: 晏曰：「君論陰陽，此世無雙。

translations.literal: Yan said: "In discoursing on yin and yang you have no peer in this age."
translations.idiomatic: He Yan said, "None under heaven can match your yin-yang reading."

sentences.zh: 」時鄧颺與晏共坐，颺言：「君見謂善易，而語初不及易中辭義，何故也？

translations.literal: At that time Deng Yang sat with Yan; Yang said: "You are praised as good at the Yi, yet your words never touch the text's wording — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang pressed him: "You are called a master of the Yi, yet you never quote the classic — why?"

sentences.zh: 」輅尋聲答之曰：「夫善易者不論易也。

translations.literal: Lu answered on the spot: "Those who truly excel at the Yi do not talk about the Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu answered, "Those who truly know the Yi do not chatter the Yi."

sentences.zh: 」晏含笑而讚之「可謂要言不煩也」。

translations.literal: Yan smiled and praised him: "That may be called grasping the gist without fuss."
translations.idiomatic: He Yan smiled, "You speak the marrow without the husk."

sentences.zh: 因請輅為卦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked Lu to cast a hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Guan Lu to cast.

sentences.zh: 輅既稱引鑑戒，晏謝之曰：「知幾其神乎，古人以為難；

translations.literal: Lu having cited warnings and mirrors, Yan thanked him, saying: "To know the pivot — that is spirit-like; the ancients thought it hard."
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Lu's warnings He Yan said, "To read the turning point is divine — the ancients called that hard."

sentences.zh: 交疏而吐其誠，今人以為難。

translations.literal: To speak truth across a distant acquaintance — modern men think that hard.
translations.idiomatic: To speak truth to a slight acquaintance — today we call that harder still."

sentences.zh: 今君一面而盡二難之道，可謂明德惟馨。

translations.literal: Now in one meeting you have exhausted both difficulties — it may be called 'bright virtue is fragrant incense.'"
translations.idiomatic: You have done both in one sitting — true virtue has its perfume."

sentences.zh: 詩不云乎，『中心藏之，何日忘之』！」〉

translations.literal: Does not the Ode say, 'I hide it in my heart — what day shall I forget it?'"〉
translations.idiomatic: The Songs say, I treasure it in the breast — what day could I forget?"〉

sentences.zh: 輅還邑舍，具以此言語舅氏，舅氏責輅言太切至。

translations.literal: Lu returned to his lodging and told his maternal uncle everything; the uncle reproached Lu for speaking too cuttingly.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu told his uncle the whole conversation; the uncle scolded him for bluntness.

sentences.zh: 輅曰；

translations.literal: Lu said;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said,

sentences.zh: 「與死人語，何所畏邪？

translations.literal: "What is there to fear in speaking with the dead?"
translations.idiomatic: "When you talk to walking corpses, what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」舅大怒，謂輅狂悖。

translations.literal: The uncle grew angry and called Lu mad and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle called him mad.

sentences.zh: 歲朝，西北大風，塵埃蔽天，十餘日，聞晏、颺皆誅，然後舅氏乃服。

translations.literal: At the new year a great wind from the northwest raised dust that veiled the sky; after more than ten days word came that Yan and Yang had both been executed — then the uncle submitted.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Day brought a northwest gale and dust; ten days later He Yan and Deng Yang fell — then the uncle believed.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：舅夏大夫問輅：「前見何、鄧之日，為已有凶氣未也？

translations.literal: Separate biography: Uncle Minister Xia asked Lu: "On the day you met He and Deng, had they already borne baleful qi?"
translations.idiomatic: 〈His uncle asked whether doom already clung to He and Deng at that meeting.〉

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「與禍人共會，然後知神明交錯；

translations.literal: Lu said: "Only after sharing a sitting with doomed men do I know how spirit and sign interweave."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Sit with the damned and you see how omens braid with fate."

sentences.zh: 與吉人相近，又知聖賢求精之妙。

translations.literal: Draw near to the fortunate and you again know how sages seek the finest essence.
translations.idiomatic: Sit with the blessed and you see how sages polish the truth."

sentences.zh: 夫鄧之行步，則筋不束骨，脈不制肉，起立傾倚，若無手足，謂之鬼躁。

translations.literal: As for Deng's gait — sinews do not bind bone, pulses do not govern flesh; standing he leans as if he had no hands or feet — this is called 'ghost-fidget.'"
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang's sinews never leash his bones — he twitches like a haunted man — 'ghost fidget.'"

sentences.zh: 何之視候，則魂不守宅，血不華色，精爽煙浮，容若槁木，謂之鬼幽。

translations.literal: As for He's mien — the soul does not guard the house, blood does not bloom in the complexion; spirit floats like smoke, the face is dead wood — this is called 'ghost-gloom.'"
translations.idiomatic: He Yan's soul seems absent from his flesh — gray smoke over a dead stump — 'ghost gloom.'"

sentences.zh: 故鬼躁者為風所收，鬼幽者為火所燒，自然之符，不可以蔽也。

translations.literal: Therefore ghost-fidget is gathered in by wind; ghost-gloom is burned by fire — natural tallies that cannot be veiled."
translations.idiomatic: Fidgeting ghosts ride the wind; gloomy ghosts feed the fire — nature's receipt, not my invention."

sentences.zh: 」輅後因得休，裴使君問：「何平叔一代才名，其實何如？

translations.literal: Later, when Lu had leave, Inspector Pei asked: "What was He Pingshu's talent in truth?"
translations.idiomatic: On leave Guan Lu was asked what He Yan was really worth.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「其才若盆盎之水，所見者清，所不見者濁。

translations.literal: Lu said: "His talent is like water in a basin or jar — what it shows is clear, what it hides is turbid."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "He is a bowl of water — clear on top, mud below."

sentences.zh: 神在廣博，志不務學，弗能成才。

translations.literal: His spirit ranges wide but his will does not labor at learning — he cannot complete talent.
translations.idiomatic: He wanders far but will not grind at study — he cannot finish the job.

sentences.zh: 欲以盆盎之水，求一山之形，形不可得，則智由此惑。

translations.literal: He wishes to use basin-water to seek a mountain's shape; when the shape cannot be obtained, understanding is muddled from it.
translations.idiomatic: He tries to map a mountain from a puddle — no wonder his wit grows murky.

sentences.zh: 故說老、莊則巧而多華，說易生義則美而多偽；

translations.literal: Therefore discoursing on Laozi and Zhuangzi he is clever yet florid; discoursing on the Yi he spins meanings fair yet false.
translations.idiomatic: On Lao-Zhuang he is glitter without weight; on the Yi he coins pretty false readings.

sentences.zh: 華則道浮，偽則神虛；

translations.literal: Floridity makes the Way float; falsity makes the spirit hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Ornament floats the Way; invention empties the spirit.

sentences.zh: 得上才則淺而流絕，得中才則遊精而獨出，輅以為少功之才也。

translations.literal: Meeting top talent it runs shallow and the stream dries; meeting middling talent it roams in subtlety alone — Lu esteems this a talent of scant achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Before a master it dries up; before a middling wit it sparkles — I call that small gift."

sentences.zh: 」裴使君曰：「誠如來論。

translations.literal: Inspector Pei said: "Truly as you argue."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui said, "You have the right of it."

sentences.zh: 吾數與平叔共說老、莊及易，常覺其辭妙於理，不能折之。

translations.literal: I several times debated Laozi, Zhuangzi, and the Yi with Pingshu; I always felt his words cleverer than his principle and could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: I often sparred with He Yan and found his words prettier than his logic, yet I could not pin him down.

sentences.zh: 又時人吸習，皆歸服之焉，益令不了。

translations.literal: Moreover the age inhales and imitates; all defer to him — that only deepens the obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd apes him, which thickens the fog.

sentences.zh: 相見得清言，然後灼灼耳。」〉

translations.literal: Once we meet in clear talk, then it will blaze bright."〉
translations.idiomatic: When we meet in plain speech, the matter will blaze clear."〉

sentences.zh: 始輅過魏郡太守鍾毓，共論易義，輅因言「卜可知君生死之日。

translations.literal: At first, when Lu passed Grand Administrator Zhong Yu of Wei commandery, they discussed the Yi's meaning together; Lu therefore said, "Divination can tell the day of your lordship's death."
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Zhong Yu of Wei, Guan Lu said divination could name his death day.

sentences.zh: 」毓使筮其生日月，如言無蹉跌。

translations.literal: Yu had him divine the birth month and day; it matched the words without slip.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu asked for his birth date; Guan Lu hit it exactly.

sentences.zh: 毓大愕然，曰：「君可畏也。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly startled and said: "You are fearsome.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu cried, "You terrify me."

sentences.zh: 死以付天，不以付君。

translations.literal: I leave death to Heaven, not to you."
translations.idiomatic: I leave my end to Heaven, not to your stalks."

sentences.zh: 」遂不復筮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divined no more.
translations.idiomatic: He never asked again.

sentences.zh: 毓問輅：「天下當太平否？

translations.literal: Yu asked Lu: "Will all under Heaven be at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu asked whether the realm would know peace.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「方今四九天飛，利見大人，神武升建，王道文明，何憂不平？

translations.literal: Lu said: "Now is the 'nine-four' flight — it profits to see the great man; divine martial power is raised, the kingly Way is bright — why worry it will not be level?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu cited the hexagram: the great man rises, martial virtue builds, the kingly Way gleams — peace is coming."

sentences.zh: 」毓未解輅言，無幾，曹爽等誅，乃覺寤云。

translations.literal: Yu did not understand Lu's words; before long Cao Shuang and company were executed, and then he awoke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu did not grasp the gloss until Cao Shuang fell — then he understood.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳云：魏郡太守鍾毓，清逸有才，難輅易二十餘事，自以為難之至精也。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Zhong Yu, grand administrator of Wei, clear and talented, posed over twenty hard questions on the Yi to Lu, thinking them supremely fine.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhong Yu stumped him with twenty Yi riddles he thought perfect.〉

sentences.zh: 輅尋聲投響，言無留滯，分張爻象，義皆殊妙。

translations.literal: Lu answered each echo with its sound, words never sticking; he spread the lines and images and every gloss was singularly subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu batted back each one without pause, splitting lines with uncanny glosses.

sentences.zh: 毓即謝輅。

translations.literal: Yu at once apologized to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu apologized at once.

sentences.zh: 輅卜知毓生日月，毓愕然曰：「聖人運神通化，連屬事物，何聰明乃爾！

translations.literal: When Lu divined Yu's birth month and day, Yu said in amazement: "Sages move spirit and transform connections, linking things — how can cleverness reach thus!"
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Lu named his birthday Zhong Yu gasped that sages alone should read fate so sharply."

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「幽明同化，死生一道，悠悠太極，終而復始。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Hidden and manifest share one transformation; death and life are one path; vast Great Ultimate ends and begins again."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Yin and yang are one cycle; the Great Ultimate turns forever."

sentences.zh: 文王損命，不以為憂，仲尼曳杖，不以為懼，緒煩蓍筮，宜盡其意。

translations.literal: King Wen shortened his life yet did not grieve; Kongzi dragged his staff yet did not fear — though tortoise and milfoil tangle, they ought to exhaust their meaning."
translations.idiomatic: King Wen and Confucius faced death calmly — stalks exist to exhaust meaning, not to frighten."

sentences.zh: 」毓曰：「生者好事，死者惡事，哀樂之分，吾所不能齊，且以付天，不以付君也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Life is a good affair, death an ill; the division of grief and joy I cannot equalize — I leave it to Heaven, not to you.""
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu said, "Life is sweet and death bitter — I cannot level joy and sorrow; I leave that to Heaven, not to you."

sentences.zh: 」石苞為鄴典農，與輅相見，問曰：「聞君鄉里翟文耀能隱形，其事可信乎？

translations.literal: Shi Bao, agricultural director at Ye, met Lu and asked: "I have heard that Zhai Wenyao in your village can hide his form — is that credible?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao asked whether Zhai Wenyao could truly vanish.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「此但陰陽蔽匿之數，苟得其數，則四岳可藏，河海可逃。

translations.literal: Lu said: "That is only the reckoning of yin-yang concealment; grasp its numbers and the four marchmounts can be hidden, river and sea escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said it is yin-yang arithmetic — master the numbers and even mountains can hide you.

sentences.zh: 況以七尺之形，遊變化之內，散雲霧以幽身，布金水以滅跡，術足數成，不足為難。

translations.literal: How much more a frame of seven chi, roaming inside transformation, scattering mist-cloud to hide the body, spreading metal-water to erase traces — when art meets number, completion is not hard."
translations.idiomatic: A seven-foot body can ride mist and metal-water to slip sight — easy once the math is sound."

sentences.zh: 」苞曰：「欲聞其妙，君且善論其數也。

translations.literal: Bao said: "I wish to hear the subtlety — please set out its reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao begged for the theory.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「夫物不精不為神，數不妙不為術，故精者神之所合，妙者智之所遇，合之幾微，可以性通，難以言論。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Things that are not refined are not spirit; numbers that are not subtle are not art — therefore refinement is where spirit joins, subtlety is where wit meets; their conjunction is too fine for speech."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Without fineness there is no spirit; without subtlety there is no art — the join is too fine for words."

sentences.zh: 是故魯班不能說其手，離硃不能說其目。

translations.literal: Therefore Lu Ban could not explain his own hand, Li Zhu could not explain his own eye.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ban could not teach his hand nor Li Zhu his eye.

sentences.zh: 非言之難，孔子曰『書不盡言』，言之細也，『言不盡意』，意之微也，斯皆神妙之謂也。

translations.literal: It is not that speech is hard — Confucius said 'writing does not exhaust words' — that is the fineness of words; 'words do not exhaust meaning' — that is the subtlety of meaning; both are what we call spirit-like."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said writing cannot exhaust words nor words meaning — that is the spirit's fineness."

sentences.zh: 請舉其大體以驗之。

translations.literal: Allow me to cite the large pattern to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Let me sketch the large pattern to prove it.

sentences.zh: 夫白日登天，運景萬里，無物不照，及其入地，一炭之光，不可得見。

translations.literal: When the white sun climbs heaven its moving radiance lights myriad li — nothing is not illuminated; yet when it enters earth, not even one ember's glow can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: The noon sun lights the world; underground even a coal cannot shine.

sentences.zh: 三五盈月，清耀燭夜，可以遠望，及其在晝，明不如鏡。

translations.literal: When the third and fifth fill the moon, clear brilliance lights the night and one can gaze far; yet in daylight it is not bright as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The full moon lights the night yet pales before a mirror by day.

sentences.zh: 今逃日月者必陰陽之數，陰陽之數通於萬類，鳥獸猶化，況於人乎！

translations.literal: Now those who flee sun and moon must use yin-yang numbers; yin-yang numbers reach the myriad kinds — birds and beasts still transform, how much more man!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who hide from sun and moon ride yin-yang; if beasts can shift form, how not men?"

sentences.zh: 夫得數者妙，得神者靈，非徒生者有驗，死亦有徵。

translations.literal: Those who obtain the numbers are subtle; those who obtain spirit are numinous — it is not only the living that have verification; the dead also have signs.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers bring subtlety, spirit brings wonder — omens follow the dead as well as the living.

sentences.zh: 是以杜伯乘火氣以流精，彭生託水變以立形。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Du rode fire-breath to drift his essence; Pengsheng relied on water-change to set his shape.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Du's ghost rode fire; Pengsheng's shade rose from water.

sentences.zh: 是故生者能出亦能入，死者能顯亦能幽，此物之精氣，化之遊魂，人鬼相感，數使之然也。

translations.literal: Therefore the living can go out and also enter; the dead can show and also hide — this is the essential breath of things, wandering souls of transformation; men and ghosts mutually stir — numbers make it so."
translations.idiomatic: Living souls pass in and out; dead souls show and hide — breath and wandering shades answer one another by number."

sentences.zh: 」苞曰：「目見陰陽之理，不過於君，君何以不隱？

translations.literal: Bao said: "I have seen yin-yang principle no deeper than yours — why then do you not hide yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao asked why, if he knew such lore, he did not vanish.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「夫陵虛之鳥，愛其清高，不原江、漢之魚；

translations.literal: Lu said: "The bird that vaults the void loves its lofty purity and does not envy the fish of the Yangzi and Han."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "The high bird loves the sky, not the river fish."

sentences.zh: 淵沼之魚，樂其濡濕，不易騰風之鳥：由性異而分不同也。

translations.literal: Fish in the deep pool delight in their damp and will not trade places with the wind-riding bird — natures differ and allotments part."
translations.idiomatic: Deep fish love the mud and will not swap with storm birds — each nature keeps its place."

sentences.zh: 僕自欲正身以明道，直己以親義，見數不以為異，知術不以為奇，夙夜研幾，孳孳溫故，而素隱行怪，未暇斯務也。」〉

translations.literal: I myself wish to straighten the body to clarify the Way, align the self to draw near righteousness; seeing numbers I do not marvel, knowing arts I do not call them strange; I study the subtle morning and night, tirelessly warming the old — as for seeking the hidden and doing the bizarre, I have not leisure for that labor."〉
translations.idiomatic: I mean to stand straight, clarify the Way, and study nightly — I leave occult tricks to others."〉

sentences.zh: 平原太守劉邠取印囊及山雞毛著器中，使筮。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Liu Bin of Pingyuan took a seal-sachet and pheasant tail-feathers, placed them in a vessel, and had him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin hid a seal pouch and hill-pheasant plumes for guessing.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「內方外圓，五色成文，含寶守信，出則有章，此印囊也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Square inside, round outside, five colors forming pattern, holding treasure and keeping faith — when it comes forth it has insignia — this is the seal-sachet.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Square within, round without, five colors — the seal satchel."

sentences.zh: 高岳岩岩，有鳥硃身，羽翼玄黃，鳴不失晨，此山雞毛也。

translations.literal: Lofty peak sheer crag, a bird vermilion-bodied, wings black and yellow, cries without missing dawn — this is hill-pheasant tail-feather."
translations.idiomatic: A red bird on a cliff, black and yellow wings, crowing at dawn — the pheasant plume."

sentences.zh: 」邠曰：「此郡官舍，連有變怪，使人恐怖，其理何由？

translations.literal: Bin said: "In this commandery office there have been successive uncanny events that terrify people — what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin asked why the yamen was haunted.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「或因漢末之亂，兵馬擾攘，軍屍流血，汙染丘山，故因昬夕，多有怪形也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Perhaps because at the end of Han, troops and horses rioted, army corpses bled and stained the hills — therefore in dusk and night many strange shapes appear."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu blamed the civil war — blood on the hills breeds phantoms after dark.

sentences.zh: 明府道德高妙，自天祐之，原安百祿，以光休寵。」

translations.literal: My enlightened lord's virtue and dao are lofty; Heaven itself guards you — I pray you secure a hundred blessings to brighten favor's radiance.""
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue is high — Heaven will bless you; may the hundred blessings settle on you."

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：故郡將劉邠字令元，清和有思理，好易而不能精。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Former commandery general Liu Bin, styled Lingyuan, was clear and harmonious with reflective judgment, loved the Yi but could not master it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Liu Bin loved the Yi yet never mastered it.〉

sentences.zh: 與輅相見，意甚喜歡，自說注易向訖也。

translations.literal: Meeting Lu, his mind was greatly pleased; he said his commentary on the Yi was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced to meet Guan Lu and boasted his Yi commentary was done.

sentences.zh: 輅言：「今明府欲勞不世之神，經緯大道，誠富美之秋。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Now the enlightened magistrate wishes to toil an unworldly spirit and weave the great Dao — truly this is the autumn of rich beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "You mean to tax a rare mind on the great Way — a splendid season for it."

sentences.zh: 然輅以為註易之急，急於水火；

translations.literal: Yet Lu thinks the urgency of annotating the Yi is keener than fire and water;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hold that glossing the Book of Changes is more urgent than fire or flood;

sentences.zh: 水火之難，登時之驗，易之清濁，延於萬代，不可不先定其神而後垂明思也。

translations.literal: fire and water's calamity has verification on the spot; the Yi's clarity and turbidity extend myriad generations — one cannot fail first to settle its spirit and then let clear thought descend."
translations.idiomatic: fire and flood prove themselves at once, while the Yi's light and shadow reach ages unborn — fix its spirit before you comment."

sentences.zh: 自旦至今，聽採聖論，未有易之一分，易安可注也！

translations.literal: From dawn until now I have listened and gathered sage discourse — not yet one fraction of the Yi — how can the Yi be annotated!"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard you all morning and still lack one scrap of the Yi — how can anyone annotate it?"

sentences.zh: 輅不解古之聖人，何以處乾位於西北，坤位於西南。

translations.literal: Lu does not understand how the ancient sages could place Qian in the northwest and Kun in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: I still do not see why the sages set Qian in the northwest and Kun in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 夫乾坤者天地之象，然天地至大，為神明君父，覆載萬物，生長無首，何以安處二位與六卦同列？

translations.literal: Qian and Kun are images of Heaven and Earth; yet Heaven and Earth are greatest, lord and father to the spirits, covering and carrying the myriad things, growing without first origin — how can they be settled in two positions listed with the six other trigrams?"
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven and Earth are the parents of all forms, why rank them like the other six lines?"

sentences.zh: 乾之象彖曰：『大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。

translations.literal: The image commentary on Qian says: 'Great indeed is Qian's origin; the myriad things rely on it for their start; thus it rules Heaven.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Qian tuan says the origin of Qian begins the myriad things and rules the sky."

sentences.zh: 』夫統者，屬也，尊莫大焉，何由有別位也？

translations.literal: 'Rule' means 'belong' — none is greater in honor — how then can there be a separate position?"
translations.idiomatic: To rule is to embrace — nothing ranks higher — so why a separate seat on the wheel?"

sentences.zh: 」邠依易係詞，諸為之理以為註，不得其要。

translations.literal: Bin relied on the Yi's appended texts and various principles to make his commentary — he did not obtain the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin patched glosses from the wings but missed the marrow.

sentences.zh: 輅尋聲下難，事皆窮析。

translations.literal: Lu followed the voice and posed difficulties; every matter was exhausted in analysis.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu pressed each point until the argument broke.

sentences.zh: 曰：「夫乾坤者，易之祖宗，變化之根源，今明府論清濁者有疑，疑則無神，恐非注易之符也。

translations.literal: He said: "Qian and Kun are the ancestors of the Yi, the root of change — now the enlightened lord's discourse on clarity and turbidity harbors doubt; where there is doubt there is no spirit — I fear that is no tally for annotating the Yi."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Without faith in Qian and Kun you cannot touch the spirit of the classic."

sentences.zh: 」輅於此為論八卦之道及爻象之精，大論開廓，眾化相連。

translations.literal: Here Lu discoursed on the way of the eight trigrams and the subtlety of lines and images; the great thesis opened wide and the myriad transformations linked in chain.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu then spun the eight trigrams and line images in one sweeping lecture.

sentences.zh: 邠所解者，皆以為妙，所不解者，皆以為神。

translations.literal: What Bin could explain he all deemed marvelous; what he could not explain he all deemed divine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin called what he grasped "marvel" and what he could not "divine."

sentences.zh: 自說：「欲注易八年，用思勤苦，歷載靡寧，定相得至論，此才不及易，不愛久勞，喜承雅言，如此相為高枕偃息矣。

translations.literal: He himself said: "I wished to annotate the Yi for eight years, using thought diligently and bitterly, year after year without peace; only now have I gained a supreme thesis — this talent does not match the Yi — I do not love endless toil — I am glad to receive elegant words — thus we may rest on high pillows and sleep at ease.""
translations.idiomatic: He confessed eight years' draft was nothing beside the Yi — he would rather sleep on Guan Lu's words."

sentences.zh: 」欲從輅學射覆，輅言：「今明府以虛神於注易，亦宜絕思於靈蓍。

translations.literal: He wished to follow Lu in learning shoot-the-covered; Lu said: "Now that the enlightened lord spends empty spirit on annotating the Yi, you ought also to cut off thought on numinous milfoil."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to learn guessing games; Guan Lu said, "If you pour spirit into the Yi, leave the stalks alone."

sentences.zh: 靈蓍者，二儀之明數，陰陽之幽契，施之於道則定天下吉凶，用之於術則收天下豪纖。

translations.literal: Numinous milfoil are the bright numbers of the two modes, the secret tally of yin and yang — applied to the Way they settle good and ill under Heaven; applied to art they gather the finest hairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The milfoil is heaven's abacus — for the Way it judges fate, for craft it catches the smallest clue.

sentences.zh: 纖微，未可以為易也。

translations.literal: Fine hairs — not yet can these serve as the Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Such trifles are not yet the Yi itself."

sentences.zh: 」邠曰：「以為術者易之近數，欲求其端耳。

translations.literal: Bin said: "I thought arts were the Yi's nearby numbers — I only wished to seek their tip."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin said he only wanted the knack behind the numbers.

sentences.zh: 若如來論，何事於斯？

translations.literal: If it is as your discourse, what business is there here?"
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, why bother with parlor tricks?"

sentences.zh: 」留輅五日，不遑卹官，但共清譚。

translations.literal: He detained Lu five days, having no leisure to pity official duties, but only pure talk together.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Guan Lu five days for pure philosophy, ignoring his yamen.

sentences.zh: 邠自言：「數與何平叔論易及老、莊之道，至於精神遐流，與化周旋，清若金水，鬱若山林，非君侶也。

translations.literal: Bin himself said: "Several times I debated the Yi and the ways of Laozi and Zhuangzi with He Pingshu — reaching where spirit flows far and mingles with transformation, clear as gold and water, dense as mountain forest — you are not his peer.""
translations.idiomatic: He boasted his talks with He Yan were lucid as metal and deep as forests — not Guan Lu's match."

sentences.zh: 」邠又曰：「此郡官舍，連有變怪，變怪多形，使人怖恐，君似當達此數者，其理何由也。

translations.literal: Bin also said: "In this commandery office there have been successive strange changes; the changes take many forms and make people terrified — you seem as if you ought to understand these numbers — what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again why the yamen was haunted if Guan Lu knew fate.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「此郡所以名平原者，本有原，山無木石，與地自然；

translations.literal: Lu said: "The reason this commandery is called Pingyuan is that originally there were plains — hills without wood or stone, natural to the earth;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Pingyuan means flat ground — naked earth without rock or tree;

sentences.zh: 含陰不能吐雲，含陽不能激風，陰陽雖弱，猶有微神；

translations.literal: containing yin it cannot spit clouds; containing yang it cannot whip wind; though yin and yang are weak, still there are slight spirits;
translations.idiomatic: the yin there cannot lift clouds nor the yang raise gales — only faint spirits linger;

sentences.zh: 微神不真，多聚凶姦，以類相求，魍魎成群。

translations.literal: slight spirits not true, many gather vicious portents; like seeks like and wangliang swarm in packs."
translations.idiomatic: weak ghosts draw wicked omens and sprites flock by kind."

sentences.zh: 或因漢末兵馬擾攘，軍屍流血，汙染丘岳，強魂相感，變化無常，故因昏夕之時，多有怪形也。

translations.literal: Or because at the end of Han troops and horses rioted, army corpses bled and stained hill ridges — strong souls mutually stirred, transformations without constant rule — therefore at dusk and night many strange shapes appear."
translations.idiomatic: Or the war dead stained the hills — angry shades stir at twilight."

sentences.zh: 昔夏禹文明，不怪於黃龍，周武信時，不惑於暴風，今明府道德高妙，神不懼妖，自天祐之，吉無不利，原安百祿以光休寵也。

translations.literal: In old days Yu of Xia was cultured and bright and marveled not at the yellow dragon; King Wu of Zhou trusted the seasons and was not deluded by sudden gales — now the enlightened lord's virtue and dao are lofty; spirits do not fear bogies — Heaven itself guards you — auspice without ill — I pray you secure a hundred blessings to brighten favor's radiance."
translations.idiomatic: He cited sage kings who ignored omens — your virtue will daunt ghosts and win Heaven's favor."

sentences.zh: 」邠曰：「聽雅論為近其理，每有變怪，輒聞鼓角聲音，或見弓劍形象。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Listening to your elegant thesis draws near the principle; yet whenever there are strange changes I then hear drum and horn sounds, or see shapes of bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin said the theory rang true, yet he still heard arms in the night.

sentences.zh: 夫以土山之精，伯有之魂，實能合會，干犯明靈也。

translations.literal: By the essence of earthen hills and the soul of Boyou they can indeed join and offend bright spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Earth spirits and Boyou's ghost can mingle to trouble the living."

sentences.zh: 」邠問輅：「易言剛健篤實，輝光日新，斯為同不？

translations.literal: Bin asked Lu: "The Yi speaks of firm, healthy, sincere, solid — 'radiance renewed daily' — is this sameness or not?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether "radiance" and "daily new" meant the same.

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「不同之名，朝旦為輝，日中為光。

translations.literal: Lu said: "They are different names — dawn is 'radiance,' noon is 'light.'"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said dawn glow differs from noon blaze.

sentences.zh: 」晉諸公贊曰：邠本名炎，犯晉太子諱，改為邠。

translations.literal: The Jin Zhugong zan says: Bin's original name was Yan; he changed it to Bin to avoid the Jin crown prince's taboo."
translations.idiomatic: Pei notes Liu Yan renamed Liu Bin for Jin taboo."

sentences.zh: 位至太子僕。

translations.literal: He rose to crown prince's steward."
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of crown prince's steward."

sentences.zh: 子粹，字純嘏，侍中。

translations.literal: His son Cui, styled Chungu, was palace attendant."
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Cui became palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 次宏，字終嘏，太常。

translations.literal: Next Hong, styled Zhonggu, was grand master of ceremonies."
translations.idiomatic: Next Liu Hong was minister of rites."

sentences.zh: 次漢，字仲嘏，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Next Han, styled Zhonggu, was supernumerary grandee."
translations.idiomatic: Next Liu Han was a supernumerary grandee."

sentences.zh: 漢清衝有貴識，名亞樂廣。

translations.literal: Han was clear and aloof with noble judgment; his fame stood second to Yue Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Han's reputation rivaled Yue Guang's."

sentences.zh: 宏子咸，徐州刺吏。

translations.literal: Hong's son Xian was inspector of Xu province."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian governed Xu as inspector."

sentences.zh: 次耽，晉陵內史。

translations.literal: Next Dan was interior minister of Jinling."
translations.idiomatic: Next Liu Dan governed Jinling."

sentences.zh: 耽子恢，字真長，尹丹楊，為中興名士也。〉

translations.literal: Dan's son Kai, styled Zhenchang, was governor of Danyang — a famed gentleman of the restoration."〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai of Danyang was a leading voice of the Eastern Jin revival."〉

sentences.zh: 清河令徐季龍使人行獵，令輅筮其所得。

translations.literal: Magistrate Xu Jilong of Qinghe sent men hunting and ordered Lu to divine what they would catch.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jilong of Qinghe sent hunters and asked Guan Lu what they would bag.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「當獲小獸，复非食禽，雖有爪牙，微而不強，雖有文章，蔚而不明，非虎非雉，其名曰狸。

translations.literal: Lu said: "You will catch a small beast, again not a game bird for eating; though it has claws and teeth, they are slight and not strong; though it has pattern, it is luxuriant but not bright — neither tiger nor pheasant — its name is raccoon-dog."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said they would take a small cat-beast — a civet, not fowl.

sentences.zh: 」獵人暮歸，果如輅言。

translations.literal: The hunters returned at dusk — indeed as Lu said.
translations.idiomatic: They came back at dusk exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 季龍取十三種物，著大篋中，使輅射。

translations.literal: Jilong took thirteen kinds of things, placed them in a large basket, and had Lu shoot the covered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu hid thirteen objects in a hamper for guessing.

sentences.zh: 云：「器中藉藉有十三種物。

translations.literal: He said: "Inside the vessel there rustle thirteen kinds of things."
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the basket held thirteen items.

sentences.zh: 」先說雞子，後道蠶蛹，遂一一名之，惟以梳為枇耳。

translations.literal: Lu first named the chicken egg, then the silkworm chrysalis, then named each one in order — only he called the comb a wooden comb for grain."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu listed them in order, mistaking the comb for a grain rake."

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：清河令徐季龍，字開明，有才機。

translations.literal: Separate biography: Xu Jilong, magistrate of Qinghe, styled Kaiming, had clever talent.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Jilong, styled Kaiming, was a clever magistrate.〉

sentences.zh: 與輅相見，共論龍動則景雲起，虎嘯則谷風至，以為火星者龍，參星者虎，火出則雲應，參出則風到，此乃陰陽之感化，非龍虎之所致也。

translations.literal: Meeting Lu, together they debated that when the dragon moves then auspicious clouds rise, when the tiger roars then valley wind arrives — they thought the Mars star was the dragon and the Shen star was the tiger; when fire appears clouds respond, when Shen rises wind comes — this is yin-yang's mutual resonance, not caused by dragon and tiger themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They argued stars, not beasts, drove wind and cloud.

sentences.zh: 輅言：「夫論難當先審其本，然後求其理，理失則機謬，機謬則榮辱之主。

translations.literal: Lu said: "In debate one must first examine the root, then seek its principle; when principle fails the pivot is wrong; when the pivot is wrong, lord of glory and shame is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "Miss the root and the whole machine slips."

sentences.zh: 若以參星為虎，則谷風更為寒霜之風，寒霜之風非東風之名。

translations.literal: If you take Shen star as tiger, then valley wind becomes the wind of cold frost — cold-frost wind is not the name of east wind."
translations.idiomatic: If Shen is tiger, "valley wind" would mean frost wind, not east wind."

sentences.zh: 是以龍者陽精，以潛為陰，幽靈上通，和氣感神，二物相扶，故能興云。

translations.literal: Therefore the dragon is yang essence; by hiding it is yin; its dark spirit ascends and connects, harmonizing qi moves spirit — the two things support each other, therefore they can raise clouds."
translations.idiomatic: The dragon is yang in yin hiding — that pairing lifts clouds."

sentences.zh: 夫虎者，陰精而居於陽，依木長嘯，動於巽林，二氣相感，故能運風。

translations.literal: As for the tiger — it is yin essence dwelling in yang; leaning on the forest it long howls, moving in the Xun grove — the two qi mutually stir, therefore it can drive wind."
translations.idiomatic: The tiger is yin in yang — its roar in the wood stirs the gale."

sentences.zh: 若磁石之取鐵，不見其神而金自來，有徵應以相感也。

translations.literal: It is like lodestone drawing iron — you do not see its spirit yet metal comes of itself — there is responsive proof in mutual stirring."
translations.idiomatic: Like a lodestone drawing iron — response without visible strings."

sentences.zh: 況龍有潛飛之化，虎有文明之變，招雲召風，何足為疑？

translations.literal: How much more when the dragon has transformation of lurking and flight and the tiger has transformation of patterned brilliance — summoning cloud and calling wind, what room for doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Dragons rise and fall; tigers blaze with stripes — why doubt their weather?"

sentences.zh: 」季龍言：「夫龍之在淵，不過一井之底，虎之悲嘯，不過百步之中，形氣淺弱，所通者近，何能𣿖景雲而馳東風？

translations.literal: Jilong said: "When the dragon lies in the abyss it is no more than the bottom of one well; when the tiger sadly roars it is not beyond a hundred paces — form and qi are shallow and weak, what they reach is near — how can they roll up bright clouds and gallop east wind?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said beasts in wells cannot summon tempests.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「君不見陰陽燧在掌握之中，形不出手，乃上引太陽之火，下引太陰之水，噓吸之間，煙景以集。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Have you not seen the yin-yang fire-mirror held in the palm — form does not leave the hand, yet upward it draws the great sun's fire, downward the great moon's water; between a breath in and out, mist and radiance gather."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu cited the burning-mirror that draws sunfire and moon dew in the hand.

sentences.zh: 苟精氣相感，縣象應乎二燧；

translations.literal: If essential qi mutually stirs, hanging images answer to the two mirrors;
translations.idiomatic: When essences answer, the paired mirrors prove it;

sentences.zh: 苟不相感，則二女同居，志不相得。

translations.literal: if they do not mutually stir, then two maidens dwell together yet their wills do not agree."
translations.idiomatic: when they fail, two wives under one roof still quarrel."

sentences.zh: 自然之道，無有遠近。

translations.literal: The natural Way knows no far or near."
translations.idiomatic: Nature's law ignores distance."

sentences.zh: 」季龍言：「世有軍事，則感雞雉先鳴，其道何由？

translations.literal: Jilong said: "When there is military affair in the world, then fowl and pheasants crow first — what is the principle?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked why cocks crow before war.

sentences.zh: 復有他佔，惟在雞雉而巳？

translations.literal: Are there other divinations, or only in fowl and pheasant?"
translations.idiomatic: Are birds the only omens?

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「貴人有事，其應在天，在天則日月星辰也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "When nobles have affairs, their response is in Heaven; in Heaven it is sun, moon, and stars."
translations.idiomatic: Great men's signs hang in the sky — sun, moon, stars.

sentences.zh: 兵動民憂，其應在物，在物則山林鳥獸也。

translations.literal: When troops move and the people grieve, the response is among things; among things it is mountains, forests, birds, and beasts."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers stir the folk — omens then walk the woods and fields."

sentences.zh: 夫雞者兌之畜，金者兵之精，雉者離之鳥，獸者武之神，故太白揚輝則雞鳴，熒惑流行則雉驚，各感數而動。

translations.literal: The fowl is the creature of Dui, metal is the essence of arms; the pheasant is the bird of Li, beasts are the spirit of war — therefore when the Great White star flares fowls crow, when the Sparkling Deluder courses pheasants startle — each moves according to its number."
translations.idiomatic: Cocks belong to Dui-metal, pheasants to Li-fire — stars prod them each.

sentences.zh: 又兵之神道，佈在六甲，六甲推移，其占無常。

translations.literal: Moreover the spirit-path of arms is spread through the six jia; the six jia shift and push — their divination has no constant."
translations.idiomatic: War's math rides the six jia — shifting signs, not fixed birds."

sentences.zh: 是以晉柩牛呴，果有西軍，鴻嘉石鼓，鳴則有兵，不專近在於雞雉也。

translations.literal: Therefore when Jin's bier-ox lowed, indeed there was an army from the west; when Hongjia's stone drum sounded there were troops — it is not confined to being near in fowl and pheasant alone."
translations.idiomatic: He cited oxen and stone drums crying war — not only chickens."

sentences.zh: 」季龍言：「魯昭公八年，有石言於晉，師曠以為作事不時，怨讟動於民，則有非言之物而言，於理為合不？

translations.literal: Jilong said: "In Duke Zhao's eighth year a stone spoke in Jin; Shi Kuang thought that when work is untimely and resentful slander stirs among the people, then there are things without speech that speak — does this fit principle or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked about the talking stone of Jin.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「晉平奢泰，崇飾宮室，斬伐林木，殘破金石，民力既盡，怨及山澤，神痛人感，二精並作，金石同氣，則兌為口舌，口舌之妖，動於靈石。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Lord Ping of Jin was extravagant, lavishly ornamenting palaces, cutting forests and smashing metal and stone — the people's strength was exhausted; resentment reached hills and marshes; spirits ached and men felt it — the two essences arose together; metal and stone share one qi — then Dui becomes mouth and tongue — the bale of mouth and tongue moved in a numinous stone."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu blamed Jin's waste — angry qi made the stone "speak."

sentences.zh: 傳曰輕百姓，飾城郭，則金不從革，此之謂也。

translations.literal: The tradition says: when the hundred surnames are slighted and walls are dressed up, then metal will not obey reform — this is what it means."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the omen: mistreat the people and metal rebels.

sentences.zh: 」季龍欽嘉，留輅經數日。

translations.literal: Jilong admired and praised him, detaining Lu several days.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jilong kept him several days in admiration.

sentences.zh: 輅佔獵既驗，季龍曰：「君雖神妙，但不多藏物耳，何能皆得之？

translations.literal: Lu's hunting divination having verified, Jilong said: "Though you are spirit-like and subtle, you do not hide many things — how can you get them all?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu teased that Guan Lu could not hide thirteen secrets.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「吾與天地參神，蓍龜通靈，抱日月而遊杳冥，極變化而覽未然，況茲近物，能蔽聰明？

translations.literal: Lu said: "I join spirit with Heaven and Earth; tortoise and milfoil penetrate the numinous; I embrace sun and moon and roam in deepest dark; I exhaust change and view what is not yet manifest — how much more these near things — could they block clear hearing?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu boasted he rode sun and moon through the unseen — trifles could not baffle him.

sentences.zh: 」季龍大笑，「君既不謙，又念窮在近矣。

translations.literal: Jilong greatly laughed: "You are not modest, and I think your limit draws near."
translations.idiomatic: Xu laughed that pride would undo him.

sentences.zh: 」輅言：「君尚未識謙言，焉能論道？

translations.literal: Lu said: "You have not yet recognized modest speech — how can you discuss the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said, "You mistake humility for pride."

sentences.zh: 夫天地者則乾坤之卦，蓍龜者則卜筮之數，日月者離坎之象，變化者陰陽之爻，杳冥者神化之源，未然者則幽冥之先，此皆周易之紀綱，何僕之不謙？

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth are then the hexagrams of Qian and Kun; tortoise and milfoil are then the numbers of divination; sun and moon are then the images of Li and Kan; change is then the lines of yin and yang; deepest dark is then the source of spirit-transformation; not-yet-manifest is then the vanguard of hidden gloom — these are all the cords of the Zhou Yi — in what is your servant not modest?"
translations.idiomatic: He listed the Yi as the grammar of heaven — hardly immodest.

sentences.zh: 」季龍於是取十三種物，欲以窮之，輅射之皆中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jilong took thirteen kinds of things, wishing to exhaust him; Lu shot them all and hit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu produced thirteen objects; Guan Lu named every one.

sentences.zh: 季龍乃歎曰：「作者之謂聖，述者之謂明，豈此之謂乎！」〉

translations.literal: Jilong then sighed: "The maker may be called sage; the transmitter may be called clear — is it not this!""〉
translations.idiomatic: He cried that Guan Lu was both maker and transmitter."〉

sentences.zh: 輅隨軍西行，過毌丘儉墓下，倚樹哀吟，精神不樂。

translations.literal: Lu followed the army west, passed by Guoqiu Jian's tomb, leaned on a tree and sadly chanted, his spirit unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Marching west he mourned at Guoqiu Jian's grave.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，輅曰：「林木雖茂，無形可久；

translations.literal: People asked the reason; Lu said: "Though the forest trees are lush, there is no form that endures long;
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said the grove would not last;

sentences.zh: 碑誄雖美，無後可守。

translations.literal: though the stele and dirge are beautiful, there is no posterity to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: fine inscriptions cannot save a doomed house.

sentences.zh: 玄武藏頭，蒼龍無足，白虎銜屍，硃雀悲哭，四危以備，法當滅族。

translations.literal: The Black Warrior hides its head, the Green Dragon lacks feet, the White Tiger holds a corpse, the Red Bird weeps — the four perils are complete — by rule the clan should be extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: He read the four spirit omens as a clan-wiping curse."

sentences.zh: 不過二載，其應至矣。

translations.literal: Within two years the response will arrive."
translations.idiomatic: The reckoning would come within two years."

sentences.zh: 」卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said."
translations.idiomatic: It happened as he foretold."

sentences.zh: 後得休，過清河倪太守。

translations.literal: Later, on obtaining leave, he passed Grand Administrator Ni of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: On leave he visited Prefect Ni of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，倪問輅雨期，輅曰：「今夕當雨。

translations.literal: The time was great drought; Ni asked Lu the date of rain; Lu said: "This very night there ought to be rain."
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he promised rain that night.

sentences.zh: 」是日暘燥，晝無形似，府丞及令在坐，咸謂不然。

translations.literal: That day was blazing dry; by day there was no sign; the assistant magistrate and magistrate sat present — all said it would not be so.
translations.idiomatic: The sun scorched; officials scoffed.

sentences.zh: 到鼓一中，星月皆沒，風雲並起，竟成快雨。

translations.literal: When the first drum struck, stars and moon all vanished; wind and cloud arose together and became a swift soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drum wind snuffed the stars and rain fell.

sentences.zh: 於是倪盛脩主人禮，共為歡樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ni lavishly performed host rites and shared joy together.
translations.idiomatic: Ni feasted him in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 〈輅別傳曰：輅與倪清河相見，既刻雨期，倪猶未信。

translations.literal: Separate biography: When Lu and Grand Administrator Ni of Qinghe met, after he had fixed the rain date Ni still did not believe."
translations.idiomatic: 〈The note says Ni doubted until the clouds rose.〉

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「夫造化之所以為神，不疾而速，不行而至。

translations.literal: Lu said: "What makes creation spirit-like is that without haste it is swift, without walking it arrives."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said nature needs neither hurry nor footsteps.

sentences.zh: 十六日壬子，直滿，畢星中已有水氣，水氣之發，動於卯辰，此必至之應也。

translations.literal: The sixteenth day is renzi, full moon; the Dipper already holds water-qi inside; the issuing of water-qi stirs between mao and chen — this is the sure response."
translations.idiomatic: He read renzi full moon and Dipper moisture for rain at mao-chen.

sentences.zh: 又天昨檄召五星，宣布星符，刺下東井，告命南箕，使召雷公、電母、風伯、雨師，群岳吐陰，眾川激精，雲漢垂澤，蛟龍含靈，堃堃硃電，吐咀杳冥，殷殷雷聲，噓吸雨靈，習習谷風，六合皆同，欬唾之間，品物流形。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven yesterday issued summons to the Five Planets, promulgated star tallies, pricked down the Eastern Well, proclaimed command to the Southern Sieve, ordered Thunder Duke, Lightning Mother, Wind Lord, and Rain Master; host hills spit yin, host rivers lash essence; the River of Stars hangs dew; dragons hold spirit; vermilion lightning chews deepest dark; rolling thunder inhales rain spirit; rustling valley wind — the six directions alike; between a cough and spit the myriad forms flow into shape."
translations.idiomatic: He painted heaven marshaling thunder, wind, and rain in one breath.

sentences.zh: 天有常期，道有自然，不足為難也。

translations.literal: Heaven has its constant term; the Way has what is natural — not enough to call difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven keeps its schedule — nothing marvelous in that."

sentences.zh: 」倪曰：「譚高信寡，相為憂之。

translations.literal: Ni said: "Lofty talk wins few believers — I worry for you."
translations.idiomatic: Ni said, "Lofty talk convinces few listeners," and he worried for him.

sentences.zh: 」於是便留輅，往請府丞及清河令。

translations.literal: Thereupon he detained Lu and went to invite the assistant magistrate and the magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Guan Lu and summoned the county staff.

sentences.zh: 若夜雨者當為啖二百斤犢肉，若不雨當住十日。

translations.literal: If it rains at night I shall treat you to two hundred jin of veal; if it does not rain, you stay ten days."
translations.idiomatic: He wagered veal against a ten-day stay.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「言念費損！

translations.literal: Lu said: "I think of the expense wasted!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu replied that the wager would waste a fortune in beef.

sentences.zh: 」至日向暮，了無雲氣，眾人並嗤輅。

translations.literal: By sunset toward evening there was no trace of cloud; the crowd together sneered at Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the sky stayed clear and the crowd mocked him.

sentences.zh: 輅言：「樹上已有少女微風，樹間又有陰鳥和鳴。

translations.literal: Lu said: "On the trees there is already a slight girl-wind; among the trees yin birds harmonize in cry.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu said he heard the maiden breeze and yin birds tuning up.

sentences.zh: 又少男風起，眾鳥和翔，其應至矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the young-boy wind rises; flocking birds harmonize in flight — the response will arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Then the young-boy wind rose and birds flew in chorus — the rain was due."

sentences.zh: 」須臾，果有艮風鳴鳥。
日未入，東南有山雲樓起。
黃昏之後，雷聲動天。
到鼓一中，星月皆沒，風雲並興，玄氣四合，大雨河傾。
倪調輅言：「誤中耳，不為神也。
」輅曰：「誤中與天期，不亦工乎！」〉
正元二年，弟辰謂輅曰：「大​​將軍待君意厚，冀當富貴乎？
」輅長歎曰：「吾自知有分直耳，然天與我才明，不與我年壽，恐四十七八間，不見女嫁兒娶婦也。
若得免此，欲作洛陽令，可使路不拾遣，枹鼓不鳴。
但恐至太山治鬼，不得治生人，如何！
」辰問其故，輅曰：「吾額上無生骨，眼中無守精，鼻無梁柱，腳無天根，背無三甲，腹無三壬，此皆不壽之驗。
又吾本命在寅，加月食夜生。
天有常數，不可得諱，但人不知耳。
吾前後相當死者過百人，略無錯也。
」是歲八月，為少府丞。
明年二月卒，年四十八。
〈輅別傳曰：既有明才，遭硃陽之運，於時名勢赫奕，若火猛風疾。
當塗之士，莫不枝附葉連。
賓客如雲，無多少皆為設食。
賓無貴賤，候之以禮。
京城紛紛，非徒歸其名勢而已，然亦懷其德焉。
向不夭命，輅之榮華，非世所測也。
弟辰嘗欲從輅學卜及仰觀事，輅言：「卿不可教耳。
夫卜非至精不能見其數，非至妙不能睹其道，孝經、詩、論，足為三公，無用知之也。
」於是遂止。
子弟無能傳其術者。
辰敘曰：「夫晉、魏之士，見輅道術神妙，佔候無錯，以為有隱書及象甲之數。
辰每觀輅書傳，惟有易林、風角及鳥鳴、仰觀星書三十餘卷，世所共有。
然輅獨在少府官舍，無家人子弟隨之，其亡沒之際，好奇不哀喪者，盜輅書，惟餘易林、風角及鳥鳴書還耳。
夫術數有百數十家，其書有數千卷，書不少也。
然而世鮮名人，皆由無才，不由無書也。
裴冀州、何、鄧二尚書及鄉里劉太常、潁川兄弟，以輅禀受天才，明陰陽之道，吉凶之情，一得其源，遂涉其流，亦不為難，常歸服之。
輅自言與此五君共語使人精神清發，昏不暇寐。
自此以下，殆白日欲寢矣。
又自言當世無所原，欲得與魯梓慎、鄭裨灶、晉卜偃、宋子韋、楚甘公、魏石申共登靈臺，披神圖，步三光，明災異，運蓍龜，決狐疑，無所复恨也。
辰不以闇淺，得因孔懷之親，數與輅有所諮論至於辨人物，析臧否，說近義，彈曲直，拙而不工也。
若敷皇、羲之典，揚文、孔之辭，周流五曜，經緯三度，口滿聲溢，微言風集，若仰眺飛鴻，漂漂兮景沒，若俯臨深溪，杳杳兮精絕；
偪以攻難，而失其端，欲受學求道，尋以迷昏，無不扼腕椎指，追響長嘆也。
昔京房雖善卜及風律之佔，卒不免禍，而輅自知四十八當亡，可謂明哲相殊。
又京房目見遘讒之黨，耳聽青蠅之聲，面諫不從，而猶道路紛紜。
輅處魏、晉之際，藏智以樸，卷舒有時，妙不見求，愚不見遺，可謂知幾相邈也。
京房上不量萬乘之主，下不避佞諂之徒，欲以天文、洪範，利國利身，困不能用，卒陷大刑，可謂枯龜之餘智，膏燭之末景，豈不哀哉！
世人多以輅疇之京房，辰不敢許也。
至於仰察星辰，俯定吉凶，遠期不失年歲，近期不失日月，辰以甘、石之妙不先也。
射覆名物，見術流速，東方朔不過也。
觀骨形而審貴賤，覽形色而知生死，許負、唐舉不超也。
若夫疏風氣而探微候，聽鳥鳴而識神機，亦一代之奇也。
向使輅官達，為宰相大臣，膏腴流於明世，華曜列乎竹帛，使幽驗皆舉，秘言不遺，千載之後，有道者必信而貴之，無道者必疑而怪之；
信者以妙過真，夫妙與神合者，得神無所惑也。
恨輅才長命短，道貴時賤，親賢遐潛，不宣於良史，而為鄙弟所見追述，既自闇濁，又從來久遠，所載卜佔事，雖不識本卦，捃拾殘餘，十得二焉。
至於仰觀靈曜，說魏、晉興衰，及五運浮沉，兵革災異，十不收一。
無源何以成河？
無根何以垂榮？
雖秋菊可採，不及春英，臨文慷慨，伏用哀慚。
將來君子，幸以高明求其義焉。
往孟荊州為列人典農，嘗問亡兄，昔東方朔射覆得何卦，正知守宮、蜥蜴二物者。
亡兄於此為安卦生象，辭喻交錯，微義豪起，變化相推，會於辰巳，分別龍蛇，各使有理。
言絕之後，孟荊州長嘆息曰：『吾聞君論，精神騰躍，殆欲飛散，何其汪汪乃至於斯邪！
'」臣松之案：辰所稱鄉里劉太常者，謂劉寔也。
辰撰輅傳，寔時為太常，潁川則寔弟智也。
寔、智並以儒學為名，無能言之。
世語稱寔博辯，猶不足以並裴、何之流也。
又案輅自說，云「本命在寅」，則建安十五年生也。
至正始九年，應三十九，而傳云三十六，以正元三年卒，應四十七，傳云四十八，皆為不相應也。
近有閻續伯者，名纘，該微通物，有良史風。
為天下補綴遺脫，敢以所聞列於篇左。
皆從受之於大人先哲，足以取信者，冀免虛誣之譏云爾。
嘗受辰傳所謂劉太常者曰：「輅始見聞，由於為鄰婦卜亡牛，云當在西面窮牆中，縣頭上向。
教婦人令視諸丘塚中，果得牛。
婦人因以為藏己牛，告官案驗，乃知以術知，故裴冀州遂聞焉。
」又云：「路中小人失妻者，輅為卜，教使明旦於東陽城門中伺擔豚人牽與共鬥。
具如其言，豚逸走，即共追之。
豚入人舍，突破主人甕，婦從甕中出。
」劉侯云甚多此類，辰所載才十一二耳。
劉侯云：「辰，孝廉才也。
」中書令史紀玄龍，輅鄉里人，云「輅在田舍，嘗候遠鄰，主人患數失火。
輅卜，教使明日於南陌上伺，當有一角巾諸生，駕黑牛故車，必引留，為設賓主，此能消之。
即從輅戒。
諸生有急求去，不聽，遂留當宿，意大不安，以為圖己。
主人罷入，生乃把刀出門，倚兩薪積間，側立假寐。
歘有一小物直來過前，如獸，手中持火，以口吹之。
生驚，舉刀斫，正斷要，視之則狐。
自此主人不復有災。
」前長廣太守陳承祐口受城門校尉華長駿語云：「昔其父為清河太守時，召輅作吏，駿與少小，後以鄉里，遂加恩意，常與同載周旋，具知其事。
云諸要驗，三倍於傳。
辰既短才，又年縣小，又多在田舍，故益不詳。
辰仕宦至州主簿、部從事，太康之初物故。
」駿又云：「輅卜亦不悉中，十得七八，駿問其故，輅云：『理無差錯來卜者或言不足以宣事實，故使爾。
』華城門夫人者，魏故司空涿郡盧公女也，得疾，連年不差。
華家時居西城下南纏里中，三厩在其東南。
輅卜當有師從東方來，自言能治，便聽使之，必得其力。
後無何，有南征厩騶，當充甲卒，來詣盧公，佔能治女郎。
公即表請留之，專使其子將詣華氏療疾，初用散藥，後復用丸治，尋有效，即奏除騶名，以補太醫。
」又云：「隨輅父在利漕時，有治下屯民捕鹿者，其晨行還，見毛血，人取鹿處來詣厩告輅，輅為卦語云：'此有盜者，是汝東巷中第三家也。
汝徑往門前，伺無人時，取一瓦子，密發其碓屋東頭第七椽，以瓦著下，不過明日食時，自送還汝。
』其夜，盜者父病頭痛，壯熱煩疼，然亦來詣輅卜。
輅為發祟，盜者俱服。
輅令擔皮肉藏還者故處，病當自愈。
乃密教鹿主往取。
又語使復往如前，舉椽棄瓦盜父病差。
又都尉治內史有失物者，輅使明晨於寺門外看，當逢一人，使指天畫地，舉手四向，自當得之。
暮果獲於故處矣。」〉
